2.4.s:
2.16
.. puṣkara uvāca .. ..
dhanurdravyatrayaṃ lohaṃ śṛṅgaṃ cāru ca bhārgava ..
jyādravyatritayaṃ carma vaṃśabhaṃgaṃ tvacastathā .. 1 ..
2.4.d:
2.16
॥ पुष्कर उवाच ॥ ॥
धनुर्द्रव्यत्रयं लोहं शृङ्गं चारु च भार्गव ॥
ज्याद्रव्यत्रितयं चर्म वंशभंगं त्वचस्तथा ॥ 1 ॥
2.4.m: Puṣkara said: / The threefold material for a bow is metal, horn, and wood, O descendant of Bhṛgu. / The threefold material for a bowstring is hide, split bamboo, and bark.

2.4.s:
vaṃśatvagvaṃśacāpaṃ tu kartavyaṃ bhṛgunandana ..
anyeṣu rāma cāpeṣu śeṣadravyamidaṃ bhaveta .. 2 ..
2.4.d:
वंशत्वग्वंशचापं तु कर्तव्यं भृगुनन्दन ॥
अन्येषु राम चापेषु शेषद्रव्यमिदं भवेत ॥ 2 ॥
2.4.m: A bow of bamboo should be made from bamboo bark, O son of Bhṛgu; / for other bows, O Rāma, these remaining materials are used.

2.4.s:
pramāṇaṃ nātra nirdiṣṭaṃ cāpayoḥ śārṅgalohayoḥ ..
dārucāpapramāṇaṃ tu śreṣṭhaṃ hastacatuṣṭayam .. 3 ..
2.4.d:
प्रमाणं नात्र निर्दिष्टं चापयोः शार्ङ्गलोहयोः ॥
दारुचापप्रमाणं तु श्रेष्ठं हस्तचतुष्टयम् ॥ 3 ॥
2.4.m: No fixed measure is prescribed here for bows of horn and metal; / but for a wooden bow, the best measure is four cubits.

2.4.s:
tadardhasamahīne tu prokte madhyakanīyasī ..
muṣṭigrāhyāṇi vṛttāni madhye sarvāṇi kārayet .. 4 ..
2.4.d:
तदर्धसमहीने तु प्रोक्ते मध्यकनीयसी ॥
मुष्टिग्राह्याणि वृत्तानि मध्ये सर्वाणि कारयेत् ॥ 4 ॥
2.4.m: Shorter by half that and by a quarter are declared the middling and shortest [bows]. / All should be made round at the center where grasped by the hand.

2.4.s:
svalpā koṭistu vārkṣāṇāṃ śārṅgalauhamayī dvija ..
kāminībhrūlatākārā koṭiḥ kāryā susaṃskṛtā ..5..
2.4.d:
स्वल्पा कोटिस्तु वार्क्षाणां शार्ङ्गलौहमयी द्विज ॥
कामिनीभ्रूलताकारा कोटिः कार्या सुसंस्कृता ॥5॥
2.4.m: The bow-tip of wooden bows is small, or it may be of horn or metal, O twice-born; / shaped like the creeper-like eyebrow of a lovely woman, the tip should be well finished.

2.4.s:
pṛthagvā dārumiśro vā lohaśārṅge tu kārayet ..
śārṅgaṃ snāyucitaṃ kāryaṃ rukmabinduvibhūṣitam .. 6 ..
2.4.d:
पृथग्वा दारुमिश्रो वा लोहशार्ङ्गे तु कारयेत् ॥
शार्ङ्गं स्नायुचितं कार्यं रुक्मबिन्दुविभूषितम् ॥ 6 ॥
2.4.m: One may make [the bow] of metal and horn separately or mixed with wood. / A horn bow should be wrapped with sinew and adorned with gold dots.

2.4.s:
kuṭilasphuṭitaṃ cāpaṃ sacchidraṃ ca na śasyate ..
hastibhagnā drumā ye ca vidyuddagdhāstathā ca ye .. 7 ..
2.4.d:
कुटिलस्फुटितं चापं सच्छिद्रं च न शस्यते ॥
हस्तिभग्ना द्रुमा ये च विद्युद्दग्धास्तथा च ये ॥ 7 ॥
2.4.m: A bow that is crooked, cracked, or full of holes is not praised. / Trees broken by elephants, or scorched by lightning,

2.4.s:
ārāmadevatāveśmatāpasāśramasaṃbhavāḥ ..
śmaśānasaṃbhavā ye ca na te kāryāḥ kathaṃcana .. 8 ..
2.4.d:
आरामदेवतावेश्मतापसाश्रमसंभवाः ॥
श्मशानसंभवा ये च न ते कार्याः कथंचन ॥ 8 ॥
2.4.m: growing in pleasure gardens, shrines of gods, or hermitages of ascetics, / or those growing in cremation grounds, must never be used.

2.4.s:
prāṇināṃ yaḥ sajātyena śṛṅgī yudhi nipātitaḥ ..
tacchṛṅgaṃ varjayeccāpaṃ nityaṃ śārṅge vicakṣaṇaḥ .. 9 ..
2.4.d:
प्राणिनां यः सजात्येन शृङ्गी युधि निपातितः ॥
तच्छृङ्गं वर्जयेच्चापं नित्यं शार्ङ्गे विचक्षणः ॥ 9 ॥
2.4.m: If a horned animal was struck down in combat by one of its own kind, / an expert should always avoid that horn for a horn bow.

2.4.s:
lohāni rāma catvāri śasyante cāpakarmaṇi ..
suvarṇaṃ rajataṃ tāmraṃ tathā kṛṣṇāyasaṃ dvija .. 10 ..
2.4.d:
लोहानि राम चत्वारि शस्यन्ते चापकर्मणि ॥
सुवर्णं रजतं ताम्रं तथा कृष्णायसं द्विज ॥ 10 ॥
2.4.m: Four metals, O Rāma, are praised in the making of bows: / gold, silver, copper, and black iron, O twice-born.

2.4.s:
kāñcanaṃ cāparatnaṃ tu saratnamapi kārayet ..
māhiṣaṃ śārabhaṃ śārṅgaṃ rauhījaṃ cāpi kārayet .. 11 ..
2.4.d:
काञ्चनं चापरत्नं तु सरत्नमपि कारयेत् ॥
माहिषं शारभं शार्ङ्गं रौहीजं चापि कारयेत् ॥ 11 ॥
2.4.m: One may also make an excellent golden bow set with jewels. / A horn bow may be made from the horn of a buffalo, a śarabha, or a rohi deer.

2.4.s:
vārkṣaṃ candanajaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ vaitasaṃ dhānvataṃ tathā ..
sālaśālmalikāśānāṃ kakubhasyāñjanasya ca .. 12 ..
2.4.d:
वार्क्षं चन्दनजं श्रेष्ठं वैतसं धान्वतं तथा ॥
सालशाल्मलिकाशानां ककुभस्याञ्जनस्य च ॥ 12 ॥
2.4.m: Among wooden bows, that made of sandalwood, cane, or dhānvana is best; / or of sāl, śālmali, kāśa, kakubha, and añjana,

2.4.s:
vaṃśasya ca mahābhāga sarvaśreṣṭhatamaṃ viduḥ ..
śaradgṛhītaiḥ kāṣṭhaistu cāpaṃ kāryaṃ prayatnataḥ .. 13 ..
2.4.d:
वंशस्य च महाभाग सर्वश्रेष्ठतमं विदुः ॥
शरद्गृहीतैः काष्ठैस्तु चापं कार्यं प्रयत्नतः ॥ 13 ॥
2.4.m: and of bamboo, O fortunate one, which is known as the best of all. / Bows should be carefully made from wood harvested in autumn.

2.4.s:
vaṃśānāmapi tacchreṣṭhaṃ yatra gaṅgā mahānadī ..
sālānāmapi tacchreṣṭhaṃ gomatī yatra bhārgava .. 14 ..
2.4.d:
वंशानामपि तच्छ्रेष्ठं यत्र गङ्गा महानदी ॥
सालानामपि तच्छ्रेष्ठं गोमती यत्र भार्गव ॥ 14 ॥
2.4.m: Even among bamboos, that is best which grows where the great river Gaṅgā is; / among sāl trees, that is best where the Gomatī is, O descendant of Bhṛgu.

2.4.s:
vitastākūlajaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ vetasīnāṃ tathaiva va ..
evaṃ dravyamayaṃ kāryaṃ cāpaṃ lakṣaṇasaṃyutam ..15..
2.4.d:
वितस्ताकूलजं श्रेष्ठं वेतसीनां तथैव व ॥
एवं द्रव्यमयं कार्यं चापं लक्षणसंयुतम् ॥15॥
2.4.m: Cane growing on the banks of the Vitastā is likewise best. / Thus made of [proper] material, a bow should possess the auspicious marks.

2.4.s:
grahaṇa lakṣaṇaṃ cāsya bhaviṣyati ca khaḍgavat ..
sukhagrāhaṃ dṛṣṭikāntaṃ śaramokṣamukhaṃ tathā .. 16 ..
2.4.d:
ग्रहण लक्षणं चास्य भविष्यति च खड्गवत् ॥
सुखग्राहं दृष्टिकान्तं शरमोक्षमुखं तथा ॥ 16 ॥
2.4.m: Its characteristic for holding will be like that of a sword: / easy to hold, pleasing to the eye, and suited for discharging arrows,

2.4.s:
ślakṣṇaṃ śliṣṭaṃ susaṃsthānaṃ sāravantaṃ susaṃhatam ..
avanāmasukhaṃ nityaṃ puṃnāmanavalotkaṭam ..17..
2.4.d:
श्लक्ष्णं श्लिष्टं सुसंस्थानं सारवन्तं सुसंहतम् ॥
अवनामसुखं नित्यं पुंनामनवलोत्कटम् ॥17॥
2.4.m: smooth, well-joined, well-proportioned, solid, firm, / always easy to bend, bearing a masculine name, and not excessively heavy.

2.4.s:
etadīdṛśakaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ cāparatnaṃ vidurbudhāḥ ..
rājñā cāpasya kartavyā pūjā bāṇavarasya ca .. 18 ..
2.4.d:
एतदीदृशकं श्रेष्ठं चापरत्नं विदुर्बुधाः ॥
राज्ञा चापस्य कर्तव्या पूजा बाणवरस्य च ॥ 18 ॥
2.4.m: Such a bow the wise know as a jewel among bows. / A king should perform worship of the bow and the excellent arrow,

2.4.s:
nityaṃ devakule rāma khaḍgasya ca viśeṣataḥ ..
ayasaścātha vaṃśasya śarasyātha śaro bhavet .. 19 ..
2.4.d:
नित्यं देवकुले राम खड्गस्य च विशेषतः ॥
अयसश्चाथ वंशस्य शरस्याथ शरो भवेत् ॥ 19 ॥
2.4.m: always in a shrine, O Rāma, and especially of the sword. / An arrow may be of iron, of reed, or of bamboo.

2.4.s:
śaravaṃśau grahītavyau śaratkāle bhṛgūttama ..
śarāḥ kirātajāḥ śreṣṭhāḥ kāñcīpurasamīpataḥ .. 20 ..
2.4.d:
शरवंशौ ग्रहीतव्यौ शरत्काले भृगूत्तम ॥
शराः किरातजाः श्रेष्ठाः काञ्चीपुरसमीपतः ॥ 20 ॥
2.4.m: Reeds and bamboos should be gathered in the autumn, O foremost of the Bhṛgus. / Arrows originating among the Kirātas near Kāñcīpura are excellent;

2.4.s:
tebhyo'pi te śreṣṭhatamāḥ skandajanmamahībhavāḥ ..
snigdhā nimagnaparvāṇaḥ sāravantaḥ samāhitāḥ .. 21 ..
2.4.d:
तेभ्योऽपि ते श्रेष्ठतमाः स्कन्दजन्ममहीभवाः ॥
स्निग्धा निमग्नपर्वाणः सारवन्तः समाहिताः ॥ 21 ॥
2.4.m: even better than those are arrows born in the land of Skanda's birth: / smooth, with flush joints, strong, straight,

2.4.s:
ṛjavo madhuvarṇābhāḥ sujātāḥ śāradā dṛḍhāḥ ..
snāyuśliṣṭāḥ sunetrāśca supuṅkhāḥ kalavāsasaḥ .. 22 ..
2.4.d:
ऋजवो मधुवर्णाभाः सुजाताः शारदा दृढाः ॥
स्नायुश्लिष्टाः सुनेत्राश्च सुपुङ्खाः कलवाससः ॥ 22 ॥
2.4.m: well-aligned, honey-colored, well-formed, autumnal, sturdy, / bound with sinew, with good notches, good feathers, and pleasing fletching.

2.4.s:
tailadhautāśca kartavyā rukmapuṅkhavibhūṣaṇāḥ ..
tathā viṣamaparvāṇaḥ phalaiśca vraṇavarjitaiḥ .. 23 ..
2.4.d:
तैलधौताश्च कर्तव्या रुक्मपुङ्खविभूषणाः ॥
तथा विषमपर्वाणः फलैश्च व्रणवर्जितैः ॥ 23 ॥
2.4.m: They should be washed with oil, adorned with gold fletchings, / with uneven knots, and with arrowheads free of flaws.

2.4.s:
eka tripuṅkhaṃ kartavyaṃ rājahaṃsacchadottaram ..
rukmapuṅkhasuvarṇāgramayaḥphalamanuttamam ..24..
2.4.d:
एक त्रिपुङ्खं कर्तव्यं राजहंसच्छदोत्तरम् ॥
रुक्मपुङ्खसुवर्णाग्रमयःफलमनुत्तमम् ॥24॥
2.4.m: One should make [an arrow] with one or three fletchings, covered with feathers of wild geese, / with a gold nock, a gold tip, and an unsurpassed iron arrowhead.

2.4.s:
snāyubaddhaṃ balaṃ tasya rukmabandhaṃ tu kārayet ..
vajraiśca lakṣaṇopetaiścitritaṃ taṃ tu kārayet..25..
2.4.d:
स्नायुबद्धं बलं तस्य रुक्मबन्धं तु कारयेत् ॥
वज्रैश्च लक्षणोपेतैश्चित्रितं तं तु कारयेत्॥25॥
2.4.m: Its strength should be secured with sinew, and bound with gold; / one should also decorate it with diamonds bearing auspicious marks.

2.4.s:
grahaṇaṃ tasya kartavyaṃ sāṃvatsarakarānnṛpaiḥ ..
tasya pūjā sadā kāryā sābhiṣekasamā bhavet .. 26 ..
2.4.d:
ग्रहणं तस्य कर्तव्यं सांवत्सरकरान्नृपैः ॥
तस्य पूजा सदा कार्या साभिषेकसमा भवेत् ॥ 26 ॥
2.4.m: It should be received by kings from the hand of an astrologer; / it should always be worshipped, equal to an royal consecration.

2.4.s:
yātrāyāmabhiṣeke ca maṅgaleṣu ca karmasu ..
sapatāke tu taṃ cāpaṃ sapatākaṃ tu kārayet ..
maṅgalyaṃ tannarendrāṇāṃ kathitaṃ bhṛgunandana .. 27 ..
2.4.d:
यात्रायामभिषेके च मङ्गलेषु च कर्मसु ॥
सपताके तु तं चापं सपताकं तु कारयेत् ॥
मङ्गल्यं तन्नरेन्द्राणां कथितं भृगुनन्दन ॥ 27 ॥
2.4.m: On military expeditions, at consecrations, and during auspicious rites, / one should provide that bow with a banner; / it is declared to bring auspiciousness to kings, O son of Bhṛgu.

2.4.s:
ye cāparatnaṃ vinataṃ tu bhūpāḥ suvarṇaratnopacitaṃ sadaiva ..
bāṇena sākaṃ paripūjayanti bhavanti te rāma vipannaduḥkhāḥ .. 28 ..
2.17
.. puṣkara uvāca ..
purā sumeruśikhare kāñcane ratnaparvate ..
svargaṅgāyāstaṭe brahmā yajñaṃ yajati bhārgava .. 1 ..
tasminyajñe sa dadṛśe vighnaṃ khe lohadānavam ..
vighnasya śamanaṃ tasya cintayāmāsa tattvavit .. 2 ..
tadā cintayatastasya puruṣaḥ pāvakādbabhau ..
nīlotpaladalaśyāmaḥ svarucā vañcitekṣaṇaḥ .. 3..
prāṃśuḥ suvadanaḥ śrīmānbalenāpratimo bhuvi ..
sa vavande tadā gatvā devaṃ kamalasambhavam .. 4 ..
abhyanandanta jātena tena devāssavāsavāḥ ..
tasmātsa nandako nāma khaṅgaratnamabhūttadā .. 5 ..
taṃ dṛṣṭvā bhagavānbrahmā keśavaṃ vākyamabravīt ..
khaḍgaṃ gṛhṇīṣva goptāraṃ dharmasya jagatāṃ pate .. 6 ..
2.4.d:
ये चापरत्नं विनतं तु भूपाः सुवर्णरत्नोपचितं सदैव ॥
बाणेन साकं परिपूजयन्ति भवन्ति ते राम विपन्नदुःखाः ॥ 28 ॥
2.17
॥ पुष्कर उवाच ॥
पुरा सुमेरुशिखरे काञ्चने रत्नपर्वते ॥
स्वर्गङ्गायास्तटे ब्रह्मा यज्ञं यजति भार्गव ॥ 1 ॥
तस्मिन्यज्ञे स ददृशे विघ्नं खे लोहदानवम् ॥
विघ्नस्य शमनं तस्य चिन्तयामास तत्त्ववित् ॥ 2 ॥
तदा चिन्तयतस्तस्य पुरुषः पावकाद्बभौ ॥
नीलोत्पलदलश्यामः स्वरुचा वञ्चितेक्षणः ॥ 3॥
प्रांशुः सुवदनः श्रीमान्बलेनाप्रतिमो भुवि ॥
स ववन्दे तदा गत्वा देवं कमलसम्भवम् ॥ 4 ॥
अभ्यनन्दन्त जातेन तेन देवास्सवासवाः ॥
तस्मात्स नन्दको नाम खङ्गरत्नमभूत्तदा ॥ 5 ॥
तं दृष्ट्वा भगवान्ब्रह्मा केशवं वाक्यमब्रवीत् ॥
खड्गं गृह्णीष्व गोप्तारं धर्मस्य जगतां पते ॥ 6 ॥
2.4.m:
Those kings who always worship a bent jewel of a bow, / adorned with gold and jewels, together with an arrow, have their misfortunes destroyed, O Rāma.
Puṣkara said: / Formerly, on the golden peak of Sumeru, the mountain of jewels, / on the bank of the heavenly Gaṅgā, Brahmā was performing a sacrifice, O descendant of Bhṛgu.
At that sacrifice, he saw an obstacle in the sky: the iron demon Lohadānava. / The knower of truth meditated on the pacification of that obstacle.
As he was meditating then, a person appeared from the fire, / dark as a blue lotus petal, blinding the eye with his radiance,
tall, handsome-faced, splendid, peerless in strength on earth. / Going forward then, he bowed to the lotus-born god.
The gods together with Indra rejoiced at his birth; / therefore, named Nandaka, he then became the jewel among swords.
Seeing him, the blessed Brahmā spoke these words to Keśava: / 'Take this sword, the protector of dharma, O Lord of the worlds!

2.4.s:
yajñavighnakaraṃ hatvā khaḍgenānena keśava ..
nipātaya mahābāho balinaṃ lohadānavam .. 7 ..
ityevamukto jagrāha grīvayā taṃ janārdanaḥ ..
gṛhītamātre devena vikośaḥ samapadyata .. 8 ..
khaḍgaḥ kamalapatrākṣo nīlotpalasamadyutiḥ ..
ratnamuṣṭirmahānrāma nirmalākāśasannibhaḥ .. 9 ..
etasminnantare tatra vyadṛśyata tadā mahān ..
karālaḥ kṛṣṇavadanaḥ śatabāhurmahodaraḥ.. 10..
prāṃśuḥ suvṛttadaṃṣṭrāgro balavām̐llauhadānavaḥ ..
yajñavighnārthinaṃ prāptaṃ sa dṛṣṭvā lohadānavam .. 11 ..
khaḍgamādāya vegena yayau taṃ prati keśavaḥ ..
sa keśavamanādṛtya devāñchakrapurogamān .. 12 ..
vidrāvayāmāsa tadā gadayā bhīmavegayā ..
tadā bhagneṣu deveṣu yuddhaṃ kṛtvā hariściram .. 13 ..
khaḍgena tasya gātrāṇi ciccheda madhuhā raṇe ..
khaḍgacchinnāni gātrāṇi nānādeśeṣu bhūtale .. 14 ..
2.4.d:
यज्ञविघ्नकरं हत्वा खड्गेनानेन केशव ॥
निपातय महाबाहो बलिनं लोहदानवम् ॥ 7 ॥
इत्येवमुक्तो जग्राह ग्रीवया तं जनार्दनः ॥
गृहीतमात्रे देवेन विकोशः समपद्यत ॥ 8 ॥
खड्गः कमलपत्राक्षो नीलोत्पलसमद्युतिः ॥
रत्नमुष्टिर्महान्राम निर्मलाकाशसन्निभः ॥ 9 ॥
एतस्मिन्नन्तरे तत्र व्यदृश्यत तदा महान् ॥
करालः कृष्णवदनः शतबाहुर्महोदरः॥ 10॥
प्रांशुः सुवृत्तदंष्ट्राग्रो बलवाम्̐ल्लौहदानवः ॥
यज्ञविघ्नार्थिनं प्राप्तं स दृष्ट्वा लोहदानवम् ॥ 11 ॥
खड्गमादाय वेगेन ययौ तं प्रति केशवः ॥
स केशवमनादृत्य देवाञ्छक्रपुरोगमान् ॥ 12 ॥
विद्रावयामास तदा गदया भीमवेगया ॥
तदा भग्नेषु देवेषु युद्धं कृत्वा हरिश्चिरम् ॥ 13 ॥
खड्गेन तस्य गात्राणि चिच्छेद मधुहा रणे ॥
खड्गच्छिन्नानि गात्राणि नानादेशेषु भूतले ॥ 14 ॥
2.4.m:
Slaying the causer of obstacles to the sacrifice with this sword, O Keśava, / strike down the mighty Lohadānava, O mighty-armed one!'
Addressed in this manner, Janārdana seized him by the neck; / as soon as he was taken by the god, he became unsheathed.
The sword, O Rāma, had eyes like lotus petals, a brilliance equal to a blue water-lily, / a jewel-studded hilt, was large, and resembled the cloudless sky.
At that moment, there appeared then a huge, / terrifying [demon] with a black face, a hundred arms, and a vast belly,
tall, with well-rounded tips of his fangs, the mighty iron-demon. / Seeing that iron-demon arrived, intent on obstructing the sacrifice,
Keśava took the sword and rushed swiftly toward him. / Disregarding Keśava, he [attacked] the gods headed by Śakra,
and then routed them with a club of terrible speed. / Then, when the gods were broken, Hari fought for a long time,
and in battle the slayer of Madhu severed his limbs with the sword. / The limbs severed by the sword [fell] upon the earth in various regions;

2.4.s:
nipetustasya dharmajña śataśo'tha sahasraśaḥ ..
nandakasya tu saṃsparśāttāni gātrāṇi bhārgava .. 15 ..
lohībhūtāni sarvāṇi prasādātkeśavasya tu ..
hatāyāsmai varaṃ prādādbhagavānmadhusūdanaḥ .. 16 ..
tvadaṅgāni pavitrāṇi bhaviṣyanti mahītale ..
āyudhāni ca tairloke kariṣyantīha mānavāḥ..17..
evamuktvā harirdevo brāhmaṇaṃ vākyamabravīt ..
vinā vighnaṃ makhamidaṃ kuru śīghraṃ jagadguro..18..
evamuktastadā brahmā yajñena madhusūdanam ..
ātmanā pūjayāmāsa susamiddhamanorathaḥ..19..
utpattiruktā khaḍgasya lohasya ca mayā tava ..
ataḥ paraṃ pravakṣyāmi khaḍgalakṣaṇamuttamam .. 20 ..
pradhānadehasaṃbhūtairdaityāsthibhirarindama ..
lohaṃ pradhānaṃ khaḍgārthe praśastaṃ tadviśeṣataḥ .. 21 ..
kaṭīkadūraṛṣikaṃ vaṅge śūrpākareṣu ca ..
videheṣu tathāṅgeṣu madhyamaṃ grāmacediṣu .. 22 ..
2.4.d:
निपेतुस्तस्य धर्मज्ञ शतशोऽथ सहस्रशः ॥
नन्दकस्य तु संस्पर्शात्तानि गात्राणि भार्गव ॥ 15 ॥
लोहीभूतानि सर्वाणि प्रसादात्केशवस्य तु ॥
हतायास्मै वरं प्रादाद्भगवान्मधुसूदनः ॥ 16 ॥
त्वदङ्गानि पवित्राणि भविष्यन्ति महीतले ॥
आयुधानि च तैर्लोके करिष्यन्तीह मानवाः॥17॥
एवमुक्त्वा हरिर्देवो ब्राह्मणं वाक्यमब्रवीत् ॥
विना विघ्नं मखमिदं कुरु शीघ्रं जगद्गुरो॥18॥
एवमुक्तस्तदा ब्रह्मा यज्ञेन मधुसूदनम् ॥
आत्मना पूजयामास सुसमिद्धमनोरथः॥19॥
उत्पत्तिरुक्ता खड्गस्य लोहस्य च मया तव ॥
अतः परं प्रवक्ष्यामि खड्गलक्षणमुत्तमम् ॥ 20 ॥
प्रधानदेहसंभूतैर्दैत्यास्थिभिररिन्दम ॥
लोहं प्रधानं खड्गार्थे प्रशस्तं तद्विशेषतः ॥ 21 ॥
कटीकदूरऋषिकं वङ्गे शूर्पाकरेषु च ॥
विदेहेषु तथाङ्गेषु मध्यमं ग्रामचेदिषु ॥ 22 ॥
2.4.m:
they fell, O knower of dharma, by the hundreds and thousands. / But from the touch of Nandaka, O Bhārgava, those limbs
all turned to iron through the grace of Keśava. / The blessed slayer of Madhu granted a boon to him when he was slain:
“Your limbs will become pure on the surface of the earth, / and with them men will fashion weapons in this world.”
Having spoken thus, Lord Hari addressed Brahmā: / “Perform this sacrifice swiftly without obstacle, O teacher of the world!”
Thus addressed, Brahmā then worshiped the slayer of Madhu / with the sacrifice himself, his desire fully accomplished.
The origin of the sword and of iron has thus been told by me to you. / Hereafter I shall declare the excellent characteristics of a sword.
O subduer of foes, from the bones of the Daitya originating from the principal part of his body / [comes] superior iron, which is particularly commended for making swords.
[The iron produced in] Kaṭīkadūra, Ṛṣika, in Vaṅga, in Śūrpākara, / in Videha, and also in Aṅga is middling; [so too] in Grāmacedi,

2.4.s:
sahagrāmeṣu nīpeṣu tathā kālañjarepi ca ..
lauhaṃ pradhānaṃ tajjānāṃ khaḍgānāṃ śṛṇu lakṣaṇam ..23..
kaṭīkadūrajātā ye darśanīyāstu te smṛtāḥ ..
kāyacchinnāstu ṛṣikā marmaghnā guravastathā ..24..
tīkṣṇāśchedasahā vāṅgā dṛḍhā śūrpārikodbhavāḥ ..
suhastāścaiva vijñeyā prabhāvanto videhajāḥ ..25 ..
aṃgadeśodbhavāstīkṣṇāścedi deśasamudbhavāḥ ..
kāliñjarā bhārasahāstathā vakṣyāmi lakṣaṇam .. 26 ..
supramāṇāṃgulāste tu śreṣṭhā khaḍgāḥ pramāṇataḥ ..
pramāṇaṃ tatra vijñāya tato hīnaṃ na dhārayet .. 27 ..
pramāṇābhyadhikaṃ caiva cchinnavaṃśaṃ tathaiva ca ..
śīghraḥ sumadhuraḥ śabdo yasya khaḍgasya bhārgava .. 28 ..
2.4.d:
सहग्रामेषु नीपेषु तथा कालञ्जरेपि च ॥
लौहं प्रधानं तज्जानां खड्गानां शृणु लक्षणम् ॥23॥
कटीकदूरजाता ये दर्शनीयास्तु ते स्मृताः ॥
कायच्छिन्नास्तु ऋषिका मर्मघ्ना गुरवस्तथा ॥24॥
तीक्ष्णाश्छेदसहा वाङ्गा दृढा शूर्पारिकोद्भवाः ॥
सुहस्ताश्चैव विज्ञेया प्रभावन्तो विदेहजाः ॥25 ॥
अंगदेशोद्भवास्तीक्ष्णाश्चेदि देशसमुद्भवाः ॥
कालिञ्जरा भारसहास्तथा वक्ष्यामि लक्षणम् ॥ 26 ॥
सुप्रमाणांगुलास्ते तु श्रेष्ठा खड्गाः प्रमाणतः ॥
प्रमाणं तत्र विज्ञाय ततो हीनं न धारयेत् ॥ 27 ॥
प्रमाणाभ्यधिकं चैव च्छिन्नवंशं तथैव च ॥
शीघ्रः सुमधुरः शब्दो यस्य खड्गस्य भार्गव ॥ 28 ॥

2.4.s:
kiṅkiṇī sadṛśastasya dhāraṇaṃ śreṣṭhamucyate ..
khaḍgaḥ padmapalāśāgro maṇḍalāgraśca śasyate ..29..
2.4.d:
किङ्किणी सदृशस्तस्य धारणं श्रेष्ठमुच्यते ॥
खड्गः पद्मपलाशाग्रो मण्डलाग्रश्च शस्यते ॥29॥
2.4.m: resembling a small bell, bearing it is said to be excellent. / A sword whose tip is like a lotus petal, and one whose tip is rounded, is praised;

2.4.s:
karavīrapalāśāgrasadṛśasya viśeṣataḥ ..
mahīghṛtasugandhaśca padmotpalasugandhikaḥ .. 30 ..
2.4.d:
करवीरपलाशाग्रसदृशस्य विशेषतः ॥
महीघृतसुगन्धश्च पद्मोत्पलसुगन्धिकः ॥ 30 ॥
2.4.m: especially one resembling the tip of an oleander petal. / A sword possessing the fragrance of earth or clarified butter, or smelling like a lotus or water-lily,

2.4.s:
varṇataścotpalākāraḥ savarṇo ṇaganasya ca ..
samāṅgulasthāḥ śasyante vraṇāḥ khaḍgeṣu bhārgava .. 31 ..
2.4.d:
वर्णतश्चोत्पलाकारः सवर्णो णगनस्य च ॥
समाङ्गुलस्थाः शस्यन्ते व्रणाः खड्गेषु भार्गव ॥ 31 ॥
2.4.m: resembling a water-lily in color, or of the same color as the sky, [is praised]. / Flaws situated at equal digits on swords, O Bhārgava, are praised;

2.4.s:
śrīvṛkṣaparvatā kāravaṃśapadmanibhāśca ye ..
maṅgalyānāṃ tathānyeṣāṃ sadṛśā ye ca bhārgava .. 32 ..
2.4.d:
श्रीवृक्षपर्वता कारवंशपद्मनिभाश्च ये ॥
मङ्गल्यानां तथान्येषां सदृशा ये च भार्गव ॥ 32 ॥
2.4.m: those that resemble the bilva tree, a mountain, a bamboo, or a lotus, / and those that resemble other auspicious things, O Bhārgava;

2.4.s:
kākolūkakabandhābhā viṣamāṅgulasaṃsthitāḥ ..
vaṃśānugāḥ prabhūtāśca na śastāste kadācana .. 33 ..
2.4.d:
काकोलूककबन्धाभा विषमाङ्गुलसंस्थिताः ॥
वंशानुगाः प्रभूताश्च न शस्तास्ते कदाचन ॥ 33 ॥
2.4.m: whereas those resembling a crow, an owl, or a headless trunk, situated at unequal digits, / following the spine, or numerous, are never praised.

2.4.s:
na khaḍge vadanaṃ paśyedvṛthā vivṛṇuyānna ca .
ucchiṣṭo na spṛśetkhaḍgaṃ niśi kuryācca śīrṣake ..
divā ca pūjayedenaṃ gandhamālyānusaṃpadā ..34..
2.4.d:
न खड्गे वदनं पश्येद्वृथा विवृणुयान्न च ।
उच्छिष्टो न स्पृशेत्खड्गं निशि कुर्याच्च शीर्षके ॥
दिवा च पूजयेदेनं गन्धमाल्यानुसंपदा ॥34॥
2.4.m: One should not look at one’s face in a sword, nor unsheathe it in vain; / impure from eating, one should not touch a sword; one should place it at the head at night, / and by day one should worship it with an abundance of perfumes and garlands.

khaḍgaṃ praśastaṃ maṇihemacitraṃ kośe sadā candanacūrṇayukte ..
saṃsthāpayedbhūmipatiḥ prayatnādrakṣettathainaṃ svaśarīravacca .. 35 ..

puṣkara uvāca ..

2.4.d:
खड्गं प्रशस्तं मणिहेमचित्रं कोशे सदा चन्दनचूर्णयुक्ते ॥
संस्थापयेद्भूमिपतिः प्रयत्नाद्रक्षेत्तथैनं स्वशरीरवच्च ॥ 35 ॥
2.18
पुष्कर उवाच ॥
इति सम्भृतसम्भारो राज्ञस्सांवत्सरस्तथा ॥
कालेऽभिषेचनं कुर्यात्तं कालं कथयामि ते ॥ 1 ॥
मृते राज्ञि न कालस्य नियमोऽत्र विधीयते ॥
तत्रास्य स्नपनं कार्यं विधिवत्तिलसर्षपैः ॥ 2 ॥
घोषयित्वा जयं चास्य सांवत्सरपुरोहितौ ॥
अन्यासनोपविष्टस्य दर्शयेतां जनं शनैः ॥ 3 ॥
स सान्त्वयित्वा स्वजनं भुक्त्वा बन्धनगांस्तथा ॥
अभयं घोषयित्वा च कालाकांक्षी तथा भवेत् ॥ 4 ॥
नाभिषेच्यो नृपश्चैत्रे नाधिमासे च भार्गव ॥
न प्रसुप्ते तथा विष्णौ विशेषात्प्रावृषि द्विज ॥ 5 ॥
न च भौमदिने राम चतुर्थ्यां न तथैव च ॥
नवम्यां नाभिषेक्तव्यः चतुर्दश्यां च भार्गव ॥ 6 ॥
2.4.m:
A ruler of the earth should carefully keep an auspicious sword, adorned with jewels and gold, / in a scabbard ever imbued with sandalwood powder, and protect it like his own body.
2.18
Puṣkara said:
Thus, when the provisions have been gathered, the king’s astrologer / should perform the consecration at the proper time; I shall declare that time to you.
When a king dies, no restriction of time is prescribed in this matter. / In that situation, his bathing should be performed according to rule with sesame seeds and mustard seeds.
Having proclaimed his victory, the astrologer and the royal chaplain / should gently present him, seated on another seat, to the people.
Having consoled his own people, fed those who were in prison, / and proclaimed freedom from fear, he should await the [proper] time.
A king should not be consecrated in the month of Caitra, nor in an intercalary month, O Bhārgava, / nor while Viṣṇu is asleep, especially in the rainy season, O twice-born;
nor on Tuesday, O Rāma, and likewise not on the fourth [tithi]; / he should not be consecrated on the ninth, nor on the fourteenth, O Bhārgava.

dhruvāṇi vaiṣṇavaṃ śākraṃ hastapuṣye tathaiva ca ..
nakṣatrāṇi praśasyante bhūmipālābhiṣecane .. 7 ..

2.4.d:
ध्रुवाणि वैष्णवं शाक्रं हस्तपुष्ये तथैव च ॥
नक्षत्राणि प्रशस्यन्ते भूमिपालाभिषेचने ॥ 7 ॥
नागश्चतुष्पदं विष्टिः किंस्तुघ्नः शकुनिस्तथा ॥
करणानि न शस्यन्ते व्यतीपातदिनं तधा ॥ 8 ॥
नक्षत्रमुल्काभिहतमुत्पाताभिहतं तथा ॥
सौरसूर्यकुजाक्रान्तं परिविष्टिञ्च भार्गव ॥ 9 ॥
मुहूर्ताश्चोक्तनक्षत्राः सतां मानहितप्रदाः ॥
कुजहोरा तथा नेष्टा सर्वत्र कुलिकस्तथा ॥ 10 ॥
वृषोऽथ कीटसिंहौ च कुम्भो लग्ने च शस्यते ॥
एतेषां जन्मलग्नाभ्यां यः स्यादुपचयस्थितः ॥ 11 ॥
तारा द्वितीया षष्ठी च चतुर्थी चाष्टमी च या ॥
नवमी च तथा शस्ता अनुकूलश्च चन्द्रमाः ॥ 12 ॥
सौम्याः केन्द्रगता लग्ना शुभाश्चैव त्रिकोणयोः ॥
पापाश्चोपचय स्थाने शस्तो लग्ने दिवाकरः ॥ 13 ॥
2.4.m:
The fixed constellations, the constellation of Viṣṇu, that of Śakra, and Hasta and Puṣya / are commended for the consecration of a ruler of the earth.
Nāga, Catuṣpada, Viṣṭi, Kiṃstughna, and Śakuni— / these karaṇas are not commended, nor is a day of Vyatīpāta;
nor a constellation struck by a meteor or struck by an unnatural portent, / or one occupied by Saturn, the Sun, or Mars, or surrounded by a halo, O Bhārgava.
The muhūrtas belonging to the spoken constellations grant respect and welfare to the virtuous; / the horā of Mars is not desired, nor is Kulika everywhere.
Taurus, Scorpio, Leo, and Aquarius are commended in the ascendant; / of these, whichever is situated in an upacaya house from the ascendant at birth [is favored].
The second, sixth, fourth, eighth, / and ninth asterisms are praised, and a favorable Moon.
Benefics in angles, in the ascendant, and benefics in the two trines, / and malefics in upacaya houses [are favorable]; the Sun in the ascendant is commended.

2.4.s:
lagne navāṃśaḥ kṣitijasya varjyo vargastathā tasya mahānubhāva ..
sūryasya vargaḥ sakalaḥ praśasto rājño'bhiṣeke sagraho nṛpāṇām .. 14 .. ..
2.19
puṣkara uvāca ..
kāryā paurandarī śāṃtiḥ prāgevāsya purodhasā ..
prāptebhiṣekadivase sopavāsaḥ purohitaḥ .. 1 ..
soṣṇīṣaḥ śvetavasanaḥ sitacandanabhūṣitaḥ ..
sitamālyopavītaśca sarvābharaṇabhūṣitaḥ ..2..
vedimullikhya yatnena kṛtvā ca vidhivattataḥ ..
juhuyādvaiṣṇavānmantrāṃstathā śākrānvicakṣaṇaḥ .. 3 ..
sāvitrānvaiśvadevāṃśca saumyāṃ ca vidhivattataḥ ..
śarmavarmagaṇaṃ caiva tathā svastyayanaṃ gaṇam .. 4 ..
āyuṣyamabhayaṃ caiva tathā caivāparājitam ..
sapātavantaṃ kalaśaṃ tathā kuryācca kāñcanam .. 5 ..
vahnerdakṣiṇapārśvasthaḥ śvetacandanabhūṣitaḥ ..
śvetānulepanaḥ sragvī sarvābharaṇabhūṣitaḥ .. 6 ..
2.4.d:
लग्ने नवांशः क्षितिजस्य वर्ज्यो वर्गस्तथा तस्य महानुभाव ॥
सूर्यस्य वर्गः सकलः प्रशस्तो राज्ञोऽभिषेके सग्रहो नृपाणाम् ॥ 14 ॥ ॥
2.19
पुष्कर उवाच ॥
कार्या पौरन्दरी शांतिः प्रागेवास्य पुरोधसा ॥
प्राप्तेभिषेकदिवसे सोपवासः पुरोहितः ॥ 1 ॥
सोष्णीषः श्वेतवसनः सितचन्दनभूषितः ॥
सितमाल्योपवीतश्च सर्वाभरणभूषितः ॥2॥
वेदिमुल्लिख्य यत्नेन कृत्वा च विधिवत्ततः ॥
जुहुयाद्वैष्णवान्मन्त्रांस्तथा शाक्रान्विचक्षणः ॥ 3 ॥
सावित्रान्वैश्वदेवांश्च सौम्यां च विधिवत्ततः ॥
शर्मवर्मगणं चैव तथा स्वस्त्ययनं गणम् ॥ 4 ॥
आयुष्यमभयं चैव तथा चैवापराजितम् ॥
सपातवन्तं कलशं तथा कुर्याच्च काञ्चनम् ॥ 5 ॥
वह्नेर्दक्षिणपार्श्वस्थः श्वेतचन्दनभूषितः ॥
श्वेतानुलेपनः स्रग्वी सर्वाभरणभूषितः ॥ 6 ॥
2.4.m:
A navāṃśa of Mars in the ascendant is to be avoided, as is his division, O noble one; / the entire division of the Sun is commended, along with the planet, for the consecration of kings.
Puṣkara said:
The Purandarī pacification rite must first be performed by his domestic priest. / When the day of the royal consecration has arrived, the domestic priest, observing a fast,
wearing a turban, clad in white garments, adorned with white sandalwood paste, / with a white garland and sacred thread, and adorned with all ornaments,
having carefully marked out the altar and duly prepared it, / the wise [priest] should then offer [oblations with] Vaiṣṇava mantras and Śākra mantras,
with Sāvitra mantras, Vaiśvadeva mantras, and Saumya mantras according to rule, / and likewise with the Śarmavarman group and the Svastyayana group,
with the Āyuṣya, the Abhaya, and likewise the Aparājita hymns. / He should also make a golden water-jar that holds the drops of oblation.
Standing on the right side of the fire, adorned with white sandalwood paste, / with white unguents, garlanded, and adorned with all ornaments,

2.4.s:
āsanasthamukhaṃ paśyennimittāni hutāśane .. 7 ..
paśyeyuranye ca tathā nṛsiṃha daivajñavākyānnipuṇaṃ svarūpam ..
sāṃvatsarasyātha sadasyamukhyāḥ sadasyamukhyāśca purohitasya .. 8 .. ..
2.20
puṣkara uvāca ..
pradakṣiṇāvartaśikhastaptajāmbūnadaprabhaḥ ..
rathaughamevanirghoṣo vidhūmaśca hutāśanaḥ ..1 ..
anulomasugandhaśca svastikākārasannibhaḥ ..
vardhamānākṛtiścaiva nandyāvartanibhastathā .. 2 ..
prasannārcirmahājvālaḥ sphuliṅgarahito hitaḥ ..
svāhāvamāne jvalanaḥ svayaṃ devamukhaṃ haviḥ .. 3 ..
yadā bhuṅkte mahābhāga tadā rājño hitaṃ bhavet ..
haviṣastu yadā vahnernasyātsimisimāyitam .. 4 ..
na varjeyuśca madhyena mārjāramṛgapakṣiṇaḥ ..
pipīlakāśca dharmajña tadā bhūyājjayī nṛpaḥ .. 5 ..
muktāhāramṛṇālābhe vahnau rājñāṃ jayo bhavet ..
tathaiva ca jayaṃ brūyātprastarasya pradāyini .. 6 ..
2.4.d:
आसनस्थमुखं पश्येन्निमित्तानि हुताशने ॥ 7 ॥
पश्येयुरन्ये च तथा नृसिंह दैवज्ञवाक्यान्निपुणं स्वरूपम् ॥
सांवत्सरस्याथ सदस्यमुख्याः सदस्यमुख्याश्च पुरोहितस्य ॥ 8 ॥ ॥
2.20
पुष्कर उवाच ॥
प्रदक्षिणावर्तशिखस्तप्तजाम्बूनदप्रभः ॥
रथौघमेवनिर्घोषो विधूमश्च हुताशनः ॥1 ॥
अनुलोमसुगन्धश्च स्वस्तिकाकारसन्निभः ॥
वर्धमानाकृतिश्चैव नन्द्यावर्तनिभस्तथा ॥ 2 ॥
प्रसन्नार्चिर्महाज्वालः स्फुलिङ्गरहितो हितः ॥
स्वाहावमाने ज्वलनः स्वयं देवमुखं हविः ॥ 3 ॥
यदा भुङ्क्ते महाभाग तदा राज्ञो हितं भवेत् ॥
हविषस्तु यदा वह्नेर्नस्यात्सिमिसिमायितम् ॥ 4 ॥
न वर्जेयुश्च मध्येन मार्जारमृगपक्षिणः ॥
पिपीलकाश्च धर्मज्ञ तदा भूयाज्जयी नृपः ॥ 5 ॥
मुक्ताहारमृणालाभे वह्नौ राज्ञां जयो भवेत् ॥
तथैव च जयं ब्रूयात्प्रस्तरस्य प्रदायिनि ॥ 6 ॥
2.4.m:
he should look at the face of [the king] seated upon the throne [and observe] omens in the sacrificial fire.
Others too should closely observe the true nature [of the signs] at the astrologer's word, O Narasiṃha: / the leading assembly members of the astrologer, and the leading assembly members of the domestic priest.
Puṣkara said:
A sacrificial fire whose flames curl clockwise, gleaming like refined gold, / roaring like a multitude of chariots, and free of smoke,
fragrant along the wind, resembling the svastika shape, / of the form of a vardhamāna, and likewise resembling a nandyāvarta,
with bright radiance, large flames, and free of sparks, is auspicious. / When the fire itself, the mouth of the gods, consumes the oblation
at the end of [the call of] 'svāhā', O highly fortunate one, then it will be auspicious for the king. / And when from the sacrificial fire there is no sizzling of the oblation,
and cats, deer, birds, and ants do not cross through the middle [of the area], / O knower of dharma, then the king will be victorious.
When the fire resembles a pearl necklace or a lotus stalk, victory belongs to kings; / likewise, one should declare victory when it gives a steady base [of flame].

2.4.s:
saṃkṣepataste'bhihitaṃ mayādya yallakṣaṇaṃ cāru hutāśanasya ..
sarvāgnikarmasvatha tena vidvānbhūyāttriloke tu jayī dvijendra .. 7 ..
2.4.d:
संक्षेपतस्तेऽभिहितं मयाद्य यल्लक्षणं चारु हुताशनस्य ॥
सर्वाग्निकर्मस्वथ तेन विद्वान्भूयात्त्रिलोके तु जयी द्विजेन्द्र ॥ 7 ॥
2.4.m: The auspicious characteristics of the sacrificial fire have thus been described to you by me today in brief. / Through this, the learned man would become victorious in the three worlds in all fire rites, O foremost of the twice-born.

2.5.s:
2.21
.. puṣkara uvāca .. ..
snānaṃ samācaredrājño homakāle purohitaḥ ..
ādau tu svecchayā snātaḥ punarmṛdbhiḥ samācaret .. 1 ..
2.5.d:
2.21
॥ पुष्कर उवाच ॥ ॥
स्नानं समाचरेद्राज्ञो होमकाले पुरोहितः ॥
आदौ तु स्वेच्छया स्नातः पुनर्मृद्भिः समाचरेत् ॥ 1 ॥
2.5.m:
Puṣkara said:
The domestic priest should perform the king's bath at the time of the fire offering. / Having first bathed at his own pleasure, he should perform it again with earths.

2.5.s:
parvatāgramṛdā tāvanmūrdhānaṃ śodhayennṛpaḥ ..
valmīkāgramṛdā karṇau candanaiḥ keśabālakān .. 2 ..
2.5.d:
पर्वताग्रमृदा तावन्मूर्धानं शोधयेन्नृपः ॥
वल्मीकाग्रमृदा कर्णौ चन्दनैः केशबालकान् ॥ 2 ॥
2.5.m: First the king should purify his head with earth from a mountain peak, / his ears with earth from an anthill, and his hair with sandalwood paste,

2.5.s:
candrālayamṛdā grīvāṃ hṛdayaṃ tu nṛpājirāt ..
karidantoddhṛtamṛdā dakṣiṇaṃ tu tathā bhujam .. 3 ..
2.5.d:
चन्द्रालयमृदा ग्रीवां हृदयं तु नृपाजिरात् ॥
करिदन्तोद्धृतमृदा दक्षिणं तु तथा भुजम् ॥ 3 ॥
2.5.m: his neck with earth from a moon-pavilion, his heart with [earth] from the royal courtyard, / and his right arm with earth uprooted by the tusk of an elephant,

2.5.s: vṛṣaśṛṅgoddhṛtamṛdā vāmaṃ caiva tadā bhujam .. 4 ..
2.5.d: वृषशृङ्गोद्धृतमृदा वामं चैव तदा भुजम् ॥ 4 ॥
2.5.m: and his left arm with earth uprooted by the horn of a bull,

2.5.s:
saromṛdā tathā pṛṣṭhaṃ codaraṃ sāṅgame mṛdā ..
nadīkūladvayamṛdā pārśve saṃśodhayettathā .. 5 ..
2.5.d:
सरोमृदा तथा पृष्ठं चोदरं साङ्गमे मृदा ॥
नदीकूलद्वयमृदा पार्श्वे संशोधयेत्तथा ॥ 5 ॥
2.5.m: his back with earth from a lake, his belly with earth from a confluence of rivers, / and he should purify his flanks with earth from both banks of a river;

2.5.s:
aśvasthānāttathā jaṃghe rājā saṃśodhayedbudhaḥ ..
rathacakroddhṛtamṛdā tathaiva ca karadvayam .. 6 ..
2.5.d:
अश्वस्थानात्तथा जंघे राजा संशोधयेद्बुधः ॥
रथचक्रोद्धृतमृदा तथैव च करद्वयम् ॥ 6 ॥
2.5.m: the wise king should purify his shanks with [earth] from a stable for horses, / and likewise both hands with earth raised up by a chariot wheel.

2.5.s:
mṛtsnātaḥ snapanīyaḥ syātpañcagavyajalena tu ..
tato bhadrāsanagataṃ mukhyāmātyacatuṣṭayam .. 7 ..
2.5.d:
मृत्स्नातः स्नपनीयः स्यात्पञ्चगव्यजलेन तु ॥
ततो भद्रासनगतं मुख्यामात्यचतुष्टयम् ॥ 7 ॥
2.5.m: Bathed with earths, he should be washed with water mixed with the five products of the cow. / Then, when he is seated on the auspicious throne, the four chief ministers,

2.5.s:
varṇapradhānaṃ bhūpālamabhiṣiñcedyathāvidhi ..
pūrvato hebhakumbhena ghṛtapūrṇena brāhmaṇaḥ .. 8 ..
2.5.d:
वर्णप्रधानं भूपालमभिषिञ्चेद्यथाविधि ॥
पूर्वतो हेभकुम्भेन घृतपूर्णेन ब्राह्मणः ॥ 8 ॥
2.5.m: led by their varṇa, should consecrate the king according to rule: / from the east, a brahmin with a golden jar filled with clarified butter;

2.5.s:
rūpyakumbhena yāmyena kṣīrapūrṇena kṣatriyaḥ ..
dadhnā ca tāmrakumbhena vaiśyaḥ paścimato dvija .. 9 ..
2.5.d:
रूप्यकुम्भेन याम्येन क्षीरपूर्णेन क्षत्रियः ॥
दध्ना च ताम्रकुम्भेन वैश्यः पश्चिमतो द्विज ॥ 9 ॥
2.5.m: from the south, a kṣatriya with a silver jar filled with milk; / from the west, O twice-born, a vaiśya with a copper jar [filled] with curd;

2.5.s:
māheyena jaleno dakśūdrāmātyo'bhiṣecayet ..
tato'bhiṣekaṃ nṛpaterbahvṛcapravaro dvijaḥ .. 10 ..
2.5.d:
माहेयेन जलेनो दक्शूद्रामात्योऽभिषेचयेत् ॥
ततोऽभिषेकं नृपतेर्बह्वृचप्रवरो द्विजः ॥ 10 ॥
2.5.m: and from the north, a śūdra minister should consecrate [him] with water using an earthen vessel. / Then a twice-born foremost among Rigvedins

2.5.s:
kurvīta madhunā rāma cchandogaśca kuśodakaiḥ ..
sampātavantaṃ kalaśaṃ tathā nutvā purohitaḥ .. 11 ..
2.5.d:
कुर्वीत मधुना राम च्छन्दोगश्च कुशोदकैः ॥
सम्पातवन्तं कलशं तथा नुत्वा पुरोहितः ॥ 11 ॥
2.5.m: should perform the consecration of the king with honey, O Rāma, and a Sāmavedin with kuśa-grass water. / And praising the jar containing the oblation drops, the domestic priest,

2.5.s:
vidhāya vahnirakṣāṃ tu sadasyeṣu yathāvidhi ..
rājasūyābhiṣeke tu ye mantrāḥ parikīrtitāḥ .. 12 ..
2.5.d:
विधाय वह्निरक्षां तु सदस्येषु यथाविधि ॥
राजसूयाभिषेके तु ये मन्त्राः परिकीर्तिताः ॥ 12 ॥
2.5.m: having duly performed the fire-protection among the assembly members, / should present [the oblations] with the mantras that are proclaimed for the Rājasūya consecration,

2.5.s:
taistu dadyānmahābhāga brāhmaṇānāṃ svanena tu ..
tataḥ purohito gacchedvedimūlaṃ tadaiva tu .. 13 ..
2.5.d:
तैस्तु दद्यान्महाभाग ब्राह्मणानां स्वनेन तु ॥
ततः पुरोहितो गच्छेद्वेदिमूलं तदैव तु ॥ 13 ॥
2.5.m: O highly fortunate one, to the sound of brahmins. / Then the domestic priest should immediately go to the base of the altar.

2.5.s:
vibhūṣitaṃ tu rājānaṃ sarvatobhadra āsane ..
śatacchidreṇa pātreṇa sauvarṇena yathāvidhi ..14..
2.5.d:
विभूषितं तु राजानं सर्वतोभद्र आसने ॥
शतच्छिद्रेण पात्रेण सौवर्णेन यथाविधि ॥14॥
2.5.m: And the [priest] skilled in the Yajurveda duly consecrates the adorned king / seated upon the sarvatobhadra throne with a golden vessel having a hundred perforations,

2.5.s:
abhiṣiñcati dharmajña yajurvedaviśāradaḥ ..
yā oṣadhīrauṣadhībhiḥ sarvābhiḥ susamāhitaḥ ..15..
2.5.d:
अभिषिञ्चति धर्मज्ञ यजुर्वेदविशारदः ॥
या ओषधीरौषधीभिः सर्वाभिः सुसमाहितः ॥15॥
2.5.m: O knower of dharma, fully composed in mind, with all medicinal herbs to the mantra 'yā oṣadhīḥ',

2.5.s:
rathe akṣeti gandhaiśca ābrahmanbrahmaṇeti ca ..
bījaiḥ puṣpaistathā cainaṃ rāma puṣpavatīti ca ..16..
2.5.d:
रथे अक्षेति गन्धैश्च आब्रह्मन्ब्रह्मणेति च ॥
बीजैः पुष्पैस्तथा चैनं राम पुष्पवतीति च ॥16॥
2.5.m: and with perfumes to 'rathe akṣa', and with seeds to 'ā brahman brāhmaṇa', / and with flowers, O Rāma, to the mantra 'puṣpavatīḥ',

2.5.s:
tenaiva cābhimantreṇa phalaistamabhiṣecayet ..
āśuḥ śiśāna ityeva sarvaratnaiśca bhārgava ..17..
2.5.d:
तेनैव चाभिमन्त्रेण फलैस्तमभिषेचयेत् ॥
आशुः शिशान इत्येव सर्वरत्नैश्च भार्गव ॥17॥
2.5.m: and with that same mantra he should consecrate him with fruits; / and with all jewels, O descendant of Bhṛgu, to 'āśuḥ śiśānaḥ',

2.5.s:
ye devāḥ purassadeti kuśābhiḥ parimārjayet ..
ṛgvedakratuto rājñe rocanāyā yathāvidhi .. 18 ..
2.5.d:
ये देवाः पुरस्सदेति कुशाभिः परिमार्जयेत् ॥
ऋग्वेदक्रतुतो राज्ञे रोचनाया यथाविधि ॥ 18 ॥
2.5.m: and he should wipe him with blades of kuśa grass to 'ye devāḥ purassadaḥ'. / In accordance with the Rigvedic rite, [applying] yellow pigment duly to the king,

2.5.s:
mūrdhānaṃ ca tathā kaṇṭhe gandhadvāreti saṃspṛśet ..
tato brāhmaṇamukhyāśca kṣattriyāśca viśastathā .. 19 ..
2.5.d:
मूर्धानं च तथा कण्ठे गन्धद्वारेति संस्पृशेत् ॥
ततो ब्राह्मणमुख्याश्च क्षत्त्रियाश्च विशस्तथा ॥ 19 ॥
2.5.m: he should touch his head and his throat with the mantra 'gandhadvārām'. / Then the chief brahmins, kṣatriyas, and vaiśyas,

2.5.s:
śūdrāśca vāramukhyāśca nānātīrthasamudbhavaiḥ ..
nādeyaiḥ sārasaiḥ kaupairnānākalaśasaṃsthitaiḥ .. 20 ..
2.5.d:
शूद्राश्च वारमुख्याश्च नानातीर्थसमुद्भवैः ॥
नादेयैः सारसैः कौपैर्नानाकलशसंस्थितैः ॥ 20 ॥
2.5.m: and śūdras, and chief courtesans, with [waters] originating from various sacred bathing sites, / river waters, lake waters, well waters contained in various jars,

2.5.s:
catussāgarajairlābhādalābhāddvijakalpitaiḥ ..
gaṅgāyamunayoścaiva nirjharaiśca tathodbhijaiḥ ..21 ..
2.5.d:
चतुस्सागरजैर्लाभादलाभाद्द्विजकल्पितैः ॥
गङ्गायमुनयोश्चैव निर्झरैश्च तथोद्भिजैः ॥21 ॥
2.5.m: born of the four oceans if obtained, or consecrated by twice-borns if not obtained, / and from the Gaṅgā and Yamunā, and from waterfalls and natural springs,

2.5.s:
chatrapāṇirbhavetkaścitkeciścāmarapāṇayaḥ ..
amātyamukhyāstaṃ kālaṃ kecidvetrakarāstathā .. 22..
2.5.d:
छत्रपाणिर्भवेत्कश्चित्केचिश्चामरपाणयः ॥
अमात्यमुख्यास्तं कालं केचिद्वेत्रकरास्तथा ॥ 22॥
2.5.m: some holding parasols in hand, some holding chowries in hand, / and at that time some chief ministers holding canes in hand,

2.5.s:
śaṃkhabherīninādena bandīnāṃ nisvanena ca ..
gītavāditraghoṣeṇa dvijakolāhalena ca .. .. 23 ..
2.5.d:
शंखभेरीनिनादेन बन्दीनां निस्वनेन च ॥
गीतवादित्रघोषेण द्विजकोलाहलेन च ॥ ॥ 23 ॥
2.5.m: to the sound of conches and kettledrums, and to the shouts of bards, / to the resonance of singing and musical instruments, and the tumultuous chanting of twice-borns,

2.5.s:
rājānamabhiṣiñceyussametya sahitā janāḥ ..
sarvaiḥ stuto'bhiṣiktaśca saṃmiśrajalamiśritam .. 24 ..
2.5.d:
राजानमभिषिञ्चेयुस्समेत्य सहिता जनाः ॥
सर्वैः स्तुतोऽभिषिक्तश्च संमिश्रजलमिश्रितम् ॥ 24 ॥
2.5.m: the gathered people assembled together should consecrate the king. / Praised by all and consecrated, [a vessel] filled with mingled waters,

2.5.s:
sarvauṣadhiyutaṃ puṇyaṃ sarvagandhayutaṃ tathā ..
ratnabījasamāyuktaṃ phalabījayutaṃ tathā .. 25 ..
2.5.d:
सर्वौषधियुतं पुण्यं सर्वगन्धयुतं तथा ॥
रत्नबीजसमायुक्तं फलबीजयुतं तथा ॥ 25 ॥
2.5.m: containing all medicinal herbs, auspicious, containing all perfumes, / accompanied by jewels and grains, and containing fruits and seeds,

2.5.s:
ūrjitaṃ sitasūtreṇa veṣṭitagrīvameva ca ..
śvetavastrāmrapatraiśca saṃvītaṃ suvibhūṣitam .. .. 26 ..
2.5.d:
ऊर्जितं सितसूत्रेण वेष्टितग्रीवमेव च ॥
श्वेतवस्त्राम्रपत्रैश्च संवीतं सुविभूषितम् ॥ ॥ 26 ॥
2.5.m: bound with strong white cord, with its neck wrapped around, / draped with white cloth and mango leaves, well adorned,

2.5.s:
kṣīravṛkṣalatāchatraṃ sudṛḍhaṃ kāṃcanaṃ navam ..
ādāya kalaśaṃ rājñā svayaṃ sāṃvatsarastathā .. 27 ..
2.5.d:
क्षीरवृक्षलताछत्रं सुदृढं कांचनं नवम् ॥
आदाय कलशं राज्ञा स्वयं सांवत्सरस्तथा ॥ 27 ॥
2.5.m: canopied with twigs of milky trees, very firm, golden, and new— / taking such a jar together with the king, the astrologer himself,

2.5.s:
mantrāvasāne kalaśaṃ dadyādbhṛgukulodvaha ..
tataḥ paśyenmukhaṃ rājā darpaṇe cātha sarpiṣi .. 28 ..
2.5.d:
मन्त्रावसाने कलशं दद्याद्भृगुकुलोद्वह ॥
ततः पश्येन्मुखं राजा दर्पणे चाथ सर्पिषि ॥ 28 ॥
2.5.m: at the conclusion of the mantras, should present the jar, O scion of Bhṛgu's lineage. / Then the king should gaze at his face in a mirror and in clarified butter.

2.5.s:
soṣṇīṣaḥ sitavastraśca maṅgalālambhanaṃ tataḥ ..
kṛtvā sampūjayedviṣṇuṃ brahmāṇaṃ śaṅkaraṃ tathā .. 29 ..
2.5.d:
सोष्णीषः सितवस्त्रश्च मङ्गलालम्भनं ततः ॥
कृत्वा सम्पूजयेद्विष्णुं ब्रह्माणं शङ्करं तथा ॥ 29 ॥
2.5.m: Wearing a turban and white garments, having then touched auspicious things, / he should worship Viṣṇu, Brahmā, and Śaṅkara,

2.5.s:
lokapālāngrahāṃścaiva nakṣatrāṇi ca bhārgava ..
tataḥ svapūjāṃ kurvīta śayanīyaṃ tato vrajet .. .. 30 ..
2.5.d:
लोकपालान्ग्रहांश्चैव नक्षत्राणि च भार्गव ॥
ततः स्वपूजां कुर्वीत शयनीयं ततो व्रजेत् ॥ ॥ 30 ॥
2.5.m: as well as the world-protectors, planets, and constellations, O descendant of Bhṛgu. / Then he should perform worship of himself, and go to the couch,

2.5.s:
vyāghracarmottaraṃ ramyaṃ sitavastrottaracchadam ..
purodhā madhuparkeṇa tatrasthaṃ taṃ samarcayet .. 31 ..
2.5.d:
व्याघ्रचर्मोत्तरं रम्यं सितवस्त्रोत्तरच्छदम् ॥
पुरोधा मधुपर्केण तत्रस्थं तं समर्चयेत् ॥ 31 ॥
2.5.m: covered with a tiger skin, charming, with a white cloth covering above. / Standing there, the domestic priest should venerate him with the honey-mixture.

2.5.s:
rājā caivārcayettatra sāṃvatsarapurohitau ..
madhuparkeṇa dharmajñastatastasya sadaiva hi .. 32 ..
2.5.d:
राजा चैवार्चयेत्तत्र सांवत्सरपुरोहितौ ॥
मधुपर्केण धर्मज्ञस्ततस्तस्य सदैव हि ॥ 32 ॥
2.5.m: And the king, knowing dharma, should then worship the astrologer and the priest / with the honey-mixture; and from then on, always,

2.5.s:
paṭṭabandhaṃ prakurvīta mukuṭasya ca bandhanam ..
tataḥ sa baddhamukuṭaḥ kāle pūrvaṃ mayeritam .. 33 ..
2.5.d:
पट्टबन्धं प्रकुर्वीत मुकुटस्य च बन्धनम् ॥
ततः स बद्धमुकुटः काले पूर्वं मयेरितम् ॥ 33 ॥
2.5.m: he should perform the tying of the royal fillet and the tying of the crown. / Then, with the crown bound, at the time previously spoken of by me,

2.5.s:
parārdhyāstaraṇopete pañcacarmottaracchade ..
dhruvā dyau iti mantreṇa sopaveśya purodhasā .. 34 ..
2.5.d:
परार्ध्यास्तरणोपेते पञ्चचर्मोत्तरच्छदे ॥
ध्रुवा द्यौ इति मन्त्रेण सोपवेश्य पुरोधसा ॥ 34 ॥
2.5.m: having been seated by the domestic priest with the mantra "Dhruvā dyauḥ" / upon an excellent seat covered with five hides—

2.5.s:
vṛkasya vṛṣadaṃśasya dvīpinaśca bhṛgūttama ..
teṣāmupari siṃhasya vyāghrasya ca tataḥ param .. 35 ..
2.5.d:
वृकस्य वृषदंशस्य द्वीपिनश्च भृगूत्तम ॥
तेषामुपरि सिंहस्य व्याघ्रस्य च ततः परम् ॥ 35 ॥
2.5.m: of a wolf, a cat, and a leopard, O foremost of the Bhṛgus, / and above them of a lion, and after that of a tiger—

2.5.s:
tatropaviṣṭasya tataḥ pratīhāraḥ pradarśayet ..
amātyāṃśca tathā paurānnaigamāṃśca vaṇigvarān .. 36 ..
2.5.d:
तत्रोपविष्टस्य ततः प्रतीहारः प्रदर्शयेत् ॥
अमात्यांश्च तथा पौरान्नैगमांश्च वणिग्वरान् ॥ 36 ॥
2.5.m: the door-keeper should then present to him seated there / the ministers, the citizens, the guild-heads, and the foremost merchants,

2.5.s:
tataḥ prakṛtayaścānyā yathāvadanupūrvaśaḥ ..
tato grahāvarāstrebhaturaṅgakanakottamaiḥ .. 37 ..
2.5.d:
ततः प्रकृतयश्चान्या यथावदनुपूर्वशः ॥
ततो ग्रहावरास्त्रेभतुरङ्गकनकोत्तमैः ॥ 37 ॥
2.5.m: and then the other subjects properly in succession. / Then, with excellent houses, weapons, elephants, horses, and gold,

2.5.s:
gojāvigrahadānaiśca sāṃvatsarapurohitau ..
pūjayitvā tataḥ paścātpūjayedbrāhmaṇatrayam .. 38 ..
2.5.d:
गोजाविग्रहदानैश्च सांवत्सरपुरोहितौ ॥
पूजयित्वा ततः पश्चात्पूजयेद्ब्राह्मणत्रयम् ॥ 38 ॥
2.5.m: and with gifts of cattle, goats, sheep, and estates, having honoured the astrologer and the domestic priest, / he should then afterwards honour three brahmins

2.5.s:
anenaiva vidhānena yena rājābhiṣecitaḥ ..
tatastvamātyānsaṃpūjya sāṃvatsarapurodhasaḥ .. 39 ..
2.5.d:
अनेनैव विधानेन येन राजाभिषेचितः ॥
ततस्त्वमात्यान्संपूज्य सांवत्सरपुरोधसः ॥ 39 ॥
2.5.m: by this very rite whereby the king was consecrated. / Then, having honoured the ministers, the astrologer, and the domestic priest,

2.5.s:
tato brāhmaṇamukhyānāṃ pūjanaṃ tu samācaret ..
govastratilarūpyānnaphalakāñcanagorasaiḥ .. .. 40 ..
2.5.d:
ततो ब्राह्मणमुख्यानां पूजनं तु समाचरेत् ॥
गोवस्त्रतिलरूप्यान्नफलकाञ्चनगोरसैः ॥ ॥ 40 ॥
2.5.m: the king should perform the honoring of the principal brahmins / with cows, clothing, sesame, silver, food, fruits, gold, and dairy products,

2.5.s:
modakākṣatapuṣpaiśca mahīdānaiśca pārthivaḥ ..
maṅgalālambhanaṃ kṛtvā gṛhītvā saśaraṃ dhanuḥ .. 41 ..
2.5.d:
मोदकाक्षतपुष्पैश्च महीदानैश्च पार्थिवः ॥
मङ्गलालम्भनं कृत्वा गृहीत्वा सशरं धनुः ॥ 41 ॥
2.5.m: with sweetmeats, unbroken rice, flowers, and gifts of land. / Having touched auspicious things, and having taken a bow with an arrow,

2.5.s:
vahniṃ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya praṇipatya tathā gurum ..
pṛṣṭhato vṛṣamālabhya gāṃ savatsāṃ ca pārthiva .. 42 ..
2.5.d:
वह्निं प्रदक्षिणीकृत्य प्रणिपत्य तथा गुरुम् ॥
पृष्ठतो वृषमालभ्य गां सवत्सां च पार्थिव ॥ 42 ॥
2.5.m: having circumambulated the fire, and bowed down to the preceptor, / having touched from behind a bull and a cow with its calf, O king,

2.5.s:
pūjayitvā ca turagaṃ mantritaṃ cābhiṣecitam ..
mantritaṃ dakṣiṇe karṇe svayaṃ vedavidā tataḥ .. 43 ..
2.5.d:
पूजयित्वा च तुरगं मन्त्रितं चाभिषेचितम् ॥
मन्त्रितं दक्षिणे कर्णे स्वयं वेदविदा ततः ॥ 43 ॥
2.5.m: and having honoured a horse that is consecrated with mantras and sprinkled, / consecrated into its right ear by one who knows the Veda himself,

2.5.s:
āruhya rājamārgeṇa svapuraṃ tu paribhramet ..
mukhyāmātyaiśca sāmantaiḥ sāṃvatsarapurohitaiḥ .. 44 ..
2.5.d:
आरुह्य राजमार्गेण स्वपुरं तु परिभ्रमेत् ॥
मुख्यामात्यैश्च सामन्तैः सांवत्सरपुरोहितैः ॥ 44 ॥
2.5.m: having mounted it, he should circumambulate his own city along the royal road, / accompanied by the chief ministers, vassals, astrologers, and domestic priests

2.5.s:
sahitaḥ kuñjarārūḍhairabhigacchecca devatāḥ ..
tāsāṃ saṃpūjanaṃ kṛtvā nagare yā niveśitāḥ .. 45 ..
2.5.d:
सहितः कुञ्जरारूढैरभिगच्छेच्च देवताः ॥
तासां संपूजनं कृत्वा नगरे या निवेशिताः ॥ 45 ॥
2.5.m: mounted on elephants, and he should go to the deities; / having performed worship to those that are established in the city,

2.5.s:
praviśeta gṛhaṃ rājā prahṛṣṭanaravāhanaḥ ..
dānamānāni satkārairgṛhṇīyātprakṛtīstataḥ .. 46 ..
2.5.d:
प्रविशेत गृहं राजा प्रहृष्टनरवाहनः ॥
दानमानानि सत्कारैर्गृह्णीयात्प्रकृतीस्ततः ॥ 46 ॥
2.5.m: the king should enter his palace, borne by delighted men. / Then he should receive the subjects with gifts, honours, and hospitality.

2.5.s:
saṃpūjitāstāstu visarjayitvā gṛhe svake syānmudito mahātmā ..
vidhānametatsamavāpya rājā kṛtsnāṃ sa pṛthvīṃ vaśagāṃ hi kuryāt..47..
2.22
rāma uvāca ..
maṃtreṇa yena dharmajña kuryādrājño'bhiṣecanam ..
tamahaṃ śrotumicchāmi tvatto varuṇanandana .. 1 ..
.. puṣkara uvāca ..
śṛṇuṣvāva hito mantraṃ rāma kalmaṣanāśanam ..
yenābhiṣikto nṛpatiściraṃ yaśasi tiṣṭhati .. 2 ..
rājño'bhiṣekaśabdānte daivavitkuśavāriṇā ..
kumbhādabhyukṣaṇaṃ kuryānmantrānte sakalaṃ nyaset .. 3 ..
surāstvāmabhiṣiñcantu brahmaviṣṇumaheśvarāḥ ..
vāsudevo jagannāthastathā saṅkarṣaṇo vibhuḥ .. 4 ..
pradyumnaścāniruddhastu bhavantu vijayāya te ..
ākhaṇḍalognirbhagavānyamo vai nairṛtistathā .. 5 ..
varuṇaḥ pavanaścaiva dhanādhyakṣastathā śivaḥ ..
brahmaṇā sahitaḥ śeṣo dikpālāḥ pāntu te sadā .. 6 ..
2.5.d:
संपूजितास्तास्तु विसर्जयित्वा गृहे स्वके स्यान्मुदितो महात्मा ॥
विधानमेतत्समवाप्य राजा कृत्स्नां स पृथ्वीं वशगां हि कुर्यात्॥47॥
2.22
राम उवाच ॥
मंत्रेण येन धर्मज्ञ कुर्याद्राज्ञोऽभिषेचनम् ॥
तमहं श्रोतुमिच्छामि त्वत्तो वरुणनन्दन ॥ 1 ॥
॥ पुष्कर उवाच ॥
शृणुष्वाव हितो मन्त्रं राम कल्मषनाशनम् ॥
येनाभिषिक्तो नृपतिश्चिरं यशसि तिष्ठति ॥ 2 ॥
राज्ञोऽभिषेकशब्दान्ते दैववित्कुशवारिणा ॥
कुम्भादभ्युक्षणं कुर्यान्मन्त्रान्ते सकलं न्यसेत् ॥ 3 ॥
सुरास्त्वामभिषिञ्चन्तु ब्रह्मविष्णुमहेश्वराः ॥
वासुदेवो जगन्नाथस्तथा सङ्कर्षणो विभुः ॥ 4 ॥
प्रद्युम्नश्चानिरुद्धस्तु भवन्तु विजयाय ते ॥
आखण्डलोग्निर्भगवान्यमो वै नैरृतिस्तथा ॥ 5 ॥
वरुणः पवनश्चैव धनाध्यक्षस्तथा शिवः ॥
ब्रह्मणा सहितः शेषो दिक्पालाः पान्तु ते सदा ॥ 6 ॥
2.5.m:
Having honoured them and dismissed them, the noble-minded one should rejoice in his own house. / A king, having performed this rite, would indeed bring the entire earth under his control.
2.22
Rāma said:
With which mantra, O knower of dharma, should one perform the king's consecration? / I wish to hear that from you, O son of Varuṇa.
Puṣkara said:
Listen attentively, O Rāma, to the sin-destroying mantra / by which a king, when consecrated, endures long in renown.
At the end of the word for the king's consecration, the astrologer should perform sprinkling / from the water-jar with kuśa grass and water; at the end of the mantra he should place everything.
"May the gods consecrate you: Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Maheśvara; / Vāsudeva, Lord of the Universe, and the all-pervading Saṃkarṣaṇa;
may Pradyumna and Aniruddha be for your victory; / may Ākhaṇḍala, the blessed Agni, Yama, and Nairṛta,
Varuṇa, Pavana, Dhanādhyakṣa, and Śiva, / and Śeṣa together with Brahmā, the guardians of the directions, protect you always.

2.5.s:
bhadro dharmo manurdakṣo ruciḥ śraddhā ca pārthiva ..
bhṛguratrirvasiṣṭhaśca sanakaśca sanandanaḥ .. 7 ..
sanatkumāraśca tathā bhagavānapi cāṅgirā ..
pulahaśca pulastyaśca marīciḥ kaśyapaḥ prabhuḥ .. 8 ..
ete tvāmabhiṣiñcantu prajādhyakṣāḥ samāgatāḥ ..
prabhāsurā barhiṣado hyagniṣvāttāstathaiva ca .. 9 ..
kravyādāścopahūtāśca ājyapāśca sukālinaḥ ..
ete tvāmabhiṣiñcantu pitaraścāgnibhiḥ saha .. 10 ..
lakṣmīrdevī satī khyātiranasūyā tathā smṛtiḥ ..
saṃbhūtissannatiścaiva kṣamā prītistathaiva ca .. 11 ..
svāhā svadhā ca tvā rājannabhiṣiñcantu mātaraḥ ..
kīrtilakṣmīrdhṛtirmedhā puṣṭiḥ śraddhā kriyā tathā .. 12 ..
buddhirlajjā vapuḥ śāntistuṣṭiḥ siddhiśca pārthiva ..
etāstvāmabhiṣiñcantu dharmapatnyaḥ samāgatāḥ .. 13 ..
2.5.d:
भद्रो धर्मो मनुर्दक्षो रुचिः श्रद्धा च पार्थिव ॥
भृगुरत्रिर्वसिष्ठश्च सनकश्च सनन्दनः ॥ 7 ॥
सनत्कुमारश्च तथा भगवानपि चाङ्गिरा ॥
पुलहश्च पुलस्त्यश्च मरीचिः कश्यपः प्रभुः ॥ 8 ॥
एते त्वामभिषिञ्चन्तु प्रजाध्यक्षाः समागताः ॥
प्रभासुरा बर्हिषदो ह्यग्निष्वात्तास्तथैव च ॥ 9 ॥
क्रव्यादाश्चोपहूताश्च आज्यपाश्च सुकालिनः ॥
एते त्वामभिषिञ्चन्तु पितरश्चाग्निभिः सह ॥ 10 ॥
लक्ष्मीर्देवी सती ख्यातिरनसूया तथा स्मृतिः ॥
संभूतिस्सन्नतिश्चैव क्षमा प्रीतिस्तथैव च ॥ 11 ॥
स्वाहा स्वधा च त्वा राजन्नभिषिञ्चन्तु मातरः ॥
कीर्तिलक्ष्मीर्धृतिर्मेधा पुष्टिः श्रद्धा क्रिया तथा ॥ 12 ॥
बुद्धिर्लज्जा वपुः शान्तिस्तुष्टिः सिद्धिश्च पार्थिव ॥
एतास्त्वामभिषिञ्चन्तु धर्मपत्न्यः समागताः ॥ 13 ॥
2.5.m:
Bhadra, Dharma, Manu, Dakṣa, Ruci, and Śraddhā, O king; / Bhṛgu, Atri, Vasiṣṭha, Sanaka, and Sanandana,
and Sanatkumāra, and the blessed Aṅgiras, / Pulaha, Pulastya, Marīci, and the lord Kaśyapa—
assembled together, may these lords of creatures consecrate you; / the Prabhāsuras, the Barhiṣads, and the Agniṣvāttas,
the Kravyāds, the Upahūtas, the Ājyapas, and the Sukālins— / may these Ancestors together with the fires consecrate you.
Goddess Lakṣmī, Satī, Khyāti, Anasūyā, and Smṛti, / Saṃbhūti, Sannati, Kṣamā, and Prīti,
Svāhā, and Svadhā: may the mothers consecrate you, O king; / Kīrti, Lakṣmī, Dhṛti, Medhā, Puṣṭi, Śraddhā, and Kriyā,
Buddhi, Lajjā, Vapuḥ, Śānti, Tuṣṭi, and Siddhi, O king— / may these wives of Dharma, assembled together, consecrate you.

2.5.s:

2.5.d:
अरुन्धती वसुर्जामी लम्बा भानुर्मरुत्वती ॥
संकल्पा च मुहूर्ता च साध्या विश्वास्तथैव च ॥ 14 ॥
धर्मपत्न्यस्तथान्यास्त्वामभिषिञ्चन्तु पार्थिव ॥
अदितिश्च दितिस्ताम्रा ह्यरिष्टा सुरसा मुनिः ॥ ॥ 15 ॥
कद्रूः क्रोधवशा प्राधा विनता सुरभिस्त्रिभिः ॥
एतास्त्वामभिषिञ्चन्तु कश्यपस्य प्रियाः स्त्रियः ॥ 16 ॥
पत्नी ते बहुपुत्रस्य सुप्रभा या च भामिनी ॥
समायात्वभिषेकाय विजयाय च पार्थिव ॥ 17 ॥
कृशाश्वपत्नी च तथा सुप्रभा च जया तथा ॥
अस्त्रग्रामस्तयोः पुत्रो विजयं विदधातु ते ॥ 18 ॥
मनोरमा भानुमती विशाला या च बाहुदा ॥
अरिष्टनेमी पत्न्यस्त्वामभिषिञ्चन्तु पार्थिव ॥ 19 ॥
कृत्तिका रोहिणी दैवी इल्वला बाहुरेव च ॥
पुनर्वसुश्च तिष्यश्च तथाश्लेषा च पार्थिव ॥ 20 ॥
2.5.m:
Arundhatī, Vasu, Jāmī, Lambā, Bhānu, Marutvatī, / Saṃkalpā, Muhūrtā, Sādhyā, and Viśvā—
may the other wives of Dharma likewise consecrate you, O king; / Aditi, Diti, Tāmrā, Ariṣṭā, Surasā, Muni,
Kadrū, Krodhavaśā, Prādhā, Vinatā, Surabhi [...]— / may these beloved wives of Kaśyapa consecrate you.
And the illustrious wife of Bahuputra who is Suprabhā, / may she come for consecration and for victory, O king.
And the wives of Kṛśāśva: Suprabhā and Jayā; / may their son, the host of divine weapons, grant you victory.
Manoramā, Bhānumatī, Viśālā, and Bāhudā— / may the wives of Ariṣṭanemi consecrate you, O king.
Kṛttikā, divine Rohiṇī, Ilvalā, and Bāhu, / Punarvasu, Tiṣya, and Āśleṣā, O king,

2.5.d:
मघा च फाल्गुनी पूर्वा तथैवोत्तरफाल्गुनी ॥
हस्तश्चित्रा तथा स्वातिर्विशाखा च नराधिप ॥ 21 ॥
अनुराधा तथा ज्येष्ठा मूलं च वसुधाधिप ॥
आषाढा च तथा पूर्वा तथैव नृप चोत्तरा ॥ 22 ॥
अभिजिच्च तथाश्वत्थो धनिष्ठा च नराधिप ॥
तथा शतभिषक्चैव पूर्वाभाद्रपदा च या ॥ 23 ॥
उत्तरा रेवती राजन्नश्विनी भरणी तथा ॥
एतास्त्वामभिषिञ्चन्तु सोमपत्न्यः समागताः ॥ 24 ॥
मृगी च मृगमन्दा च श्वेता भद्रासना हरिः ॥
भूता च कपिशा दंष्ट्री सुरसा सरमा तथा ॥ 25 ॥
एताः पुलहपत्न्यस्त्वामभिषिञ्चन्तु पार्थिव ॥
श्येनी भासी तथा क्रौञ्ची धृतराष्ट्री शुकी तथा ॥ 26 ॥
पत्न्यस्त्वामभिषिञ्चन्तु अरुणस्यार्कसारथेः ॥
आयतिर्नियतिश्चैव रात्रिर्निद्रा तथैव च ॥ 27 ॥

2.5.s:
etāstvāmabhiṣiñcantu lokasaṃsthānahetavaḥ ..
umā menā śacī caiva ghrūmrorṇā nivṛtistathā .. 28 ..
gaurī śivā ca siddhiśca velā caivātha naḍvalā ..
asiknī ca tathā jyotsnā yā ca devī vanaspateḥ..29..
etāstvāmabhiṣiñcantu devapatnyaḥ samāgatāḥ ..
mahākalpaśca kalpaśca manvantarayugāni ca ..30..
saṃvatsarāṇi sarvāṇi tathā caivāyanadvayam ..
ṛtavaśca tathā māsāḥ pakṣau rātryahanī tathā..31..
saṃdhyāśca tithayaścaiva muhūrtāḥ karaṇāni ca ..
ete tvāmabhiṣiñcantu kālasyāvayavāḥ śubhāḥ .. 32 ..
ādityaścandramā bhaumo budho jīvaḥ sitārkajau ..
grahāstvāmabhiṣiñcantu rāhuketū ca pārthiva .. 33 ..
svāyambhuvo manuḥ pūrvamanuḥ svārociṣastathā ..
auttamastāmasaścaiva raivataścākṣuṣastathā .. 34 ..
vaivasvato yathākarṇo dakṣo brahmasutāvubhau ..
dharmaputro rudraputro rocyo bhautyaśca yo manuḥ .. 35 ..
2.5.d:
एतास्त्वामभिषिञ्चन्तु लोकसंस्थानहेतवः ॥
उमा मेना शची चैव घ्रूम्रोर्णा निवृतिस्तथा ॥ 28 ॥
गौरी शिवा च सिद्धिश्च वेला चैवाथ नड्वला ॥
असिक्नी च तथा ज्योत्स्ना या च देवी वनस्पतेः॥29॥
एतास्त्वामभिषिञ्चन्तु देवपत्न्यः समागताः ॥
महाकल्पश्च कल्पश्च मन्वन्तरयुगानि च ॥30॥
संवत्सराणि सर्वाणि तथा चैवायनद्वयम् ॥
ऋतवश्च तथा मासाः पक्षौ रात्र्यहनी तथा॥31॥
संध्याश्च तिथयश्चैव मुहूर्ताः करणानि च ॥
एते त्वामभिषिञ्चन्तु कालस्यावयवाः शुभाः ॥ 32 ॥
आदित्यश्चन्द्रमा भौमो बुधो जीवः सितार्कजौ ॥
ग्रहास्त्वामभिषिञ्चन्तु राहुकेतू च पार्थिव ॥ 33 ॥
स्वायम्भुवो मनुः पूर्वमनुः स्वारोचिषस्तथा ॥
औत्तमस्तामसश्चैव रैवतश्चाक्षुषस्तथा ॥ 34 ॥
वैवस्वतो यथाकर्णो दक्षो ब्रह्मसुतावुभौ ॥
धर्मपुत्रो रुद्रपुत्रो रोच्यो भौत्यश्च यो मनुः ॥ 35 ॥

2.5.d:
एते त्वामभिषिञ्चन्तु मनवश्च चतुर्दश ॥
विश्वभुक्च विपश्चिच्च सुशान्तिश्च शिखी विभुः ॥ 36 ॥
मनोजवस्तथोजस्वी बहिरद्भुतशान्तिकौ ॥
वृषश्च ऋतधामा च दिवस्पाच्छुचिरेव च॥37॥
एते त्वामभिषिञ्चन्तु देवनाथाश्चतुर्दश ॥
रैवतश्च कुमारश्च तथा वर्चाविनायकः ॥ ॥ 38 ॥
वीरभद्रश्च नन्दी च विश्वकर्मा मनोजवः ॥
एते त्वामभिषिञ्चन्तु सुरमुख्याः समागताः ॥39॥
आत्मा चायुर्मनोदक्षो ह्यापः प्राणस्तथैव च॥
हविष्मांश्च गविष्ठश्च ऋतः सत्यश्च पार्थिव॥40॥
अभिषिञ्चन्तु राजंस्त्वां देवा ह्याङ्गिरसा दश ॥
क्रतुर्दक्षो वसुस्सत्यः कालः कामो मुनिस्तथा॥ ॥41॥
कुरवोन्मनुजश्चैव रोचमानस्तथैव च ॥
एते त्वामभिषिञ्चन्तु विश्वेदेवास्तथा दश॥42॥
अङ्गारकस्तथा सर्पो निरृतिश्च तथा घसः ॥
अजैकपादहिर्बुध्न्यो धूमकेतुस्तथा द्विजः ॥43॥

2.5.s:
bharataśca tathā mṛtyuḥ kāpāliratha kiṅkiṇiḥ ..
ekādaśaite rudrāstvāmabhiṣiñcantu pārthiva ..44..
bhuvano bhāvanaścaiva sujanyaḥ sujanastathā ..
kratuḥ sarvaśca mūrdhā ca tyājyaścaiva stutastathā .. 45 ..
