ete tvāmabhiṣiñcantu bhṛgavo nāma devatāḥ .. 46 ..
mano mantā ca prāṇaśca naro'pānaśca vīryavān ..
vinirbhayo nayaścaiva haṃso nārāyaṇastathā .. 47 ..
2.5.d:
भरतश्च तथा मृत्युः कापालिरथ किङ्किणिः ॥
एकादशैते रुद्रास्त्वामभिषिञ्चन्तु पार्थिव ॥44॥
भुवनो भावनश्चैव सुजन्यः सुजनस्तथा ॥
क्रतुः सर्वश्च मूर्धा च त्याज्यश्चैव स्तुतस्तथा ॥ 45 ॥
प्रसवश्चाव्ययश्चैव दक्षश्च मनुजाधिप ॥
एते त्वामभिषिञ्चन्तु भृगवो नाम देवताः ॥ 46 ॥
मनो मन्ता च प्राणश्च नरोऽपानश्च वीर्यवान् ॥
विनिर्भयो नयश्चैव हंसो नारायणस्तथा ॥ 47 ॥

2.5.s:
vibhuścāpi prabhuścāpi devaśreṣṭhā jagaddhitāḥ ..
ete tvāmabhiṣiñcantu sādhyā dvādaśa pārthiva .. 48 ..
2.5.d:
विभुश्चापि प्रभुश्चापि देवश्रेष्ठा जगद्धिताः ॥
एते त्वामभिषिञ्चन्तु साध्या द्वादश पार्थिव ॥ 48 ॥
2.5.m:
Vibhu, and Prabhu—foremost of the gods, benefactors of the world;
may these twelve Sādhyas consecrate you, O king;

2.5.s:
dhātā mitro'ryamā pūṣā śakreśau varuṇo bhagaḥ ..
tvaṣṭā vivasvānsavitā viṣṇurdvādaśamastathā .. 49 ..
2.5.d:
धाता मित्रोऽर्यमा पूषा शक्रेशौ वरुणो भगः ॥
त्वष्टा विवस्वान्सविता विष्णुर्द्वादशमस्तथा ॥ 49 ॥
2.5.m:
Dhātṛ, Mitra, Aryaman, Pūṣan, Śakra, Īśa, Varuṇa, Bhaga,
Tvaṣṭṛ, Vivasvat, Savitṛ, and Viṣṇu as the twelfth;

2.5.s:
ete tvāmabhiṣiñcantu kaśyapāditisambhavāḥ ..
ekajyotiśca dvijyotistricaturjyotireva ca.. .. 50 ..
2.5.d:
एते त्वामभिषिञ्चन्तु कश्यपादितिसम्भवाः ॥
एकज्योतिश्च द्विज्योतिस्त्रिचतुर्ज्योतिरेव च॥ ॥ 50 ॥
2.5.m:
born of Kaśyapa and Aditi, may these consecrate you;
Ekajyotis, Dvijyotis, Trijyotis, Caturjyotis,

2.5.s:
ekaśakro dviśakraśca triśakraśca mahābalaḥ ..
indrāśca gatyā dṛśyante tataḥ pratisakṛttayā .. 51 ..
2.5.d:
एकशक्रो द्विशक्रश्च त्रिशक्रश्च महाबलः ॥
इन्द्राश्च गत्या दृश्यन्ते ततः प्रतिसकृत्तया ॥ 51 ॥
2.5.m:
Ekaśakra, Dviśakra, and the very powerful Triśakra;
and the Indras seen in succession by their motion,

2.5.s:
mitaśca sammitaścaiva amitaśca mahābalaḥ ..
ṛtajitsatyajiccaiva suṣeṇaḥ satyajittathā .. 52 ..
2.5.d:
मितश्च सम्मितश्चैव अमितश्च महाबलः ॥
ऋतजित्सत्यजिच्चैव सुषेणः सत्यजित्तथा ॥ 52 ॥
2.5.m:
Mita, Sammita, the very powerful Amita,
Ṛtajit, Satyajit, Suṣeṇa, and Satyajit,

2.5.s:
atimitro namitraśca purumitraḥ purānitaḥ ..
ṛtaśca ṛtadhātā ca vidhātā dhāraṇo dhruvaḥ .. 53 ..
2.5.d:
अतिमित्रो नमित्रश्च पुरुमित्रः पुरानितः ॥
ऋतश्च ऋतधाता च विधाता धारणो ध्रुवः ॥ 53 ॥
2.5.m:
Atimitra, Namitra, Purumitra, Purānita,
Ṛta, Ṛtadhātṛ, Vidhātṛ, Dhāraṇa, Dhruva,

2.5.s:
vidhāraṇo mahātejā vāsavasya paraḥ sakhā ..
īdṛkṣaścāpyadṛkṣaśca etādṛgamitāśanaḥ .. 54 ..
2.5.d:
विधारणो महातेजा वासवस्य परः सखा ॥
ईदृक्षश्चाप्यदृक्षश्च एतादृगमिताशनः ॥ 54 ॥
2.5.m:
Vidhāraṇa of great splendour, the supreme friend of Vāsava,
Īdṛkṣa, Adṛkṣa, Etādṛk, Amitāśana,

2.5.s:
krītinaḥ prasadṛkṣaśca sarabhaśca mahā yaśāḥ ..
dhāturugrodhvanirbhīmo hyatiyuktaḥ kṣipaḥ sahaḥ .. 55 ..
2.5.d:
क्रीतिनः प्रसदृक्षश्च सरभश्च महा यशाः ॥
धातुरुग्रोध्वनिर्भीमो ह्यतियुक्तः क्षिपः सहः ॥ 55 ॥
2.5.m:
Krītin, Prasadṛkṣa, the far-famed Śarabha,
Dhātṛ, Ugra, Dhvani, Bhīma, Atiyukta, Kṣipa, Saha,

2.5.s:
dyutirvapuranādhṛṣyo vāsaḥ kāmo jayo virāṭ ..
ete tvāmabhiṣiñcantu marutaste samā gatāḥ .. 56 ..
2.5.d:
द्युतिर्वपुरनाधृष्यो वासः कामो जयो विराट् ॥
एते त्वामभिषिञ्चन्तु मरुतस्ते समा गताः ॥ 56 ॥
2.5.m:
Dyuti, Vapus, Anādhṛṣya, Vāsa, Kāma, Jaya, and Virāṭ;
may those Maruts, having gathered together, consecrate you,

2.5.s:
devā ekonapañcāśanmahābalaparākramāḥ ..
citrāṅgadaścitrarathaścitrasenaśca vīryavān .. 57 ..
2.5.d:
देवा एकोनपञ्चाशन्महाबलपराक्रमाः ॥
चित्राङ्गदश्चित्ररथश्चित्रसेनश्च वीर्यवान् ॥ 57 ॥
2.5.m:
the forty-nine gods of great strength and valour;
Citrāṅgada, Citraratha, and the mighty Citrasena,

2.5.s:
ūrṇāyuranaghaścaiva ugrasenaśca vīryavān ..
dhṛtarāṣṭraśca gopaśca sūryāvartastathaiva ca .. 58 ..
2.5.d:
ऊर्णायुरनघश्चैव उग्रसेनश्च वीर्यवान् ॥
धृतराष्ट्रश्च गोपश्च सूर्यावर्तस्तथैव च ॥ 58 ॥
2.5.m:
Ūrṇāyu, Anagha, and the mighty Ugrasena,
Dhṛtarāṣṭra, Gopa, and Sūryāvarta,

2.5.s:
yugapastraṇayaḥ kārṣṇirnaṃdaścitrastathaiva ca ..
kaliḥ śāliḥ śirā rājanparjanyo nāradastathā .. 59 ..
2.5.d:
युगपस्त्रणयः कार्ष्णिर्नंदश्चित्रस्तथैव च ॥
कलिः शालिः शिरा राजन्पर्जन्यो नारदस्तथा ॥ 59 ॥
2.5.m:
Yugapa, Straṇaya, Kārṣṇi, Nanda, Citra,
Kali, Śāli, Śiras, O king, Parjanya, and Nārada,

2.5.s:
vṛṣaparvā ca haṃsaśca tathā caiva hahā hūhūḥ ..
viśvāvasustumburuśca tathā ca suruciśca yaḥ .. 60 ..
2.5.d:
वृषपर्वा च हंसश्च तथा चैव हहा हूहूः ॥
विश्वावसुस्तुम्बुरुश्च तथा च सुरुचिश्च यः ॥ 60 ॥
2.5.m:
Vṛṣaparvan, Haṃsa, Hahā, Hūhū,
Viśvāvasu, Tumburu, and Suruci;

2.5.s:
ete tvāmabhiṣiñcantu gandharvāḥ pṛthivīpate ..
āhutyastā bhavatyaśca vargavatyastathaiva ca .. 61 ..
2.5.d:
एते त्वामभिषिञ्चन्तु गन्धर्वाः पृथिवीपते ॥
आहुत्यस्ता भवत्यश्च वर्गवत्यस्तथैव च ॥ 61 ॥
2.5.m:
may these gandharvas consecrate you, O lord of the earth;
Āhutis, Bhavatīs, and Vargavatīs,

2.5.s:
āyurvatyastathorjāśca tathā vai kuravāḥ stavāḥ ..
bahvāyuścāmṛtāyuśca bhuvaścaiva rucastathā .. 62 ..
2.5.d:
आयुर्वत्यस्तथोर्जाश्च तथा वै कुरवाः स्तवाः ॥
बह्वायुश्चामृतायुश्च भुवश्चैव रुचस्तथा ॥ 62 ॥
2.5.m:
Āyurvatīs, Ūrjās, Kurus, Stavas,
Bahvāyu, Amṛtāyu, Bhuvas, and Rucas,

2.5.s:
bhīravaḥ śobhayaṃtyaśca divyā yāścāpsarogaṇāḥ ..
ete tvāmabhiṣiñcantu samāgatya mahīpate .. 63 ..
2.5.d:
भीरवः शोभयंत्यश्च दिव्या याश्चाप्सरोगणाः ॥
एते त्वामभिषिञ्चन्तु समागत्य महीपते ॥ 63 ॥
2.5.m:
Bhīrus, Śobhayantīs, and whichever are the celestial troops of apsarases;
may these consecrate you, having gathered together, O lord of the earth;

2.5.s:
anavadyā satyakāmā cānūnā varuṇā priyā ..
anūpā subhagā caiva sukeśā ca manovatī .. 64 ..
2.5.d:
अनवद्या सत्यकामा चानूना वरुणा प्रिया ॥
अनूपा सुभगा चैव सुकेशा च मनोवती ॥ 64 ॥
2.5.m:
Anavadyā, Satyakāmā, Anūnā, Varuṇā, Priyā,
Anūpā, Subhagā, Sukeśā, and Manovatī,

2.5.s:
menakā sahajanyā ca parṇāśā puñjikasthalā ..
kṛtasthalā ghṛtācī ca viśvācī pūrvacityapi .. 65 ..
2.5.d:
मेनका सहजन्या च पर्णाशा पुञ्जिकस्थला ॥
कृतस्थला घृताची च विश्वाची पूर्वचित्यपि ॥ 65 ॥
2.5.m:
Menakā, Sahajanyā, Parṇāśā, Puñjikasthalā,
Kṛtasthalā, Ghṛtācī, Viśvācī, and Pūrvacitti,

2.5.s:
pramlocā cāpyanumlocā raṃbhā caivorvaśī tathā ..
pañcacūḍā sānumatī citralekhā ca pārthiva .. 66 ..
2.5.d:
प्रम्लोचा चाप्यनुम्लोचा रंभा चैवोर्वशी तथा ॥
पञ्चचूडा सानुमती चित्रलेखा च पार्थिव ॥ 66 ॥
2.5.m:
Pramlocā, Anumlocā, Rambhā, and Urvaśī,
Pañcacūḍā, Sānumatī, and Citralekhā, O king,

2.5.s:
miśrakeśī marīciśca vidyutparṇā tilottamā ..
adrikā lakṣmaṇā kṣepā asitā rucikā tathā ..67..
2.5.d:
मिश्रकेशी मरीचिश्च विद्युत्पर्णा तिलोत्तमा ॥
अद्रिका लक्ष्मणा क्षेपा असिता रुचिका तथा ॥67॥
2.5.m:
Miśrakeśī, Marīci, Vidyutparṇā, Tilottamā,
Adrikā, Lakṣmaṇā, Kṣepā, Asitā, and Rucikā,

2.5.s:
suhemā cātha hemā ca śāḍvalī ca vapustathā ..
suvratā ca subāhuśca sugandhā suvapustathā..68..
2.5.d:
सुहेमा चाथ हेमा च शाड्वली च वपुस्तथा ॥
सुव्रता च सुबाहुश्च सुगन्धा सुवपुस्तथा॥68॥
2.5.m:
Suhemā, Hemā, Śāḍvalī, Vapus,
Suvratā, Subāhu, Sugandhā, and Suvapus,

2.5.s:
puṇḍarīkā sudānā cāsudānā surasā tathā ..
hemā śāradvatī caiva sūnṛtā kamalālayā..69..
2.5.d:
पुण्डरीका सुदाना चासुदाना सुरसा तथा ॥
हेमा शारद्वती चैव सूनृता कमलालया॥69॥
2.5.m:
Puṇḍarīkā, Sudānā, Asudānā, Surasā,
Hemā, Śāradvatī, Sūnṛtā, Kamalālayā,

2.5.s:
sumukhī haṃsapādī ca vāruṇī ratilālasā ..
etāstvāmabhiṣiñcantu rājannapsarasaḥ śubhāḥ .. 70..
2.5.d:
सुमुखी हंसपादी च वारुणी रतिलालसा ॥
एतास्त्वामभिषिञ्चन्तु राजन्नप्सरसः शुभाः ॥ 70॥
2.5.m:
Sumukhī, Haṃsapādī, Vāruṇī, and Ratilālasā;
may these auspicious apsarases consecrate you, O king.

2.5.s:
prahlādaśca mahātejāstathā rājanvirocanaḥ ..
balirbāṇastathānye ca ditiputrāḥ samāgatāḥ.....
abhiṣiñcantu daityāstvāṃ divyenāpyambhasā svayam ..
vipracittimukhāḥ sarve dānavāstvāṃ samāgatāḥ .. 72 ..
2.5.d:
प्रह्लादश्च महातेजास्तथा राजन्विरोचनः ॥
बलिर्बाणस्तथान्ये च दितिपुत्राः समागताः॥॥।
अभिषिञ्चन्तु दैत्यास्त्वां दिव्येनाप्यम्भसा स्वयम् ॥
विप्रचित्तिमुखाः सर्वे दानवास्त्वां समागताः ॥ 72 ॥
2.5.m: And Prahlāda of great splendor, and likewise Virocana, O king, / Bali, Bāṇa, and the other sons of Diti who have assembled, / may the Daityas consecrate you themselves with divine water; / all the Dānavas headed by Vipracitti who have assembled,

2.5.s:
abhiṣiñcantu rājendra rājarājyena satvarāḥ ..
hetiścaiva prahetiśca mālī śaṅkustathaiva ca .. 73 ..
2.5.d:
अभिषिञ्चन्तु राजेन्द्र राजराज्येन सत्वराः ॥
हेतिश्चैव प्रहेतिश्च माली शङ्कुस्तथैव च ॥ 73 ॥
2.5.m: may they swiftly consecrate you, O king of kings, for imperial sovereignty; / and Heti, Praheti, Mālī, and likewise Śaṅku,

2.5.s:
sukeśī pauruṣeyaśca yajñahā puruṣādhamaḥ ..
vidyutsphūrjastathā vyāghro vadhaśca rasanastathā .. 74 ..
2.5.d:
सुकेशी पौरुषेयश्च यज्ञहा पुरुषाधमः ॥
विद्युत्स्फूर्जस्तथा व्याघ्रो वधश्च रसनस्तथा ॥ 74 ॥
2.5.m: Sukeśin, Pauruṣeya, Yajñahan, Puruṣādhama, / Vidyutsphūrja, likewise Vyāghra, Vadha, and Rasana,

2.5.s:
ete tvāmabhiṣiñcantu samāgamyādya rākṣasāḥ ..
siddhārtho maṇibhadraśca sumano nandanastathā .. 75..
2.5.d:
एते त्वामभिषिञ्चन्तु समागम्याद्य राक्षसाः ॥
सिद्धार्थो मणिभद्रश्च सुमनो नन्दनस्तथा ॥ 75॥
2.5.m: having assembled today, may these Rākṣasas consecrate you; / Siddhārtha, Maṇibhadra, Sumana, and Nandana,

2.5.s:
kāṇḍabhiḥ pañcamaścaiva maṇimānuyamām̐stathā ..
sarvānubhūtaḥ śaṃkhaśca piṅgākṣaścastarastathā .. 76 ..
2.5.d:
काण्डभिः पञ्चमश्चैव मणिमानुयमाम्̐स्तथा ॥
सर्वानुभूतः शंखश्च पिङ्गाक्षश्चस्तरस्तथा ॥ 76 ॥
2.5.m: Kāṇḍabhi, and as the fifth Maṇimat, as well as Uyamānt, / Sarvānubhūta, Śaṅkha, Piṅgākṣa, and likewise Astar,

2.5.s:
yaśo mandaraśobhī ca padmacandraprabhaṅkarāḥ ..
meghavarṇaḥ subhadraśca pradyotaśca mahāghasaḥ ..77..
2.5.d:
यशो मन्दरशोभी च पद्मचन्द्रप्रभङ्कराः ॥
मेघवर्णः सुभद्रश्च प्रद्योतश्च महाघसः ॥77॥
2.5.m: Yaśas, Mandaraśobhin, Padmacandraprabhaṅkara, / Meghavarṇa, Subhadra, Pradyota, and Mahāghasa,

2.5.s:
dyutimānketumāṃścaiva maulimāṃśca sudarśanaḥ ..
śvetaśca vipulaścaiva puṣpadanto jayāvahaḥ .. 78 ..
2.5.d:
द्युतिमान्केतुमांश्चैव मौलिमांश्च सुदर्शनः ॥
श्वेतश्च विपुलश्चैव पुष्पदन्तो जयावहः ॥ 78 ॥
2.5.m: Dyutimat, Ketumat, Maulimat, Sudarśana, / Śveta, Vipula, Puṣpadanta, Jayāvaha,

2.5.s:
padmavarṇo balākaśca kumudaśca balāhakaḥ ..
padmanābhaḥ sugandhaśca pravīro vijayaḥ kṛtiḥ .. 79 ..
2.5.d:
पद्मवर्णो बलाकश्च कुमुदश्च बलाहकः ॥
पद्मनाभः सुगन्धश्च प्रवीरो विजयः कृतिः ॥ 79 ॥
2.5.m: Padmavarṇa, Balāka, Kumuda, Balāhaka, / Padmanābha, Sugandha, Pravīra, Vijaya, Kṛti,

2.5.s:
pūrṇamāso hiraṇyākṣaḥ śatajihvaśca vīryavān ..
ete tvāmabhiṣiñcantu rājanyakṣendra sattamāḥ .. 80 ..
2.5.d:
पूर्णमासो हिरण्याक्षः शतजिह्वश्च वीर्यवान् ॥
एते त्वामभिषिञ्चन्तु राजन्यक्षेन्द्र सत्तमाः ॥ 80 ॥
2.5.m: Pūrṇamāsa, Hiraṇyākṣa, and the powerful Śatajihva— / may these best of Yakṣa chiefs consecrate you, O king.

2.5.s:
śaṃkhapadmastu rājendra makaraḥ kacchapastathā ..
ete tvāmabhiṣiñcantu nidhayastu samāgatāḥ .. 81 ..
2.5.d:
शंखपद्मस्तु राजेन्द्र मकरः कच्छपस्तथा ॥
एते त्वामभिषिञ्चन्तु निधयस्तु समागताः ॥ 81 ॥
2.5.m: Śaṅkha and Padma, O king of kings, Makara and Kacchapa— / having assembled, may these treasures consecrate you.

2.5.s:
palagāścaiva vakrāśca ye ca sūcīmukhā nṛpa ..
duḥpūraṇā viṣādāśca jvalanāṅgārakāstathā .. 82 ..
2.5.d:
पलगाश्चैव वक्राश्च ये च सूचीमुखा नृप ॥
दुःपूरणा विषादाश्च ज्वलनाङ्गारकास्तथा ॥ 82 ॥
2.5.m: The Palagas, the Vakras, and those that have needles for mouths, O king, / the Duḥpūraṇas, the Viṣādas, and likewise the Jvalanāṅgārakas,

2.5.s:
kumbhapātāḥ pratuṇḍāśca tapavīrā ulūkhalāḥ ..
akarṇāśca kuṣaṇḍāśca tathā ye pātra pāṇayaḥ .. 83 ..
2.5.d:
कुम्भपाताः प्रतुण्डाश्च तपवीरा उलूखलाः ॥
अकर्णाश्च कुषण्डाश्च तथा ये पात्र पाणयः ॥ 83 ॥
2.5.m: the Kumbhapātas, the Pratuṇḍas, the Tapavīras, the Ulūkhalas, / the Akarṇas, the Kuṣaṇḍas, and likewise those who hold vessels in their hands,

2.5.s:
pāṃsavaśca vituṇḍāśca nipuṇāḥ skandanāstathā ..
ete tvāmabhiṣiñcantu piśācānāñca jātayaḥ .. 84 ..
2.5.d:
पांसवश्च वितुण्डाश्च निपुणाः स्कन्दनास्तथा ॥
एते त्वामभिषिञ्चन्तु पिशाचानाञ्च जातयः ॥ 84 ॥
2.5.m: the Pāṃsus, the Vituṇḍas, the Nipuṇas, and likewise the Skandanas— / may these classes of Piśācas consecrate you.

2.5.s:
brahmacarye sthitā dāntāḥ sarvajñāḥ sarvadarśinaḥ ..
nānāprakāravadanā nānābāhuśirodharāḥ ..85..
2.5.d:
ब्रह्मचर्ये स्थिता दान्ताः सर्वज्ञाः सर्वदर्शिनः ॥
नानाप्रकारवदना नानाबाहुशिरोधराः ॥85॥
2.5.m: Steadfast in celibacy, restrained, all-knowing, all-seeing, / having various forms of faces, having manifold arms and necks,

2.5.s:
catuṣpathapurāṭṭālaśūnyālayaniketanāḥ ..
madhuratve bhavedevaṃ ye gatā manujeśvarāḥ .. 86..
2.5.d:
चतुष्पथपुराट्टालशून्यालयनिकेतनाः ॥
मधुरत्वे भवेदेवं ये गता मनुजेश्वराः ॥ 86॥
2.5.m: dwelling in crossroads, city watchtowers, and abandoned houses— / those lords of men who have departed may it be so in gentleness—

2.5.s:
te tvāmadyābhiṣiñcantu bhūtā bhūtapateḥ svayam ..
mahākālaṃ puraskṛtya narasiṃhaṃ ca mātaraḥ .. 87 ..
2.5.d:
ते त्वामद्याभिषिञ्चन्तु भूता भूतपतेः स्वयम् ॥
महाकालं पुरस्कृत्य नरसिंहं च मातरः ॥ 87 ॥
2.5.m: may those spirits of the Lord of Spirits themselves consecrate you today; / placing Mahākāla and Narasiṃha at the head, the Mothers,

2.5.s:
sarvāstvāmabhiṣiñcantu rājarājye narādhipa ..
guhaḥ skando viśākhaśca naigameyastathaiva ca .. 88 ..
2.5.d:
सर्वास्त्वामभिषिञ्चन्तु राजराज्ये नराधिप ॥
गुहः स्कन्दो विशाखश्च नैगमेयस्तथैव च ॥ 88 ॥
2.5.m: may they all consecrate you for imperial sovereignty, O ruler of men; / Guha, Skanda, Viśākha, and likewise Naigameya,

2.5.s:
abhiṣiñcantu rājam̐stvāṃ sarve skandagrahāḥ śubhāḥ ..
ḍākinyo yāśca yoginyaḥ khecarībhūcarīśca yāḥ .. 89 ..
2.5.d:
अभिषिञ्चन्तु राजम्̐स्त्वां सर्वे स्कन्दग्रहाः शुभाः ॥
डाकिन्यो याश्च योगिन्यः खेचरीभूचरीश्च याः ॥ 89 ॥
2.5.m: may all the auspicious Skanda-grahas consecrate you, O king; / and whatever ḍākinīs and yoginīs there are, both the sky-goers and earth-goers,

2.5.s:
sarvāstvāmabhiṣiñcantu sametya manujeśvara ..
garuḍaścāruṇaścaiva āruṇiśca mahākhagaḥ .. 90 ..
2.5.d:
सर्वास्त्वामभिषिञ्चन्तु समेत्य मनुजेश्वर ॥
गरुडश्चारुणश्चैव आरुणिश्च महाखगः ॥ 90 ॥
2.5.m: having assembled, may all of them consecrate you, O lord of men; / Garuḍa, Aruṇa, and Āruṇi, the great bird,

2.5.s:
saṃpātī vinataścaiva viṣṇugandhaḥ kumārakaḥ ..
ete tvāmabhiṣiñcantu suparṇāḥ pṛthivīpate .. 91 ..
2.5.d:
संपाती विनतश्चैव विष्णुगन्धः कुमारकः ॥
एते त्वामभिषिञ्चन्तु सुपर्णाः पृथिवीपते ॥ 91 ॥
2.5.m: Saṃpāti, Vinata, Viṣṇugandha, and Kumāraka— / may these birds consecrate you, O lord of the earth.

2.5.s:
anantaśca mahānāgaḥ śeṣo vāsukitakṣakau ..
saparṇīraśca kumbhaśca vāmanaścāñjanastathā .. 92 ..
2.5.d:
अनन्तश्च महानागः शेषो वासुकितक्षकौ ॥
सपर्णीरश्च कुम्भश्च वामनश्चाञ्जनस्तथा ॥ 92 ॥
2.5.m: And Ananta the great serpent, Śeṣa, Vāsuki, and Takṣaka, / Saparṇīra, Kumbha, Vāmana, and likewise Añjana,

2.5.s:
airāvato mahānāgaḥ kambalāśvatarāvubhau ..
ailamantraśca śaṃkhaśca karkoṭakadhanañjayau .. 93 ..
2.5.d:
ऐरावतो महानागः कम्बलाश्वतरावुभौ ॥
ऐलमन्त्रश्च शंखश्च कर्कोटकधनञ्जयौ ॥ 93 ॥
2.5.m: Airāvata the great serpent, both Kambala and Aśvatara, / Ailamantra, Śaṅkha, Karkoṭaka, and Dhanañjaya,

2.5.s:
mahākarṇamahānīlau dhṛtarāṣṭrabalāhakau ..
kumāraḥ puṣpadantaśca sumukho durmukhastathā .. 94 ..
2.5.d:
महाकर्णमहानीलौ धृतराष्ट्रबलाहकौ ॥
कुमारः पुष्पदन्तश्च सुमुखो दुर्मुखस्तथा ॥ 94 ॥
2.5.m: Mahākarṇa, Mahānīla, Dhṛtarāṣṭra, Balāhaka, / Kumāra, Puṣpadanta, Sumukha, and likewise Durmukha,

2.5.s:
sūcīmukho dadhimukhaḥ kāliyaḥ śālipiṇḍakaḥ ..
bilvapādaḥ pāṇḍurako nāgaścāpūraṇastathā .. 95..
2.5.d:
सूचीमुखो दधिमुखः कालियः शालिपिण्डकः ॥
बिल्वपादः पाण्डुरको नागश्चापूरणस्तथा ॥ 95॥
2.5.m: Sūcīmukha, Dadhimukha, Kāliya, Śālipiṇḍaka, / Bilvapāda, Pāṇḍuraka, and the serpent Āpūraṇa,

2.5.s:
kapilaścāmbarīṣaśca kumāraścātha kaśyapaḥ ..
prahrādaḥ puṣpadantaśca gandharvaśca manasvikaḥ.. 96 ..
2.5.d:
कपिलश्चाम्बरीषश्च कुमारश्चाथ कश्यपः ॥
प्रह्रादः पुष्पदन्तश्च गन्धर्वश्च मनस्विकः॥ 96 ॥
2.5.m: Kapila, Ambarīṣa, Kumāra, and then Kaśyapa, / Prahrāda, Puṣpadanta, Gandharva, and Manasvika,

2.5.s:
nahuṣaḥ khararomā ca śaṃkhapālastathaiva ca ..
padmaśca kulikaścaiva pāṇirityevamādayaḥ .. 97 ..
2.5.d:
नहुषः खररोमा च शंखपालस्तथैव च ॥
पद्मश्च कुलिकश्चैव पाणिरित्येवमादयः ॥ 97 ॥
2.5.m: Nahuṣa, Khararoman, and likewise Śaṅkhapāla, / Padma, Kulika, Pāṇi, and others of this kind—

2.5.s:
nāgāstvāmabhiṣiñcantu rājarājyena pārthiva ..
kumudairāvaṇau padmaḥ puṣpa danto'tha vāmanaḥ .. 98 ..
2.5.d:
नागास्त्वामभिषिञ्चन्तु राजराज्येन पार्थिव ॥
कुमुदैरावणौ पद्मः पुष्प दन्तोऽथ वामनः ॥ 98 ॥
2.5.m: may the serpents consecrate you for imperial sovereignty, O king; / Kumuda, Airāvaṇa, Padma, Puṣpadanta, then Vāmana,

2.5.s:
supratīkoñjano nīlaḥ pāntu tvāṃ sarvataḥ sadā ..
cakraṃ triśūlaṃ vajraśca nandakostrāṇi cāpyatha .. 99 ..
2.5.d:
सुप्रतीकोञ्जनो नीलः पान्तु त्वां सर्वतः सदा ॥
चक्रं त्रिशूलं वज्रश्च नन्दकोस्त्राणि चाप्यथ ॥ 99 ॥
2.5.m: Supratīka, Añjana, and Nīla—may they protect you always on all sides; / the discus, the trident, the vajra, Nandaka, and the weapons,

2.5.s:
paitāmahāstathā haṃsā vṛṣabhaḥ śaṅkarasya ca ..
durgāsiṃhaśca pāntu tvāṃ yamasya mahiṣastathā ..100..
2.5.d:
पैतामहास्तथा हंसा वृषभः शङ्करस्य च ॥
दुर्गासिंहश्च पान्तु त्वां यमस्य महिषस्तथा ॥100॥
2.5.m: and the swans of the Grandfather, the bull of Śaṅkara, / Durgā’s lion, and Yama’s buffalo—may they protect you;

2.5.s:
uccaiḥśravāścāśvapatistathā dhanvantarirnṛpa ..
kaustubhaḥ śaṃkharājaśca pāntu tvāṃ sarvataḥ sadā ..101..
2.5.d:
उच्चैःश्रवाश्चाश्वपतिस्तथा धन्वन्तरिर्नृप ॥
कौस्तुभः शंखराजश्च पान्तु त्वां सर्वतः सदा ॥101॥
2.5.m: Uccaiḥśravas, lord of horses, and likewise Dhanvantari, O king, / the Kaustubha jewel, and the king of conches—may they protect you always on all sides.

2.5.s:
sarve'bhiṣekaṃ dattvā te diśantu vijayaṃ dhuvam ..
dharmaśca vyavasāyaśca satyo dānaṃ tapastathā .. 102 ..
2.5.d:
सर्वेऽभिषेकं दत्त्वा ते दिशन्तु विजयं धुवम् ॥
धर्मश्च व्यवसायश्च सत्यो दानं तपस्तथा ॥ 102 ॥
2.5.m: Having all performed the consecration, may they grant you firm victory; / Dharma, Resolution, Truth, Generosity, and Asceticism,

2.5.s:
yamo yajñastathā vāyurbrahmacarya damaḥ śamaḥ ..
ete tvāmabhiṣiñcantu citraguptaśca pārthiva .. 103 ..
2.5.d:
यमो यज्ञस्तथा वायुर्ब्रह्मचर्य दमः शमः ॥
एते त्वामभिषिञ्चन्तु चित्रगुप्तश्च पार्थिव ॥ 103 ॥
2.5.m: Yama, Sacrifice, Vāyu, Celibacy, Self-restraint, Tranquility— / may these consecrate you, and Citragupta, O king;

2.5.s:
daṇḍaśca piṅgalaścaiva mṛtyukālāvubhau tathā ..
vālakhilyāstathā sarve bhavantu vijayāya te ..104..
2.5.d:
दण्डश्च पिङ्गलश्चैव मृत्युकालावुभौ तथा ॥
वालखिल्यास्तथा सर्वे भवन्तु विजयाय ते ॥104॥
2.5.m: Daṇḍa, Piṅgala, both Death and Time, / and likewise all the Vālakhilyas—may they be for your victory.

2.5.s:
digdhenavaścatasrastvāṃ surābhiśca tathā nṛpa ..
abhiṣiñcantu sarvābhirgobhiḥ sārdhaṃ nareśvara ..105 ..
2.5.d:
दिग्धेनवश्चतस्रस्त्वां सुराभिश्च तथा नृप ॥
अभिषिञ्चन्तु सर्वाभिर्गोभिः सार्धं नरेश्वर ॥105 ॥
2.5.m: May the four cows of the directions and Surabhi, O king, / consecrate you along with all cows, O ruler of men.

2.5.s:
vedavyāsaśca vālmīkiḥ kamaṭho'tha parāśaraḥ ..
devalaḥ parvataścaiva durvāsāśca tathā muniḥ .. 106 ..
2.5.d:
वेदव्यासश्च वाल्मीकिः कमठोऽथ पराशरः ॥
देवलः पर्वतश्चैव दुर्वासाश्च तथा मुनिः ॥ 106 ॥
2.5.m: Vedavyāsa, Vālmīki, Kamaṭha, then Parāśara, / Devala, Parvata, and likewise the sage Durvāsas,

2.5.s:
yājñavalkyaśca jābāliḥ jamadagniḥ śuciśravāḥ ..
viśvāmitraḥ sthūlaśirāścyavano'trirvidūrathaḥ .. 107 ..
2.5.d:
याज्ञवल्क्यश्च जाबालिः जमदग्निः शुचिश्रवाः ॥
विश्वामित्रः स्थूलशिराश्च्यवनोऽत्रिर्विदूरथः ॥ 107 ॥
2.5.m: Yājñavalkya, Jābāli, Jamadagni, Śuciśravas, / Viśvāmitra, Sthūlaśiras, Cyavana, Atri, Vidūratha,

2.5.s:
ekataśca dvitaścaiva trito gautamagālavau ..
śāṇḍilyaśca bharadvājo maudgalyo vedavāhanaḥ .. 108..
2.5.d:
एकतश्च द्वितश्चैव त्रितो गौतमगालवौ ॥
शाण्डिल्यश्च भरद्वाजो मौद्गल्यो वेदवाहनः ॥ 108॥
2.5.m: Ekata, Dvita, Trita, Gautama, Gālava, / Śāṇḍilya, Bharadvāja, Maudgalya, Vedavāhana,

2.5.s:
bṛhadaśvaḥ kuṭiśaṭho jaṭājānurghaṭodaraḥ ..
yavakrīto'rtharaityaśca ātmavānatha jaiminiḥ ..109..
2.5.d:
बृहदश्वः कुटिशठो जटाजानुर्घटोदरः ॥
यवक्रीतोऽर्थरैत्यश्च आत्मवानथ जैमिनिः ॥109॥
2.5.m: Bṛhadaśva, Kuṭiśaṭha, Jaṭājānu, Ghaṭodara, / Yavakrīta, Artharaitya, Ātmavat, and then Jaimini,

2.5.s:
ṛṣiḥ śārṅgaravaścaiva tathāgastyo mahātapāḥ ..
unmuvurmumuvuścaiva idhmabāhurmahodayaḥ .. 110 ..
2.5.d:
ऋषिः शार्ङ्गरवश्चैव तथागस्त्यो महातपाः ॥
उन्मुवुर्मुमुवुश्चैव इध्मबाहुर्महोदयः ॥ 110 ॥
2.5.m: the sage Śārṅgarava, and likewise Agastya of great austerities, / Unmuvu, Mumuvu, Idhmabāhu, Mahodaya,

2.5.s:
kātyāyanaśca kaṇvaśca valvakāmborunandanaḥ ..
ete tvāmabhiṣiñcantu ṛṣayaḥ pārthivottama .. 111 ..
2.5.d:
कात्यायनश्च कण्वश्च वल्वकाम्बोरुनन्दनः ॥
एते त्वामभिषिञ्चन्तु ऋषयः पार्थिवोत्तम ॥ 111 ॥
2.5.m: Kātyāyana, Kaṇva, and Valvakāmborunandana— / may these sages consecrate you, O best of kings.

2.5.s:
pṛthurdilīpo bharato duṣyantaḥ śatrujidbalī ..
manuḥ kakutsthaścānenā yuvanāśvo jayadrathaḥ .. 112 ..
2.5.d:
पृथुर्दिलीपो भरतो दुष्यन्तः शत्रुजिद्बली ॥
मनुः ककुत्स्थश्चानेना युवनाश्वो जयद्रथः ॥ 112 ॥
2.5.m: Pṛthu, Dilīpa, Bharata, Duṣyanta, the mighty Śatrujit, / Manu, Kakutstha, Anenas, Yuvanāśva, Jayadratha,

2.5.s:
māndhātā mucukundaśca tathā rājā purūravāḥ ..
āyuśca nahuṣaścaiva yayātiraparājitaḥ .. 113 ..
2.5.d:
मान्धाता मुचुकुन्दश्च तथा राजा पुरूरवाः ॥
आयुश्च नहुषश्चैव ययातिरपराजितः ॥ 113 ॥
2.5.m: Māndhātṛ, Mucukunda, and likewise King Purūravas, / Āyu, Nahuṣa, and the undefeated Yayāti,

2.5.s:
ikṣvākuśca yaduścaiva punarbhūriśravāstathā ..
ambarīṣaśca nābhāgo bṛhadaśvo mahāhanuḥ .. 114 ..
2.5.d:
इक्ष्वाकुश्च यदुश्चैव पुनर्भूरिश्रवास्तथा ॥
अम्बरीषश्च नाभागो बृहदश्वो महाहनुः ॥ 114 ॥
2.5.m: Ikṣvāku, Yadu, and again Bhūriśravas, / Ambarīṣa, Nābhāga, Bṛhadaśva, Mahāhanu,

2.5.s:
pradyumnaścātha sudyumno bhūridyumnaśca sṛñjayaḥ ..
ete cānye ca rājānastava rājandivaṅgatāḥ ..115 ..
2.5.d:
प्रद्युम्नश्चाथ सुद्युम्नो भूरिद्युम्नश्च सृञ्जयः ॥
एते चान्ये च राजानस्तव राजन्दिवङ्गताः ॥115 ॥
2.5.m: Pradyumna, Sudyumna, Bhūridyumna, and Sṛñjaya— / these and other kings of yours who have gone to heaven, O king,

2.5.s:
samāyāntvabhiṣekāya vijayāya tathā śriye ..
parjanyādyāstathā sarve vāstudevāssamāsataḥ .. 116 ..
2.5.d:
समायान्त्वभिषेकाय विजयाय तथा श्रिये ॥
पर्जन्याद्यास्तथा सर्वे वास्तुदेवास्समासतः ॥ 116 ॥
2.5.m: May they assemble for your consecration, for victory and prosperity, / and all the site-deities, beginning with Parjanya, in their entirety.

2.5.s:
drumāścauṣadhayo ratnabījāni vividhāni ca ..
sarve tvāmabhiṣiñcantu rājanrājyena satvarāḥ .. 117 ..
2.5.d:
द्रुमाश्चौषधयो रत्नबीजानि विविधानि च ॥
सर्वे त्वामभिषिञ्चन्तु राजन्राज्येन सत्वराः ॥ 117 ॥
2.5.m: May trees, medicinal herbs, jewels, and diverse seeds— / may all of them swiftly consecrate you to kingship, O king!

2.5.s:
puruṣaścāprameyātmā mahābhūtāni yāni ca ..
pṛthivīvāyurākāśamāpo jyotistathaiva ca .. 118 ..
2.5.d:
पुरुषश्चाप्रमेयात्मा महाभूतानि यानि च ॥
पृथिवीवायुराकाशमापो ज्योतिस्तथैव च ॥ 118 ॥
2.5.m: The Cosmic Person of immeasurable nature, and whichever gross elements there are: / earth, wind, ether, water, and fire;

2.5.s:
manobuddhistathaivātmā avyaktaśca mahīpate ..
ete tvāmabhiṣiñcantu sametā vasudhādhipa .. 119 ..
2.5.d:
मनोबुद्धिस्तथैवात्मा अव्यक्तश्च महीपते ॥
एते त्वामभिषिञ्चन्तु समेता वसुधाधिप ॥ 119 ॥
2.5.m: mind, intellect, the self, and the unmanifest, O lord of the earth— / may these, assembled together, consecrate you, O ruler of the earth!

2.5.s:
rukmabhaumaḥ śilābhaumaḥ pātālo nīlamṛttikaḥ ..
pīto raktakṣitiścaiva śvetabhaumastathaiva ca .. 120 ..
2.5.d:
रुक्मभौमः शिलाभौमः पातालो नीलमृत्तिकः ॥
पीतो रक्तक्षितिश्चैव श्वेतभौमस्तथैव च ॥ 120 ॥
2.5.m: The golden-soiled [underworld], the stone-soiled, the netherworld with black soil, / the yellow-soiled, the red-earthed, and the white-soiled underworld;

2.5.s:
ete tvāmabhiṣiñcantu vijayāya mahīpate ..
bhūloko'tha bhuvarlokaḥ svarloko'tha mahajjanaḥ .. 121 ..
2.5.d:
एते त्वामभिषिञ्चन्तु विजयाय महीपते ॥
भूलोकोऽथ भुवर्लोकः स्वर्लोकोऽथ महज्जनः ॥ 121 ॥
2.5.m: may these consecrate you for victory, O lord of the earth! / The earth-world, then the atmosphere, the heaven-world, and the Maharloka, Janaloka,

2.5.s:
tapaḥ satyaśca rājendra vijayāya bhavantu te ..
jambūśākakuśakrauñcāḥ śālmalidvīpa eva ca .. 122 ..
2.5.d:
तपः सत्यश्च राजेन्द्र विजयाय भवन्तु ते ॥
जम्बूशाककुशक्रौञ्चाः शाल्मलिद्वीप एव च ॥ 122 ॥
2.5.m: Tapoloka, and Satyaloka, O king of kings, may they be for your victory! / Jambu, Śāka, Kuśa, Krauñca, and Śālmalidvīpa,

2.5.s:
gomedhaḥ puṣkaraścaiva svasāmyaṃ pradiśantu te ..
uttarāḥ kuravaḥ puṇyā ramyā hairaṇvatastathā .. 123 ..
2.5.d:
गोमेधः पुष्करश्चैव स्वसाम्यं प्रदिशन्तु ते ॥
उत्तराः कुरवः पुण्या रम्या हैरण्वतस्तथा ॥ 123 ॥
2.5.m: Gomedha, and Puṣkara—may they bestow their mastery upon you! / The holy Northern Kurus, Ramyaka, and Hiraṇmaya,

2.5.s:
bhadrāśvaḥ ketumālaśca varṣaścaiva ilāvṛtaḥ ..
harivarṣaḥ kiṃpuruṣo varṣo bhāratasaṃjñikaḥ .. 124..
2.5.d:
भद्राश्वः केतुमालश्च वर्षश्चैव इलावृतः ॥
हरिवर्षः किंपुरुषो वर्षो भारतसंज्ञिकः ॥ 124॥
2.5.m: Bhadrāśva, Ketumāla, and the continent of Ilāvṛta, / Harivarṣa, Kiṃpuruṣa, and the continent named Bhārata—

2.5.s:
ete tvāmabhiṣiñcantu sametya vasudhādhipa ..
indradvīpaḥ kaśeruśca tāmravarṇo gabhastimān .. 125 ..
2.5.d:
एते त्वामभिषिञ्चन्तु समेत्य वसुधाधिप ॥
इन्द्रद्वीपः कशेरुश्च ताम्रवर्णो गभस्तिमान् ॥ 125 ॥
2.5.m: may these, coming together, consecrate you, O lord of the earth! / Indradvīpa, Kaśeru, Tāmravarṇa, Gabhastimat,

2.5.s:
nāgadvīpastathā saumyo gāndharvo vāruṇastathā ..
ayaṃ caruvasasteṣāṃ svasāmyaṃ pradiśantu te .. 126 ..
2.5.d:
नागद्वीपस्तथा सौम्यो गान्धर्वो वारुणस्तथा ॥
अयं चरुवसस्तेषां स्वसाम्यं प्रदिशन्तु ते ॥ 126 ॥
2.5.m: Nāgadvīpa, Saumya, Gāndharva, and Vāruṇa, / and this Caruva of theirs—may they bestow their mastery upon you!

2.5.s:
himavānhemakūṭaśca niṣadho nīlaparvataḥ ..
śvetaśca śṛṅgavānmerurmālyavāngandhamādanaḥ ..127 ..
2.5.d:
हिमवान्हेमकूटश्च निषधो नीलपर्वतः ॥
श्वेतश्च शृङ्गवान्मेरुर्माल्यवान्गन्धमादनः ॥127 ॥
2.5.m: Himavat, Hemakūṭa, Niṣadha, the blue mountain Nīla, / Śveta, Śṛṅgavat, Meru, Mālyavat, and Gandhamādana;

2.5.s:
mahendro malayaḥ sahyaḥ śuktimānṛkṣavāṃstathā ..
vindhyaśca pāriyātraśca sarva eva mahīdharāḥ .. 128 ..
2.5.d:
महेन्द्रो मलयः सह्यः शुक्तिमानृक्षवांस्तथा ॥
विन्ध्यश्च पारियात्रश्च सर्व एव महीधराः ॥ 128 ॥
2.5.m: Mahendra, Malaya, Sahya, Śuktimat, and Ṛkṣavat, / Vindhya, and Pāriyātra, indeed all the mountains—

2.5.s:
samāgamyābhiṣiñcantu tvāmadya vasudhādhipa! ..
ṛgvedo'tha yajurvedaḥ sāmavedastathaiva ca .. 129 ..
2.5.d:
समागम्याभिषिञ्चन्तु त्वामद्य वसुधाधिप! ॥
ऋग्वेदोऽथ यजुर्वेदः सामवेदस्तथैव च ॥ 129 ॥
2.5.m: may they assemble and consecrate you today, O lord of the earth! / The Ṛgveda, then the Yajurveda, and likewise the Sāmaveda,

2.5.s:
atharvavedo vedāstvāmabhiṣiñcantu pārthiva ..
itihāso dhanurvedo gandharvaścāyussaṃjñitaḥ .. 130 ..
2.5.d:
अथर्ववेदो वेदास्त्वामभिषिञ्चन्तु पार्थिव ॥
इतिहासो धनुर्वेदो गन्धर्वश्चायुस्संज्ञितः ॥ 130 ॥
2.5.m: and the Atharvaveda: may the Vedas consecrate you, O king! / The Itihāsa, the Dhanurveda, the Gandharvaveda, and that named Āyus [Āyurveda],

2.5.s:
vedopavedāśca tathā vijayāya bhavantu te ..
śikṣā kalpo vyākaraṇaṃ niruktaṃ jyotiṣāṅgatiḥ .. 131 ..
2.5.d:
वेदोपवेदाश्च तथा विजयाय भवन्तु ते ॥
शिक्षा कल्पो व्याकरणं निरुक्तं ज्योतिषाङ्गतिः ॥ 131 ॥
2.5.m: the Vedas and secondary Vedas: may they be for your victory! / Phonetics, ritual procedure, grammar, etymology, the course of astronomy,

2.5.s:
chandovicitiṣaṣṭhāni vijayaṃ pradiśantu te ..
aṅgāni vedāścatvāro mīmāṃsā nyāyavistaraḥ .. 132 ..
2.5.d:
छन्दोविचितिषष्ठानि विजयं प्रदिशन्तु ते ॥
अङ्गानि वेदाश्चत्वारो मीमांसा न्यायविस्तरः ॥ 132 ॥
2.5.m: and metrics as the sixth [ancillary science]: may they grant you victory! / The limbs [of the Veda], the four Vedas, Mīmāṃsā, the extent of Nyāya,

2.5.s:
dharmaśāstraṃ purāṇañca vidyā etāścaturdaśa ..
sāṃkhyayogaḥ pañcarātraṃ vedāḥ pāśupataṃ tathā .. 133 ..
2.5.d:
धर्मशास्त्रं पुराणञ्च विद्या एताश्चतुर्दश ॥
सांख्ययोगः पञ्चरात्रं वेदाः पाशुपतं तथा ॥ 133 ॥
2.5.m: Dharmaśāstra, and the Purāṇa—these fourteen branches of learning, / Sāṃkhya-Yoga, Pāñcarātra, the Vedas, and Pāśupata;

2.5.s:
kṛtānnapañcakaṃ hyetacchāstrāṇi vividhāni ca ..
gāyatrī pāpaśamanī durgā devī mahāśivā .. 134 ..
2.5.d:
कृतान्नपञ्चकं ह्येतच्छास्त्राणि विविधानि च ॥
गायत्री पापशमनी दुर्गा देवी महाशिवा ॥ 134 ॥
2.5.m: these indeed are the established quintet, and the diverse treatises; / Gāyatrī, remover of sin, goddess Durgā, Mahāśivā,

2.5.s:
gandhārī ca tathā vidyā vijayaṃ pradiśantu te ..
devadānavagandharvayakṣarākṣasapannagāḥ .. 135 ..
2.5.d:
गन्धारी च तथा विद्या विजयं प्रदिशन्तु ते ॥
देवदानवगन्धर्वयक्षराक्षसपन्नगाः ॥ 135 ॥
2.5.m: and the lore Gandhārī—may they grant you victory! / Gods, Dānavas, Gandharvas, Yakṣas, Rākṣasas, and serpents;

2.5.s:
ṛṣayo manavo gāvo devamātara eva ca ..
devapatnyo drumā nāgāḥ daityāścāpsarasāṅgaṇāḥ .. 136 ..
2.5.d:
ऋषयो मनवो गावो देवमातर एव च ॥
देवपत्न्यो द्रुमा नागाः दैत्याश्चाप्सरसाङ्गणाः ॥ 136 ॥
2.5.m: sages, Manus, cows, the mothers of the gods, / the wives of the gods, trees, serpents, Daityas, and hosts of Apsarases;

2.5.s:
śastrāṇi sarvaśāstrāṇi rājāno vāhanāni ca ..
auṣadhāni ca ratnāni kālasyāvayavāstathā ..137..
2.5.d:
शस्त्राणि सर्वशास्त्राणि राजानो वाहनानि च ॥
औषधानि च रत्नानि कालस्यावयवास्तथा ॥137॥
2.5.m: weapons, all treatises of learning, kings, vehicles, / medicinal herbs, jewels, and the divisions of time;

2.5.s:
sthānāni ca samastāni puṇyānyāyatanāni ca ..
jīmūtāni ca sarvāṇi tadvikārāśca ye tathā .. 138 ..
2.5.d:
स्थानानि च समस्तानि पुण्यान्यायतनानि च ॥
जीमूतानि च सर्वाणि तद्विकाराश्च ये तथा ॥ 138 ॥
2.5.m: all holy places, shrines, / all clouds, and their various transformations;

2.5.s:
uktāni cāpya'nuktāni vijayāya bhavantu te ..
lavaṇaḥ kṣāratoyaśca ghṛtamaṇḍodakastathā .. 139 ..
2.5.d:
उक्तानि चाप्यऽनुक्तानि विजयाय भवन्तु ते ॥
लवणः क्षारतोयश्च घृतमण्डोदकस्तथा ॥ 139 ॥
2.5.m: those mentioned and those unmentioned: may they be for your victory! / The salt ocean, the alkaline-watered ocean, and the clarified-butter-watered ocean,

2.5.s:
dadhimaṇḍodakaścaiva surodaśca narādhipa ..
tathaivekṣurasodaśca tathā svādūdakaśca yaḥ .. 140 ..
2.5.d:
दधिमण्डोदकश्चैव सुरोदश्च नराधिप ॥
तथैवेक्षुरसोदश्च तथा स्वादूदकश्च यः ॥ 140 ॥
2.5.m: the ocean of whey-waters, and the ocean of wine, O ruler of men, / and the ocean of sugarcane juice, and that which is of sweet water,

2.5.s:
garbhodaśca svatoyaistvāmabhiṣiñcantu pārthiva ..
catvārassāgarāścaiva svena toyena pārthiva .. 141 ..
2.5.d:
गर्भोदश्च स्वतोयैस्त्वामभिषिञ्चन्तु पार्थिव ॥
चत्वारस्सागराश्चैव स्वेन तोयेन पार्थिव ॥ 141 ॥
2.5.m: and the ocean of the cosmic womb—may they consecrate you with their waters, O king! / And the four oceans with their waters, O king,

2.5.s:
samāgamyābhiṣiñcantu vijayaṃ pradiśantu te ..
puṣkaraśca prayāgaśca prabhāso naimiṣastathā .. 142 ..
2.5.d:
समागम्याभिषिञ्चन्तु विजयं प्रदिशन्तु ते ॥
पुष्करश्च प्रयागश्च प्रभासो नैमिषस्तथा ॥ 142 ॥
2.5.m: may they assemble, consecrate you, and bestow victory upon you! / Puṣkara, Prayāga, Prabhāsa, and Naimiṣa,

2.5.s:
tathā brahmasaraḥ puṇyaṃ gayāśīrṣaṃ ca pārthiva ..
kālodako nandikuṇḍaḥ tathaivottaramānasaḥ .. 143 ..
2.5.d:
तथा ब्रह्मसरः पुण्यं गयाशीर्षं च पार्थिव ॥
कालोदको नन्दिकुण्डः तथैवोत्तरमानसः ॥ 143 ॥
2.5.m: and the holy Brahmasaras, and Gayāśīrṣa, O king; / Kālodaka, Nandikuṇḍa, and Uttaramānasa;

2.5.s:
svargamārgapradaścaiva tathā pañcanadaśca yaḥ ..
bhṛgutīrthaṃ caujasaśca tathaivāmarakaṇṭakaḥ..144..
2.5.d:
स्वर्गमार्गप्रदश्चैव तथा पञ्चनदश्च यः ॥
भृगुतीर्थं चौजसश्च तथैवामरकण्टकः॥144॥
2.5.m: the one that bestows the path to heaven, and the holy site Pañcanada; / Bhṛgutīrtha, Ojas, and Amarakaṇṭaka;

2.5.s:
āśramaḥ kālikāyāśca tṛṇabindostathāśramaḥ..
gopatīrthaṃ cāpatīrthaṃ vimalaḥ svarga eva ca..145..
2.5.d:
आश्रमः कालिकायाश्च तृणबिन्दोस्तथाश्रमः॥
गोपतीर्थं चापतीर्थं विमलः स्वर्ग एव च॥145॥
2.5.m: the hermitage of Kālikā, and the hermitage of Tṛṇabindu; / Gopatīrtha, Āpatīrtha, Vimala, and Svarga;

2.5.s:
jambūmārgaśca rājendra puṇyastaṇḍulikāśramaḥ ..
kapilasya tathā tīrthaṃ tīrthe vāṭikaṣaṇḍike .. 146 ..
2.5.d:
जम्बूमार्गश्च राजेन्द्र पुण्यस्तण्डुलिकाश्रमः ॥
कपिलस्य तथा तीर्थं तीर्थे वाटिकषण्डिके ॥ 146 ॥
2.5.m: Jambūmārga, O king of kings, the sacred Taṇḍulikāśrama; / the holy bathing place of Kapila, the two holy places at Vāṭikaṣaṇḍika;

2.5.s:
mahāsarastathāgastyaḥ kumārī tīrtha eva ca ..
gaṅgātīraḥ kuśāvarto bilvako nīlaparvataḥ .. 147 ..
2.5.d:
महासरस्तथागस्त्यः कुमारी तीर्थ एव च ॥
गङ्गातीरः कुशावर्तो बिल्वको नीलपर्वतः ॥ 147 ॥
2.5.m: Mahāsaras, Agastya, and the holy bathing place Kumārī; / the bank of the Gaṅgā, Kuśāvarta, Bilvaka, and Nīlaparvata;

2.5.s:
varāhaparvataścaiva tīrthaḥ kanakhalastathā ..
svargandhā vaśakumbhā ca tathā śākambharī ca yā .. 148 ..
2.5.d:
वराहपर्वतश्चैव तीर्थः कनखलस्तथा ॥
स्वर्गन्धा वशकुम्भा च तथा शाकम्भरी च या ॥ 148 ॥
2.5.m: Varāhaparvata, and the holy bathing place Kanakhala; / Svargandhā, Vaśakumbhā, and Śākambharī;

2.5.s: bhṛgutuṅgaḥ sakubjāmraḥ kapilasya tathāśramam .. 149 ..
2.5.d: भृगुतुङ्गः सकुब्जाम्रः कपिलस्य तथाश्रमम् ॥ 149 ॥
2.5.m: Bhṛgutuṅga, along with Kubjāmra, and the hermitage of Kapila;

2.5.s:
camasodbhedanaḥ puṇyastathā vinaśanaḥ śubhaḥ ..
ajatuṅgaśca somaśca ajogandhaśca pārthiva ..
kāliñjaraśca kedāro rudrakoṭistathaiva ca .. 150 ..
2.5.d:
चमसोद्भेदनः पुण्यस्तथा विनशनः शुभः ॥
अजतुङ्गश्च सोमश्च अजोगन्धश्च पार्थिव ॥
कालिञ्जरश्च केदारो रुद्रकोटिस्तथैव च ॥ 150 ॥
2.5.m: holy Camasodbhedana, and auspicious Vinaśana; / Ajatuṅga, Soma, and Ajogandha, O king; / Kāliñjara, Kedāra, and Rudrakoṭi;

2.5.s:
mahālagnaśca rājendra vadanāśrama eva ca ..
nandā ca sūryatīrthaṃ ca somatīrthaṃ śatakratoḥ .. 151 ..
2.5.d:
महालग्नश्च राजेन्द्र वदनाश्रम एव च ॥
नन्दा च सूर्यतीर्थं च सोमतीर्थं शतक्रतोः ॥ 151 ॥
2.5.m: Mahālagna, O king of kings, and Vadanāśrama; / Nandā, Sūryatīrtha, and the Somatīrtha of Śatakratu [Indra];

2.5.s:
aśvinorvaruṇasyāpi vāyovairśravaṇasya ca ..
brahmaṇaścaiva śarvasya yamasya cyavanasya ca ..152 ..
2.5.d:
अश्विनोर्वरुणस्यापि वायोवैर्श्रवणस्य च ॥
ब्रह्मणश्चैव शर्वस्य यमस्य च्यवनस्य च ॥152 ॥
2.5.m: [the holy bathing places] of the Aśvins, of Varuṇa, of Vāyu, of Vaiśravaṇa, / of Brahmā, of Śarva, of Yama, and of Cyavana;

2.5.s:
virūpākṣasya dharmasya tathā cāpsarasāṃ nṛpa ..
ṛṣīṇāṃ ca vasūnāṃ ca sādhyānāṃ marutāṃ tathā .. 153 ..
2.5.d:
विरूपाक्षस्य धर्मस्य तथा चाप्सरसां नृप ॥
ऋषीणां च वसूनां च साध्यानां मरुतां तथा ॥ 153 ॥
2.5.m: of Virūpākṣa, of Dharma, and of the Apsarases, O king; / of the ṛṣis, of the Vasus, of the Sādhyas, and of the Maruts;

2.5.s:
ādityānāṃ ca rudrāṇāṃ tathā cāṅgirasāṃ nṛpa ..
viśvedevabhṛgūṇāṃ ca gandharvāṇāṃ ca mānada .. 154 ..
2.5.d:
आदित्यानां च रुद्राणां तथा चाङ्गिरसां नृप ॥
विश्वेदेवभृगूणां च गन्धर्वाणां च मानद ॥ 154 ॥
2.5.m: of the Ādityas, of the Rudras, and of the Āṅgirases, O king; / of the Viśvedevas, of the Bhṛgus, and of the Gandharvas, O bestower of honor;

2.5.s:
plakṣaprasravaṇaścaiva suṣeṇaśca narādhipa ..
śāligrāmasaraścaiva vārāho vāmanastathā .. 155 ..
2.5.d:
प्लक्षप्रस्रवणश्चैव सुषेणश्च नराधिप ॥
शालिग्रामसरश्चैव वाराहो वामनस्तथा ॥ 155 ॥
2.5.m: Plakṣaprasravaṇa, and Suṣeṇa, O ruler of men; / the lake Śāligrāmasaras, Vārāha, and Vāmana;

2.5.s:
kāmaśramastrikūṭaśca citrakūṭastathaiva ca ..
saptarcaḥ kratusāraśca tathā viṣṇupadaṃ saraḥ .. 156 ..
2.5.d:
कामश्रमस्त्रिकूटश्च चित्रकूटस्तथैव च ॥
सप्तर्चः क्रतुसारश्च तथा विष्णुपदं सरः ॥ 156 ॥
2.5.m: Kāmāśrama, Trikūṭa, and Citrakūṭa; / Saptarca, Kratusāra, and the lake Viṣṇupada;

2.5.s:
kapilasya tathā tīrthaṃ vāsukestīrthameva ca ..
sindhūttamaṃ tapo dānaṃ tathā śūrpākaraḥ śubhaḥ .. 157 ..
2.5.d:
कपिलस्य तथा तीर्थं वासुकेस्तीर्थमेव च ॥
सिन्धूत्तमं तपो दानं तथा शूर्पाकरः शुभः ॥ 157 ॥
2.5.m: the holy bathing place of Kapila, and the holy bathing place of Vāsuki; / Sindhūttama, Tapodāna, and auspicious Śūrpākara;

2.5.s:
pauṇḍīrakaśca rājendra gaṅgāsāgarasaṅgamaḥ ..
sindhusāgarayoścaiva saṅgamaḥ sumanoharaḥ .. 158 ..
2.5.d:
पौण्डीरकश्च राजेन्द्र गङ्गासागरसङ्गमः ॥
सिन्धुसागरयोश्चैव सङ्गमः सुमनोहरः ॥ 158 ॥
2.5.m: Pauṇḍīraka, O king of kings, the confluence of the Gaṅgā and the ocean, / and the captivating confluence of the Sindhu and the ocean;

2.5.s:
tathā kundāvasundhaśca mānasaṃ ca mahatsaraḥ ..
tathā bindusaraḥ puṇyaṃ saraścācchodakaṃ tathā .. 159 ..
2.5.d:
तथा कुन्दावसुन्धश्च मानसं च महत्सरः ॥
तथा बिन्दुसरः पुण्यं सरश्चाच्छोदकं तथा ॥ 159 ॥
2.5.m: Kundāvasundha, the great lake Mānasa, / the holy lake Bindusaras, and Lake Acchodaka;

2.5.s:
dharmāraṇyaṃ phalgutīrthaṃ savimuktaṃ tathaiva ca ..
lauhityaśca tathā puṇyo badarīpāvanaḥ śivaḥ .. 160 ..
2.5.d:
धर्मारण्यं फल्गुतीर्थं सविमुक्तं तथैव च ॥
लौहित्यश्च तथा पुण्यो बदरीपावनः शिवः ॥ 160 ॥
2.5.m: Dharmāraṇya, Phalgutīrtha, along with Vimukta, / the holy Lauhitya, and auspicious Badarīpāvana.

2.5.s:
tīrthaṃ saptaṛṣīṇāṃ ca vahnitīrthaṃ ca pārthiva ..
vastrāpathastato meṣaśchāgaleśaśca pārthiva .. ..161..
2.5.d:
तीर्थं सप्तऋषीणां च वह्नितीर्थं च पार्थिव ॥
वस्त्रापथस्ततो मेषश्छागलेशश्च पार्थिव ॥ ॥161॥
2.5.m: And the holy site of the Seven Sages, and the holy site of Agni, O king, / then Vastrāpatha, Meṣa, and Chāgaleśa, O king,

2.5.s:
puṣpanyāsassakāmeśastīrtho haṃsapadastathā ..
aśvaśīrṣaḥ sa kṛṣṇākhyo maṇibhadrastathaiva ca .. 162 ..
2.5.d:
पुष्पन्यासस्सकामेशस्तीर्थो हंसपदस्तथा ॥
अश्वशीर्षः स कृष्णाख्यो मणिभद्रस्तथैव च ॥ 162 ॥
2.5.m: Puṣpanyāsa with Kāmeśa, and the holy site Haṃsapada, / Aśvaśīrṣa named Kṛṣṇa, and Maṇibhadra as well,

2.5.s:
devikā sindhumārgaśca svarṇabindustathaiva ca ..
āhalyakastathā tīrthastīrthaścairāvatastathā..163..
2.5.d:
देविका सिन्धुमार्गश्च स्वर्णबिन्दुस्तथैव च ॥
आहल्यकस्तथा तीर्थस्तीर्थश्चैरावतस्तथा॥163॥
2.5.m: Devikā, Sindhumārga, and Svarṇabindu as well, / and the holy site Āhalyaka, and the holy site Airāvata,

2.5.s:
airāvatisamudbhede tīrthaṃ bhogayaśastathā ..
karavīrāśramaścaiva nāgamodānikastathā..164..
2.5.d:
ऐरावतिसमुद्भेदे तीर्थं भोगयशस्तथा ॥
करवीराश्रमश्चैव नागमोदानिकस्तथा॥164॥
2.5.m: and at the confluence of the Airāvatī, the holy site Bhogayaśas, / and the hermitage of Karavīra, and Nāgamodānika,

2.5.s:
pāpamocanikaścaiva ṛṇamocanikastathā ..
udvejanastathā puṇyaḥ puṇyaśca hariśeśvaraḥ .. 165 ..
2.5.d:
पापमोचनिकश्चैव ऋणमोचनिकस्तथा ॥
उद्वेजनस्तथा पुण्यः पुण्यश्च हरिशेश्वरः ॥ 165 ॥
2.5.m: and Pāpamocanika, and Ṛṇamocanika, / and holy Udvejana, and holy Hariśeśvara,

2.5.s:
devabrahmasaraḥ puṇyaṃ sarpirdarvī ca pārthiva ..
ete cānye ca bahavaḥ puṇyasaṅkīrtanāḥ śubhāḥ .. 166 ..
2.5.d:
देवब्रह्मसरः पुण्यं सर्पिर्दर्वी च पार्थिव ॥
एते चान्ये च बहवः पुण्यसङ्कीर्तनाः शुभाः ॥ 166 ॥
2.5.m: the holy Devabrahmasaras, and Sarpirdarvī, O king: / may these and many other auspicious [sites], holy to recite,

2.5.s:
toyaistvāmabhiṣiñcantu sarvapātakanāśanaiḥ ..
gaṅgā mahānadī puṇyā hrādinī hlādinī tathā .. .. 167 ..
2.5.d:
तोयैस्त्वामभिषिञ्चन्तु सर्वपातकनाशनैः ॥
गङ्गा महानदी पुण्या ह्रादिनी ह्लादिनी तथा ॥ ॥ 167 ॥
2.5.m: consecrate you with waters that destroy all sins. / The holy Gaṅgā, the great river, and Hrādinī and Hlādinī,

2.5.s:
pāvanī ca tathā sītā cakṣuḥ sindhuśca narmadā ..
suprabhā kātarākṣī ca śithilā mānasī hradā .. 168 ..
2.5.d:
पावनी च तथा सीता चक्षुः सिन्धुश्च नर्मदा ॥
सुप्रभा कातराक्षी च शिथिला मानसी ह्रदा ॥ 168 ॥
2.5.m: and Pāvanī, Sītā, Cakṣu, Sindhu, and Narmadā, / Suprabhā, Kātarākṣī, Śithilā, Mānasī, Hradā,

2.5.s:
sarasvatyoghanādā ca suveṇurvimalodakā ..
siprā śoṇaḥ śatadruśca sarayūrgaṇḍakī tathā .. 169 ..
2.5.d:
सरस्वत्योघनादा च सुवेणुर्विमलोदका ॥
सिप्रा शोणः शतद्रुश्च सरयूर्गण्डकी तथा ॥ 169 ॥
2.5.m: Sarasvatī, Oghanādā, Suveṇu with pure waters, / Siprā, Śoṇa, Śatadru, Sarayū, and Gaṇḍakī,

2.5.s:
acchodā ca vipāśā ca candrabhāgā irāvatī ..
vitastā devikā rambhā pītā devahradā śivā .. 170 ..
2.5.d:
अच्छोदा च विपाशा च चन्द्रभागा इरावती ॥
वितस्ता देविका रम्भा पीता देवह्रदा शिवा ॥ 170 ॥
2.5.m: Acchodā, Vipāśā, Candrabhāgā, Irāvatī, / Vitastā, Devikā, Rambhā, Pītā, Devahradā, Śivā,

2.5.s:
tathaivekṣumatī puṇyā kauśikī yamunā tathā ..
gomatī dhūtapāpā ca bāhudā ca dṛṣadvatī .. 171 ..
2.5.d:
तथैवेक्षुमती पुण्या कौशिकी यमुना तथा ॥
गोमती धूतपापा च बाहुदा च दृषद्वती ॥ 171 ॥
2.5.m: and holy Ikṣumatī, Kauśikī, and Yamunā, / Gomatī, Dhūtapāpā, Bāhudā, and Dṛṣadvatī,

2.5.s:
niḥśīrā ca tṛtīyā ca lauhityaśca mahānadaḥ ..
vedasmṛtirvedasinī vetraghnī varadā tathā .. 172 ..
2.5.d:
निःशीरा च तृतीया च लौहित्यश्च महानदः ॥
वेदस्मृतिर्वेदसिनी वेत्रघ्नी वरदा तथा ॥ 172 ॥
2.5.m: Niḥśīrā, Tṛtīyā, and the great river Lauhitya, / Vedasmṛti, Vedasinī, Vetraghnī, and Varadā,

2.5.s:
varṇā mā candanā caiva bahunīrā kumudvatī ..
pārā carmaṇvatī rūpā vidiśā veṇuvatyapi .. 173 ..
2.5.d:
वर्णा मा चन्दना चैव बहुनीरा कुमुद्वती ॥
पारा चर्मण्वती रूपा विदिशा वेणुवत्यपि ॥ 173 ॥
2.5.m: Varṇā, Mā, Candanā, Bahunīrā, Kumudvatī, / Pārā, Carmaṇvatī, Rūpā, Vidiśā, and Veṇuvatī,

2.5.s:
avantī ca tathā kuntī surasā ca palāśinī ..
mandākinī daśārṇā ca citrakūṭā dṛṣadvatī .. .. 174 ..
2.5.d:
अवन्ती च तथा कुन्ती सुरसा च पलाशिनी ॥
मन्दाकिनी दशार्णा च चित्रकूटा दृषद्वती ॥ ॥ 174 ॥
2.5.m: Avantī, Kuntī, Surasā, Palāśinī, / Mandākinī, Daśārṇā, Citrakūṭā, Dṛṣadvatī,

2.5.s:
tamasā pippalā senī karamodā piśācikā ..
citropalā cittravarṇā maṃjulā vālukāvatī .. 175 ..
2.5.d:
तमसा पिप्पला सेनी करमोदा पिशाचिका ॥
चित्रोपला चित्त्रवर्णा मंजुला वालुकावती ॥ 175 ॥
2.5.m: Tamasā, Pippalā, Senī, Karamodā, Piśācikā, / Citropalā, Citravarṇā, Mañjulā, Vālukāvatī,

2.5.s:
śuktīmatī silī randhrā saṅkuṇātyayakāptataḥ ..
tāpī payoṣṇī nirvindhyā sitā ca niṣadhāvatī .. 176 ..
2.5.d:
शुक्तीमती सिली रन्ध्रा सङ्कुणात्ययकाप्ततः ॥
तापी पयोष्णी निर्विन्ध्या सिता च निषधावती ॥ 176 ॥
2.5.m: Śuktimatī, Silī, Randhrā, Saṅkuṇā, Saṃtāpā, / Tāpī, Payoṣṇī, Nirvindhyā, Sitā, Niṣadhāvatī,

2.5.s:
veṇā vaitaraṇī bhīmā carmā rāmā tathā kuhuḥ ..
toyā caiva mahāgaurī durgā matuśilā tathā .. 177 ..
2.5.d:
वेणा वैतरणी भीमा चर्मा रामा तथा कुहुः ॥
तोया चैव महागौरी दुर्गा मतुशिला तथा ॥ 177 ॥
2.5.m: Veṇā, Vaitaraṇī, Bhīmā, Carmā, Rāmā, and Kuhu, / Toyā, Mahāgaurī, Durgā, and Matuśilā,

2.5.s:
godāvarī bhīmarathī kṛṣṇā veṇā ca vaṃjulā ..
tuṅgabhadrā suprakārā bāhyā kāverireva ca .. 178 ..
2.5.d:
गोदावरी भीमरथी कृष्णा वेणा च वंजुला ॥
तुङ्गभद्रा सुप्रकारा बाह्या कावेरिरेव च ॥ 178 ॥
2.5.m: Godāvarī, Bhīmarathī, Kṛṣṇā, Veṇā, Vañjulā, / Tuṅgabhadrā, Suprakārā, Bāhyā, and Kāverī,

2.5.s:
kṛtamālā tāmraparṇī puṣpajā hyutpalāvatī ..
trisamā ṛṣikulyā ca pṛthukā tridivālayā .. 179 ..
2.5.d:
कृतमाला ताम्रपर्णी पुष्पजा ह्युत्पलावती ॥
त्रिसमा ऋषिकुल्या च पृथुका त्रिदिवालया ॥ 179 ॥
2.5.m: Kṛtamālā, Tāmraparṇī, Puṣpajā, Utpalāvatī, / Trisamā, Ṛṣikulyā, Pṛthukā, Tridivālayā,

2.5.s:
lāṅgūlinī vaṃśadharā sukumārā kulāvatī ..
ṛṣikā karivegā ca mandagā mandavāhinī .. 180 ..
2.5.d:
लाङ्गूलिनी वंशधरा सुकुमारा कुलावती ॥
ऋषिका करिवेगा च मन्दगा मन्दवाहिनी ॥ 180 ॥
2.5.m: Lāṅgūlinī, Vaṃśadharā, Sukumārā, Kulāvatī, / Ṛṣikā, Karivegā, Mandagā, Mandavāhinī,

2.5.s:
kṛpī darvī dayā vyomā paroṣṇī kolavāhinī ..
kampanā ca viśalyā ca karatoyāṃśuvāhinī .. 181 ..
2.5.d:
कृपी दर्वी दया व्योमा परोष्णी कोलवाहिनी ॥
कम्पना च विशल्या च करतोयांशुवाहिनी ॥ 181 ॥
2.5.m: Kṛpī, Darvī, Dayā, Vyomā, Paroṣṇī, Kolavāhinī, / Kampanā, Viśalyā, Karatoyā, Aṃśuvāhinī,

2.5.s:
tāmrāruṇā vetravatī gomatī cātha nadyapi ..
adriṇī trikasā caiva suprakārā hiraṇvatī .. 182 ..
2.5.d:
ताम्रारुणा वेत्रवती गोमती चाथ नद्यपि ॥
अद्रिणी त्रिकसा चैव सुप्रकारा हिरण्वती ॥ 182 ॥
2.5.m: Tāmrāruṇā, Vetravatī, Gomatī, and the river, / Adriṇī, Trikasā, Suprakārā, Hiraṇvatī,

2.5.s:
āpagā cālakā bhāsī sandhyā ca maḍavā nadī ..
nandā cālakanandā ca śuddhā ca vasuvāhinī .. 183 ..
2.5.d:
आपगा चालका भासी सन्ध्या च मडवा नदी ॥
नन्दा चालकनन्दा च शुद्धा च वसुवाहिनी ॥ 183 ॥
2.5.m: Āpagā, Alakā, Bhāsī, Sandhyā, and the river Maḍavā, / Nandā, Alakanandā, Śuddhā, and Vasuvāhinī—

2.5.s:
etāścānyāśca rājendra nadyastvāṃ vimalodakāḥ ..
sarvapāpapraśamanāssarvalokasya mātaraḥ ..
svatoyapūrṇaiḥ kalaśairabhiṣiñcantu pārthiva .. 184 ..
2.5.d:
एताश्चान्याश्च राजेन्द्र नद्यस्त्वां विमलोदकाः ॥
सर्वपापप्रशमनास्सर्वलोकस्य मातरः ॥
स्वतोयपूर्णैः कलशैरभिषिञ्चन्तु पार्थिव ॥ 184 ॥
2.5.m: these and other rivers with pure waters, O best of kings, / removers of all sin, mothers of the entire universe: / may they consecrate you, O king, with jars filled with their own waters.

2.5.s:
etairyathoktairnṛpa rājarājye dattābhiṣekaḥ pṛthivīṃ samagrām ..
sasāgarāṃ bhuṃkṣva ciraṃ ca jīva dharme ca te buddhiratīva cāstu..185..
2.23
puṣkara uvāca ..
mantrā ye kīrtitā rāma mayāsmiṃstava bhārgava ..
teṣāṃ saṃkīrtanaṃ dhanyaṃ sarvapāpapraṇāśanam ..1..
aiteṣāṃ kalyamutthāya yaḥ kuryātkīrtanaṃ naraḥ ..
sarvapāpavinirmuktaḥ svargalokamavāpnuyāt..2..
tiryagyoniṃ na gacchettu narakaṃ saṃkarāṇi ca ..
na ca duḥkhaṃ na ca bhayaṃ maraṇaṃ na sa ca muhyati .. 3 ..
eteṣāṃ ca namaskāraṃ yaḥ kuryātprayato naraḥ ...
na tasya tiṣṭhate pāpamabbinduriva puṣkare .. 4 ..
eteṣāṃ tarpaṇaṃ kṛtvā snātaḥ prayatamānasaḥ ..
mahāpātakayukto'pi tvacevāhirvimucyate .. 5 ..
eteṣāṃ puṣpadānena mahatīṃ śriyamaśnute ..
eteṣāṃ cārghyadānena pūjyo bhavati mānavaḥ .. 6 ..
2.5.d:
एतैर्यथोक्तैर्नृप राजराज्ये दत्ताभिषेकः पृथिवीं समग्राम् ॥
ससागरां भुंक्ष्व चिरं च जीव धर्मे च ते बुद्धिरतीव चास्तु॥185॥
2.23
पुष्कर उवाच ॥
मन्त्रा ये कीर्तिता राम मयास्मिंस्तव भार्गव ॥
तेषां संकीर्तनं धन्यं सर्वपापप्रणाशनम् ॥1॥
ऐतेषां कल्यमुत्थाय यः कुर्यात्कीर्तनं नरः ॥
सर्वपापविनिर्मुक्तः स्वर्गलोकमवाप्नुयात्॥2॥
तिर्यग्योनिं न गच्छेत्तु नरकं संकराणि च ॥
न च दुःखं न च भयं मरणं न स च मुह्यति ॥ 3 ॥
एतेषां च नमस्कारं यः कुर्यात्प्रयतो नरः ॥।
न तस्य तिष्ठते पापमब्बिन्दुरिव पुष्करे ॥ 4 ॥
एतेषां तर्पणं कृत्वा स्नातः प्रयतमानसः ॥
महापातकयुक्तोऽपि त्वचेवाहिर्विमुच्यते ॥ 5 ॥
एतेषां पुष्पदानेन महतीं श्रियमश्नुते ॥
एतेषां चार्घ्यदानेन पूज्यो भवति मानवः ॥ 6 ॥
2.5.m:
Having received royal consecration into sovereignty over kings by these [sites and waters] as proclaimed, O king, / enjoy the whole earth together with its oceans, live long, and may your mind be exceedingly devoted to dharma.
2.23
Puṣkara said: / The mantras which have been recited by me in this [chapter] for you, O Rāma, Bhārgava— / their recitation is auspicious and destroys all sins.
A man who, rising at dawn, recites these, / freed from all sins, attains the heavenly world.
He does not go to animal wombs, nor to hell, nor to mixed castes; / nor does he suffer grief, fear, or delusion at death.
And the restrained man who makes obeisance to these, / sin does not cling to him, like a drop of water on a lotus.
Having bathed, with a restrained mind, and having offered water to them, / even one burdened by a grave sin is released, like a snake from its slough.
By offering flowers to them, he attains great fortune; / by offering guest-water to them, a person becomes worthy of honor.

2.5.s:
eteṣāṃ dīpadānena bhrājante candravaddivi ..
eteṣāmāhutiṃ dattvā kāmānāpnoti puṣkalān .. 7 ..
naivedyaṃ ca baliṃ dattvā bhogānprāpnotyanuttamāna ..
etānuddiśya vipreṣu dattvā bhārgava bhojanam .. 8 ..
saṃtarpya dakṣiṇābhiśca tridivaṃ prāpnuyācciram ..
abhiṣekadine rājñāṃ puṣpasnāne tathaiva ca .. 9 ..
tathā saṃvatsaragranthau sarve pūjyā hitaiṣiṇā ..
yāni tīrthāni coktāni saritaśca samāsataḥ .. 10 ..
teṣāṃ gamena pūjyante ye'pi pātakino janāḥ ..
snānaṃ mahāphalaṃ teṣāṃ tapaḥ śrāddha kriyāstathā .. 11 ..
dānaṃ bahuphalaṃ proktaṃ darśanaṃ pāpanāśanam ..
kīrtanaṃ bhārgavaśreṣṭha na me cāsti vicāraṇā .. 12 ..
tīrtheṣvathaiteṣu bhṛgupradhāna snātā narā yānti narendra sadyaḥ..
tīrthāni gamyāni tataḥ prayatnātpuṇyāśca sarvāssaritaśca rāma.. 13 ..
2.5.d:
एतेषां दीपदानेन भ्राजन्ते चन्द्रवद्दिवि ॥
एतेषामाहुतिं दत्त्वा कामानाप्नोति पुष्कलान् ॥ 7 ॥
नैवेद्यं च बलिं दत्त्वा भोगान्प्राप्नोत्यनुत्तमान ॥
एतानुद्दिश्य विप्रेषु दत्त्वा भार्गव भोजनम् ॥ 8 ॥
संतर्प्य दक्षिणाभिश्च त्रिदिवं प्राप्नुयाच्चिरम् ॥
अभिषेकदिने राज्ञां पुष्पस्नाने तथैव च ॥ 9 ॥
तथा संवत्सरग्रन्थौ सर्वे पूज्या हितैषिणा ॥
यानि तीर्थानि चोक्तानि सरितश्च समासतः ॥ 10 ॥
तेषां गमेन पूज्यन्ते येऽपि पातकिनो जनाः ॥
स्नानं महाफलं तेषां तपः श्राद्ध क्रियास्तथा ॥ 11 ॥
दानं बहुफलं प्रोक्तं दर्शनं पापनाशनम् ॥
कीर्तनं भार्गवश्रेष्ठ न मे चास्ति विचारणा ॥ 12 ॥
तीर्थेष्वथैतेषु भृगुप्रधान स्नाता नरा यान्ति नरेन्द्र सद्यः॥
तीर्थानि गम्यानि ततः प्रयत्नात्पुण्याश्च सर्वास्सरितश्च राम॥ 13 ॥
2.5.m:
By offering lamps to them, they shine like the moon in heaven; / having given an oblation to them, he obtains abundant desires.
Having offered food-offerings and oblations, he attains peerless enjoyments. / Dedicating [it] to them, having given food to brahmins, O Bhārgava,
and having satisfied them with sacrificial fees, he attains heaven for a long time. / On the day of royal consecration of kings, and at the flower-bath as well,
and on the knot of the year, all should be worshiped by one seeking well-being. / And whichever holy sites and rivers have been stated in brief,
by visiting them, even sinful people are purified. / Bathing in them brings great fruit, as do austerity, ancestor rites, and rituals.
Giving [gifts there] is said to bear great fruit; seeing them destroys sin; / [and so does] reciting [their names], O best of the Bhṛgus—there is no doubt in my mind.
Then, having bathed in these holy sites, O foremost of the Bhṛgus, men immediately attain [the status of] a king of men. / Therefore, with diligence, holy sites are to be visited, and all the holy rivers, O Rāma.

॥ राम उवाच ॥ ॥
राज्ञोऽभिषिक्तमात्रस्य किन्नु कृत्यतमं भवेत् ॥
एतन्मे सर्वमाचक्ष्व सर्वं वेत्ति यतो भवान् ॥ 1 ॥
॥ पुष्कर उवाच ॥ -
अभिषेकार्द्रशिरसा राज्ञा राजीवलोचन ॥
सहायवरणं कार्यं तत्र राज्यं प्रतिष्ठितम् ॥ 2 ॥
यदप्यल्पतरं कर्म तदथैकेन दुष्करम् ॥
पुरुषेणासहायेन किन्नु राज्यं महत्पदम् ॥ 3॥
तस्मात्सहायान्वरयेत्कुलीनान्नृपतिः स्वयम् ॥
शूरानुत्तमजातीयान्बलयुक्ताञ्छ्रुतान्वितान् ॥ 4 ॥
रूपसत्वगुणौदार्यसंयुक्तान्क्षमया युतान्॥
क्लेशक्षमान्महोत्साहान्धर्मज्ञांश्च प्रियंवदान् ॥ 5 ॥
हितोपदेशिकान्प्राज्ञान्स्वामिभक्तान्यशोर्थिनः ॥
एवं विधान्सहायांस्तु शुभ कर्मणि योजयेत् ॥ 6 ॥
गुणहीनानपि तथा विज्ञाय नृपतिः स्वयम् ॥
कर्मस्वेव नियुञ्जीत यथायोग्येषु भार्गव ॥ 7 ॥
2.5.m:
2.24
Rāma said: / What should be the very first duty of a king just consecrated? / Explain all this to me, since you know everything.
Puṣkara said: / With his head still wet from royal consecration, O lotus-eyed one, / the king must appoint assistants; [for] kingdom is established thereon.
Even an action that is rather small is difficult for one man / without assistance to perform; how then kingship, a great station?
Therefore, the king himself should choose assistants of noble birth, / heroic, of the highest caste, endowed with strength, and possessed of sacred learning,
endowed with beauty, character, excellence, and nobility, joined with patience, / capable of enduring hardship, filled with great enterprise, knowing dharma, and speaking kindly,
giving beneficial counsel, wise, devoted to their master, and desiring renown. / Such assistants he should employ in auspicious tasks.
Likewise, having recognized those who are devoid of virtues, the king himself / should assign them only to suitable duties, O descendant of Bhṛgu.

2.5.d:
कुलीनाः शीलसंपन्ना धनुर्वेदविशारदाः ॥
हस्तिशिक्षाश्वशिक्षासु कुशलाश्श्लक्ष्णभाषितैः ॥ 8 ॥
निमित्ते शकुनज्ञाने वित्तवैद्यचिकित्सके ॥
पुरुषान्तरविज्ञाने षाड्गुण्येन विनिश्चिताः ॥ 9 ॥
कृतज्ञाः कर्मणां शूरास्तथा क्लेशसहा ऋजुः ॥
व्यूहतत्त्वविधानज्ञः फल्गुसारविशेषवित् ॥ 10 ॥
राज्ञां सेनापतिः कार्यो ब्राह्मणः क्षत्रियोऽथवा ॥
प्रांशुः सुरूपो दक्षश्च प्रियवादी न चोद्धतः ॥ 11 ॥
चित्तग्राहश्च सर्वेषां प्रतीहारो विधीयते ॥
यथोक्तवादी धूर्त्तः स्याद्देशभाषाविशारदः ॥ 12 ॥
शाब्दः क्लेशसहो वाग्मी देशकालविभाषिता ॥
विज्ञाय देशं कालं वा हितं यत्स्यान्महीक्षितः ॥ 13 ॥
वक्तापि तस्यः यः काले स दूतो नृपतिर्भवेत् ॥
प्रांशवो व्यायताः शूरा दृढभक्ता निराकुलाः ॥ 14 ॥
राज्ञा तु रक्षिणः कार्यास्तदा क्लेशसहा हिताः ॥
अहार्याश्चानृशंसाश्च दृढभक्ताश्च पार्थिवे ॥ 15 ॥
2.5.m:
Of noble birth, accomplished in virtue, skilled in the science of archery, / proficient in training elephants and horses, gentle in their speech,
skilled in portents and the knowledge of omens, in finance, medicine, and healing, / in discerning the differences among men, and resolved in the sixfold policy,
grateful, heroic in action, patient of hardship, upright, / knowing the rules of troop-array tactics, distinguishing the valueless from the substantial—
a commander-in-chief should be appointed by kings, either a brahmin or a kṣatriya. / Tall, handsome, capable, sweet-spoken, and not arrogant,
and winning the hearts of all—such is ordained as the doorkeeper. / Speaking as instructed, astute, skilled in the languages of the regions,
learned in grammar, capable of enduring hardship, eloquent, speaking according to place and time, / understanding the place or time and whatever is advantageous for the ruler of the earth,
and speaking it out at the proper time—he should be the king's envoy. / Tall, well-built, heroic, firmly devoted, calm,
patient of hardship, beneficial, incorruptible, not cruel, / and firmly devoted to the king—such should be appointed by the king as guards.

ताम्बूलधारी भवति नारी चाप्यथ तद्गुणा ॥
षाड्गुण्यविधि तत्त्वज्ञो देशभाषाविशारदः ॥ 16 ॥
सन्धिविग्रहकः कार्यो राज्ञा नयविशारदः ॥

सुरूपस्तरुणः शूरो दृढभक्तः कुलोचितः ॥ 18 ॥
शूरः क्लेशसहश्चैव खड्गधारी प्रकीर्तितः ॥
शूरश्च बहुयुक्तश्च गजाश्वरथकोविदः ॥ 19 ॥
कोशधारी भवेद्राज्ञः सदा क्लेशसहश्च यः ॥
निमित्तशकुनज्ञानहयशिक्षाविशारदः ॥20 ॥
हयायुर्वेदतत्त्वज्ञो भूमिभागविशेषवित् ॥
बलाबलज्ञो रथिनां स्थिरदृष्टिर्विशारदः ॥ 23 ॥
शूरश्च कृतविद्यश्च सारथिः परिकीर्तितः ॥
अनाहार्यः शुचिर्दक्षः चिकित्सकवचोरतः ॥ 22 ॥
सूदशास्त्रविधानाज्ञः सूदाध्यक्षः प्रशस्यते ॥
सूदशास्त्रविधानज्ञाः पराभेद्याः कुलोद्गताः ॥ 23 ॥
2.5.m:
A woman endowed with these same qualities may also be the betel-bearer. / Knowing the essence of the rules of the sixfold policy, skilled in the languages of the regions,
expert in statecraft—such a person the king should appoint as minister of peace and war. / Knowing income and expenditure, knowing the ways of the world, skilled in the products of the realm,
knowing what has been done and left undone by servants, a competent protector should be understood [as the superintendent of works]. / Handsome, young, heroic, firmly devoted, suitable to his lineage,
heroic, and capable of enduring hardship—such a one is praised as the sword-bearer. / Heroic, endowed with great [strength], and skilled in elephants, horses, and chariots,
and always capable of enduring hardship—he should be the king's treasurer. / Skilled in portents, knowledge of omens, and horse-training,
knowing the essence of the medical lore of horses, distinguishing the varieties of terrain, / knowing the strength and weakness of chariot-warriors, steady-sighted, proficient,
heroic, and educated—such is proclaimed as the charioteer. / Incorruptible, pure, capable, devoted to the physician's words,
knowing the rules of the culinary science—such is commended as the superintendent of the kitchen. / Knowing the rules of the culinary science, unbribable by enemies, born of good family,

सर्वे महानसे कार्या नीचकेशनखा जनाः ॥
समः शत्रौ च मित्रे च धर्मशास्त्रविशारदः ॥ 24 ॥
विप्रमुख्यः कुलीनश्च धर्माधिकरणो भवेत् ॥
कार्यास्तथाविधास्तत्र द्विजमुख्याः सभासदः॥25॥
सर्वदेशाक्षराभिज्ञाः सर्वशास्त्रविशारदाः ॥
लेखकाः कथिता राम सर्वाधिकरणेषु वै॥26॥
शीर्षोपेतान्सुसंपूर्णान्समद्रोणीगतान्समान् ॥
अक्षरान्विलिखेद्यस्तु लेखकः स वरः स्मृतः ॥ 27 ॥
उपायवाक्यकुशलः सर्वशास्त्रविशारदः ॥
बह्वर्थवक्ता चाल्पेन लेखकः स्याद्भृगूत्तम ॥ 28 ॥
पुरुषान्तरतत्त्वज्ञाः प्रांशवश्चाप्यलोलुपाः ॥
धर्माधिकरणे कार्या जनाह्वानकरा नराः ॥ 29॥
एवंविधास्तथा कार्या राज्ञो दौवारिका जनाः ॥
लोहवस्त्रादिधातूनां रत्नानां च विभागवित् ॥30॥
विज्ञाता फल्गुसाराणां त्वनाहार्यः शुचिस्सदा ॥
निपुणश्चाप्रमत्तश्च धनाध्यक्षः प्रकीर्तितः ॥ 31 ॥
2.5.m:
all people employed in the kitchen should have cut hair and nails. / Impartial toward enemy and friend, skilled in the legal codes,
an eminent and high-born brahmin should be the judge; / and eminent twice-born men of such kind should be made assessors of the court.
Familiar with the scripts of all regions, proficient in all branches of learning— / such scribes are prescribed, O Rāma, in all judicial tribunals.
One who writes letters with proper headings, fully formed, aligned straight, and even— / such a scribe is held to be the best.
Skilled in diplomatic speech, proficient in all treatises, / stating much meaning with few words—such should be the scribe, O foremost of the Bhṛgus.
Knowing the essential nature of different men, tall, and free from greed— / such men should be employed in the judicial court as summoners of people.
People of such kind should likewise be appointed as the king's doorkeepers. / Knowing the classification of metals, cloth, and gems,
a discerner of the worthless and the valuable, ever incorruptible and pure, / skillful and vigilant—such is declared as the treasurer.

2.5.d:
आयद्वारेषु सर्वेषु धनाध्यक्षसमा नराः ॥
व्ययद्वारेषु सर्वेषु कर्तव्याः पृथिवीक्षिता ॥ 32 ॥
परं पारं गतो यः स्यादष्टाङ्गेषु चिकित्सिते ॥
अनाहार्यस्स वैद्यः स्याद्धर्मात्मा च कुलोद्गतः ॥ 33 ॥
प्राणाचार्यस्स विज्ञेयो वचनं तस्य भूभुजा ॥
राम स्नेहात्सदा कार्यं यथा कार्यं पृथग्जनैः ॥ 34 ॥
हस्तिशिक्षाविधानज्ञो वनजातिविशारदः ॥
क्लेशक्षमस्तथा राज्ञो गजाध्यक्षः प्रशस्यते ॥ 35 ॥
एतैरेव गुणैर्युक्तो स्वाधीनश्च विशेषतः ॥
गजारोहो नरेन्द्रस्य सर्वकर्मसु शस्यते ॥ 36 ॥
हयशिक्षाविधानज्ञ स्तच्चिकित्सितपारगः ॥
अश्वाध्यक्षो महीभर्त्तुः स्वासनश्च प्रशस्यते ॥ 37 ॥
अनाहार्यश्च शूरश्च तथा प्राज्ञः कुलोद्गतः ॥
दुर्गाध्यक्षः स्मृतो राम उद्युक्तः सर्वकर्मसु ॥ 38 ॥
2.5.m:
At all avenues of revenue and at all avenues of expenditure, / men equal to the treasurer should be appointed by the ruler of the earth.
One who has reached the further shore in the eight-limbed science of medicine, / incorruptible, righteous, and born of good family—such should be the physician.
He should be known as the teacher of life; his word should always be obeyed / out of affection by the earth-protector, O Rāma, just as it is by ordinary men.
Knowing the rules of elephant-training, expert in forest species, / and capable of enduring hardship—such a one is commended as the king's superintendent of elephants.
Endowed with these very qualities and especially self-controlled, / the king's elephant-rider is commended in all operations.
Knowing the rules of horse-training, having mastered their medical treatment, / and having a firm seat—such is commended as the earth-lord's superintendent of horses.
Incorruptible, heroic, wise, born of good family, / and zealous in all tasks—such is remembered, O Rāma, as the superintendent of the fort.

2.5.d:
वास्तुविद्याविधानज्ञो लग्नहस्तो जितश्रमः ॥
दीर्घदर्शी च शूरश्च स्थपतिः परिकीर्तितः ॥ 39 ॥
यन्त्रमुक्ते पाणिमुक्ते अमुक्ते मुक्तधारिते ॥
अस्त्राचार्यो नियुद्धे च कुशलश्च तथेष्यते ॥ 40 ॥
पञ्चाशदधिका नार्यः पुरुषाः सप्ततिस्तथा ॥
अन्तःपुरचराः कार्या राज्ञा सर्वेषु कर्मसु ॥ 41 ॥
स्थविरा जातितत्त्वज्ञाः सततं प्रतिजाग्रतः ॥
राज्ञः स्यादायुधागारे दक्षः कर्मसु चोद्यतः ॥ 42 ॥
कर्माण्यपरिमेयानि राज्ञां भृगुकुलोद्वह ॥
उत्तमाधममध्यानि बुद्ध्वा कर्माणि पार्थिव ॥ 43 ॥
उत्तमाधममध्याम्̐स्तु पुरुषान्विनियोजयेत ॥
न कर्मणि विपर्यासाद्राजा नाशमवाप्नुयात् ॥ 44 ॥
नियुक्तपुरुषे भक्तिं श्रुतं शौर्यं बलं कुलम् ॥
ज्ञात्वा वृत्तिर्विधातव्या पुरुषाणां महीक्षिता ॥ 45 ॥
पुरुषान्तरविज्ञाने तत्त्वमात्रनिबन्धनाः ॥
नरेन्द्रलक्ष्या धर्मज्ञास्तत्रायत्तो भवेन्नृपः ॥46॥
2.5.m:
Knowing the rules of architecture, sure-handed, having overcome weariness, / far-sighted, and courageous—such is proclaimed as the master architect.
In weapons discharged by machines, hurled by hand, retained, and hurled-and-retained, / and in hand-to-hand combat, a master of weapons is desired to be skilled.
Women over fifty years of age, and men over seventy, / should be employed by the king in all tasks inside the inner apartments.
Elderly, knowing the true nature of their classes, and continually vigilant— / in the king's armory there should be one who is capable and zealous in duties.
The duties of kings are immeasurable, O descendant of the Bhṛgu race. / Having understood duties as high, low, and middling, O ruler of the earth,
he should assign men who are high, low, and middling [accordingly]. / The king would not meet with ruin through confusion of tasks.
Having recognized in an appointed man his devotion, learning, valor, strength, and family, / a livelihood should be established for his men by the ruler of the earth.
When discerning the differences between men, whose reliance is upon true reality alone, / men possessing the royal marks and knowing dharma—on them the king should depend.

2.5.d:
स्वभृत्याश्च तथा पुष्टास्सततं प्रतिमानिताः ॥
राज्ञा सहायाः कर्तव्याः पृथिवीं जेतुमिच्छता ॥47॥
यथार्हं चाथ सुभृतान्राजा कर्मसु योजयेत ॥
धर्मिष्ठान्धर्मकार्येषु शूरान्संग्रामकर्मणि ॥ 48 ॥
निपुणानर्थकृत्येषु सर्वत्र च तथा शुचीन् ॥
स्त्रीषु षण्ढान्नियुञ्जीत तीक्ष्णान्दारुणकर्मसु ॥49॥
धर्मे चार्थे च कामे च भये च भृगुनन्दन ॥
राजा यथार्हं कुर्यात्तान्ह्युपधाभिः परीक्षितान् ॥ 50 ॥
समतीतो यथार्हायां कुर्याद्धस्तिवने चरान् ॥
उत्पादान्वेषणं यत्तानध्यक्षाम्̐स्तत्र कारयेत् ॥ 51 ॥
एवमादीनि कर्माणि यत्नैः कार्याणि भार्गव ॥
सर्वथा नेष्यते राज्ञस्तीक्ष्णोपकरणक्षयः ॥ 52 ॥
पापसाध्यानि कर्माणि यानि राज्ञां भृगूत्तम ॥
सन्तस्तानि न कुर्वन्ति तस्मात्तान्बिभृयान्नृपः ॥ 53 ॥
2.5.m:
Well-nourished servants, continually honored, / should be made assistants by the king who wishes to conquer the earth.
And the king should employ the well-supported men in duties according to their merit: / the most righteous in matters of dharma, and heroes in the work of battle.
[He should assign] the skilled to financial duties, and likewise the pure everywhere. / He should assign eunuchs to women, and the fierce to cruel tasks.
In matters of dharma, wealth, pleasure, and fear, O son of Bhṛgu, / the king should suitably employ those who have been tested by secret tests.
Having passed [the tests], he should employ agents in the elephant-forest according to their suitability; / he should appoint superintendents there to carefully seek out whatever occurs.
Such tasks and others must be carried out with effort, O descendant of Bhṛgu. / By no means is the loss of harsh instruments desirable for a king.
Those deeds of kings that must be accomplished through sin, O foremost of the Bhṛgus— / good men do not do them; therefore the king must maintain these [fierce men].

2.5.d:
नेष्यते पृथिवीशानां तीक्ष्णोपकरणक्षयः ॥
यस्मिन्कर्मणि यस्य स्याद्विशेषेण च कौशलम् ॥ 54 ॥
तस्मिन्कर्मणि तं राजा परीक्ष्य विनियोजयेत् ॥
पितृपैतामहान्भृत्यान्सर्वकर्मसु योजयेत् ॥ 55 ॥
विना दायादकृत्येषु तत्र ते हि समासतः ॥
राजा दायादकृत्येषु परीक्ष्य स्वकृतान्नरान् ॥ 56 ॥
नियुञ्जीत महाभागः तस्य ते हितकारिणः ॥
परराजगृहान्प्राप्ताञ्जनसंग्रहकाम्यया ॥ 57 ॥
उष्टान्वाप्यथ वा दुष्टान्संश्रयेत प्रयत्नतः ॥
दुष्टं विज्ञाय विश्वासं न कुर्यात्तत्र भूमिपः ॥ 68 ॥
वृत्तिं तस्यापि वर्त्तेत जनसंग्रहकाम्यया ॥
राजा देशान्तरप्राप्तं पुरुषं पूजयेद्भृशम् ॥ 59 ॥
सहायं देशसंप्राप्तं बहुमानेन चिन्तयेत ॥
कामं भृत्यार्जनं राजा नैव कुर्याद्भृगूत्तम ॥ 60 ॥

2.5.d:
न वै वासं विभक्तं तु भृत्यं कुर्यात्कथञ्चन ॥
शस्त्रमग्निं विषं सर्पान्निस्त्रिंशमपि चैकतः ॥ 61 ॥
भृत्या मनुजशार्दूल कुभृत्याश्च तथैकतः ॥
तेषां चारेण विज्ञानं राज्ञा विज्ञाय नित्यशः ॥ 62 ॥
गुणिनां पूजनं कुर्यान्निर्गुणानां च शासनम् ॥
कथिताः सततं राम राजानश्चारचक्षुषः ॥ ॥ 63 ॥
स्वदेशे परदेशे च जातिशीलान्विचक्षणान् ॥
अनाहार्यान्क्लेशसहान्नियुञ्जीत सदा चरान् ॥ 64 ॥
जनस्याविततान्सौम्यांस्तथा ज्ञातान्परस्परम् ॥
वणिजो मन्त्रकुशलान्सांवत्सरचिकित्सितान् ॥ 65 ॥
तथा प्रव्रजिताकारान्राजा चारान्नियोजयेत ॥
नैकस्य राजा श्रद्दध्याच्चारस्यापि च भाषितम् ॥ 66 ॥
द्वयोस्संवादमाज्ञाय सन्दध्यान्नृपतिस्ततः ॥
परस्परस्याविदितौ यदि स्यातां न तावुभौ ॥ 67 ॥
2.5.m:
nor should he ever divide the quarters of his servants. / Weapon, fire, poison, serpents, and a sword on one side,
and bad servants on the other, O tiger among men! / Ever ascertaining their conduct by means of spies,
the king should honor the virtuous and punish the unprincipled. / Kings are perpetually declared to have spies as their eyes, O Rāma.
In one's own country and in foreign territory, he should always appoint as spies / men of good birth and character, discerning, incorruptible, and capable of enduring hardship,
not conspicuous to people, gentle, and unknown to one another: / merchants, those skilled in statecraft, astrologers, physicians,
and likewise in the guise of wandering ascetics the king should employ spies. / A king should not believe the report of a single spy.
Ascertaining the agreement of two, the king should then rely upon it, / provided that the two were not known to each other.

2.5.d:
तस्माद्राजा प्रयत्नेन गूढांश्चारान्प्रयोजयेत ॥
राज्यस्य मूलमेतावद्यद्राज्ञश्चारदृष्टिता ॥ 68 ॥
चाराणामपि यत्नेन राज्ञा कार्यं परीक्षणम् ॥
रागापरागौ भृत्यानां जनस्य च गुणागुणान् ॥ 69 ॥
शुभानामशुभानां च विज्ञानं राम कर्मणाम् ॥
सर्वं राज्ञां चरायत्तं तेष्वायत्तस्सदा भवेत् ॥ 70 ॥
कर्मणा केन मे लोके जनस्सर्वोऽनुरज्यते ॥
विरज्यते तथा केन विज्ञेयं तन्महीक्षिता ॥
विरागजननं सर्वं वर्जनीयं प्रयत्नतः ॥ 71 ॥
जनानुरागप्रभवो हि लक्ष्यो राज्ञां यतो भार्गववंशचन्द्र ॥
तस्मात्प्रयत्नेन नरेन्द्रमुख्यैः कार्योऽनुरागो भुवि मानवेषु ॥ 72 ॥
2.25
॥ पुष्कर उवाच॥
यथानुवर्तितव्यं स्याद्राम राजोपजीविभिः ॥
तथा ते कथयिष्यामि निबोध गदतो मम ॥ 1 ॥
2.5.m:
Therefore the king should diligently employ secret spies. / The root of the kingdom is just this: that the king has spies for his sight.
The king must also examine his spies with care. / The loyalty and disaffection of his servants, the merits and faults of the people,
and the discernment of good and bad deeds, O Rāma, / are all dependent upon spies for kings; he should always rely upon them.
"By what deed of mine are all people in the world pleased with me? / And by what do they become estranged?" This must be known by the ruler of the earth. / Everything that causes disaffection must be avoided with care.
For royal fortune arises from the affection of the people, O moon of the Bhārgava lineage; / therefore, foremost rulers of men must diligently cultivate affection among people on earth.
2.25 / Puṣkara said: / How royal dependents should conduct themselves, O Rāma, / that I shall tell you; listen as I speak.

2.5.d:
आज्ञा सर्वात्मना कार्या स्वशक्त्या भृगुनन्दन ॥
आक्षिप्य वचनं तस्य न वक्तव्यं तथा वचः ॥ 2 ॥
अनुकूलं प्रियं तस्य वक्तव्यं जनसन्निधौ ॥
रहोगतस्य वक्तव्यमप्रियं यद्धितं भवेत् ॥ 3 ॥
परार्थमथ वक्तव्यं स्वस्थे चेतसि भार्गव ॥
स्वास्थ्यं सुहृद्भिर्वक्तव्यं न स्वयं तु कथंचन ॥ 4 ॥
कार्यातिपातकं कार्यै रक्षितव्यं प्रयत्नतः ॥
न च हिंस्यधनं किञ्चिन्नियुक्तेन च कर्मणि ॥ 5 ॥
नोपेक्ष्यं तस्य मानं च तथा राज्ञा प्रियो भवेत् ॥
राज्ञश्च न तथा कार्यं वेशभाषितचेष्टितम् ॥6॥
राजलीला न कर्तव्या तद्दिष्टं च विवर्जयेत् ॥
राज्ञस्समाधिकौ वेशौ न तु कार्यौ विजानता ॥ 7 ॥
द्यूतादिषु तथैवास्य कौशलं तु प्रदर्शयेत् ॥
प्रदर्श्य कौशलं चास्य राजानं न विशेषयेत् ॥ 8 ॥
2.5.m:
A command must be carried out with all one's heart, to the best of one's ability, O son of Bhṛgu. / One must not speak words contradicting his words.
What is agreeable and pleasing to him should be spoken in public; / when he is in private, that which is beneficial, even if unpleasant, should be spoken.
On another's behalf, one should speak when his mind is at ease, O descendant of Bhṛgu. / One's own comfort should be spoken of by friends, but never by oneself.
Neglect of duty must be guarded against with effort through one's deeds, / and when appointed to a duty, one must not destroy any property.
His honor should not be disregarded; thus one becomes dear to the king. / One should not imitate the king's dress, speech, or gestures.
Royal sports must not be engaged in, and what is appointed for him must be avoided. / One who knows should not adopt dress that is equal or superior to the king's.
In gambling and the like, he should display his skill to him; / yet having displayed his skill, he should not surpass the king.

2.5.d:
अन्तःपुरधनाध्यक्षैर्वैरिदूतैर्निराकृतैः ॥
संसर्गं न व्रजेद्राम विना पार्थिवशासनम् ॥ 9 ॥
निम्नेहतां चावमानं तत्प्रयुक्तं च गोपयेत् ॥
यच्च गुह्यं भवेद्राज्ञस्तन्न लोके प्रकाशयेत् ॥ 10 ॥
नृपेण श्रावितं यत्स्याद्गुह्याद्गुह्यं भृगूत्तम ॥
न तत्संश्रावयेल्लोके तथा राज्ञः प्रियो भवेत् ॥ 11 ॥
आज्ञप्यमाने चान्यस्मिन्समुत्थाय त्वरान्वितः ॥
अहं किङ्करवाणीति वाच्यो राजा विजानता ॥ 12 ॥
कार्यावस्थां च विज्ञाय कार्यमेतत्तथा भवेत् ॥
सततं क्रियमाणेस्मिम्̐ल्लाघवं तु व्रजेद्बुधः ॥ 13 ॥
राज्ञः प्रियाणि वाक्यानि न चात्यर्थं पुनःपुनः ॥
न हास्यशीलश्च भवेन्न चापि भृकुटीमुखः॥ ॥ 14 ॥
नातिवक्ता न निर्वक्ता न च मात्सरिकस्तथा ॥
आत्मसम्भावितश्चैव न भवेत्तु कथञ्चन ॥ 15 ॥
2.5.m:
With superintendents of the inner quarters and of the treasury, with envoys of enemies, and with those who have been dismissed, / one must not associate, O Rāma, without the ruler's command.
He should conceal low desire and any disrespect directed at him; / and whatever is secret to the king, he should not disclose to the world.
What has been disclosed by the king as the secret of secrets, O foremost of the Bhṛgus, / he should not make known to the world; thus he will become dear to the king.
When another is being commanded, one who knows should rise with haste / and say to the king: "What may I do?"
Having recognized the state of the task, this duty should be performed thus. / If this is done constantly, the wise man would incur contempt.
One should not repeat words pleasing to the king excessively again and again. / One should not be given to laughter, nor should one have a frowning face.
He should not speak too much, nor be completely silent, nor be envious; / and by no means should he be self-conceited.

2.5.d:
दुष्कृतानि नरेन्द्रस्य न च संकीर्तयेत्क्वचित् ॥
वस्त्रं पत्रमलङ्कारं राज्ञा दत्तं तु धारयेत् ॥ 16 ॥
औदार्येण न तद्देयमन्यस्मिन्भूतिमिच्छता ॥
न चैवाध्यशनं राज्ञः स्वपनं चापि कारयेत् ॥ 17 ॥
नानिर्दिष्टे तथा द्वारे प्रविशेत कथञ्चन ॥
न च पश्येत राजानमयोग्यासु च भूमिषु ॥ 18 ॥
राज्ञस्तु दक्षिणे पार्श्वे वामे चोपविशेत्तदा ॥
पुरस्तात्तु यथा पश्चादासनं तु विगर्हितम्॥19॥
जृम्भा निष्ठीवनं कामं कोपं पर्यंकिकाश्रयम्॥
मुकुटं वातमुद्गारं तत्समीपे विवर्जयेत्॥
स्वयं तथा न कुर्वीत स्वगुणाख्यापनं बुधः॥
स्वगुणाख्यापने कुर्यात्परानेव प्रयोजकान्॥21॥
हृदयं निर्मलं कृत्वा परं भक्तिमुपाश्रितैः ॥
अनुजीविगणैर्भाव्यं नित्यं राज्ञामतन्द्रितैः ॥ 22 ॥
2.5.m:
One should never proclaim the misdeeds of the ruler of men. / One should wear the garment, badge of honor, and ornament given by the king;
it should not be given to another out of generosity by one who desires prosperity. / Nor should he interrupt the king while he is eating or sleeping.
One should never enter through an unauthorized door, / nor should one look upon the king in inappropriate places.
He should sit on the king's right side or on his left side; / but a seat in front or behind is condemned.
Yawning, spitting, desire, anger, leaning against a couch, / a crown, breaking wind, and belching should be avoided near him. / The wise man should likewise not proclaim his own virtues himself; / when proclaiming his own virtues, he should employ only others.
Having made their hearts pure and having resorted to supreme devotion, / the hosts of dependents of kings should always be unwearied.

2.5.d:
शाठ्यं लौल्यमपैशुन्यं नास्तिक्यं क्षुद्रतां तथा ॥
चापल्यं च परित्याज्यं नित्यं राजानुजीविना ॥ 23 ॥
श्रुतेन विद्याशिल्पैश्च संयोज्यात्मानमात्मना ॥
राजसेवां ततः कुर्याद्भूतये भीतिवर्धनः ॥ 24 ॥
नमस्कार्यास्सदा चास्य पुत्रवल्लभमन्त्रिणः ॥
सचिवैश्चास्य विश्वासं न तु कार्यं कथञ्चन ॥ 25 ॥
अपृष्टश्चास्य न ब्रूयात्कामं ब्रूयात्तथापदि ॥
हितं पथ्यं च वचनं हितैस्सह सुनिश्चितम् ॥ 26 ॥
चित्तं चैवास्य विज्ञेयं नित्यमेवानुजीविना ॥
भर्तुराराधनं कुर्याच्चित्तज्ञो मानवः सुखम् ॥ 27 ॥ ।
रागापरागौ चैवास्य विज्ञेयौ भूतिमिच्छता ॥
त्यजेद्विरक्तं नृपतिं रक्ताद्वृत्तिं तु कामयेत् ॥ 28 ॥
कर्मोपकारयोर्नाशं विपक्षाभ्युदयं तथा ॥
आशासंवर्धनं कृत्वा फलनाशं करोति च ॥ 29 ॥
2.5.m:
Deceit, greed, malice, atheism, meanness, / and fickleness should always be abandoned by the king's dependent.
Having joined himself by himself with sacred learning, sciences, and crafts, / increasing [others'] awe, he should then serve the king for prosperity.
His sons, favorites, and ministers should always be saluted by him, / but he should never place trust in his ministers.
Unasked, he should not speak to him, though he may speak at will in misfortune; / along with well-wishers, he should speak well-ascertained words that are beneficial and salutary.
And his mind must always be known by the dependent; / a man who knows [his lord's] mind pleases his master with ease.
One who desires prosperity should also know his affection and disaffection; / he should abandon an alienated king, but seek his livelihood from an affectionate one.
He causes the ruin of work and benefit, and likewise the rise of adversaries; / having raised expectations, he causes the ruin of the fruit;

2.5.d:
अकोपोपि प्रकोपाभः प्रसन्नोपि च निष्फलः ॥
वाक्यं समन्दं वदति वृत्तिच्छेदं करोति च ॥ ॥। 30 ॥
प्रवेशवाक्यानुदितौ न संभावयतीत्यथ ॥
आराधनासु सर्वासु सुप्तवच्च विचेष्टते ॥ 31 ॥
कथासु दोषैः क्षिपति वाक्यच्छेदं करोति च ॥
लक्ष्यते विमुखश्चैव गुणसङ्कीर्तने कृते ॥ 052 ॥
दृष्टिं क्षिपत्यथान्यत्र क्रियमाणे च कर्मणि ॥
विरक्तलक्षणं श्रुत्वा शृणु रक्तस्य लक्षणम् ॥ 33 ॥
दृष्ट्वा प्रसन्नो भवति वाक्यं गृह्णाति चादरात् ॥
कुशलादिपरिप्रश्ने संप्रयच्छति चासनम् ॥ 34 ॥
विविक्तदर्शने चास्य रहस्ये न च शङ्कते ॥
जायते हृष्टवदनः श्रुत्वा तस्य तु सङ्कथाम् ॥ 35 ॥
अप्रियाण्यपि वाक्यानि तदुक्तान्यभिनन्दति ॥
उपायनं च गृह्णाति स्तोकमप्यादरात्तथा ॥ 36 ॥

इति रक्तस्य कर्तव्या सेवा भृगुकुलोद्वह ॥
आपत्सु न त्यजेत्पूर्वं विरक्तमपि सेवितम्॥37॥
मित्रं न चापत्सु तथा न भृत्यं व्रजन्ति ये निर्गुणमप्रमेयम् ॥
प्रभुं विशेषेण च ते व्रजन्ति सुरेन्द्रधामासुरवृन्द जुष्टम् ॥ 38 ॥ ॥
2.5.m:
and during pauses in conversation he moves with a cheerful face. / Thus should service to an affectionate king be rendered, O scion of the Bhṛgu clan; / in misfortunes he should not abandon one previously served, even if alienated.
Those who do not abandon a friend, or likewise a servant, or especially an insignificant, / unmeasurable master in misfortunes, go to the abode of the lord of the gods, frequented by hosts of celestial maidens.

2.6.m: Puṣkara said: / A king accompanied by allies, having subdued his neighbors, should dwell in a region / with abundant grass and firewood, pleasant, and suitable for cattle;

2.6.s:
vaiśyaśūdrajanaprāyamanāhāryaṃ tathā paraiḥ ..
kiñcidbrāhmaṇasaṃyuktaṃ bahukarmakaraṃ tathā .. 2 ..

वैश्यशूद्रजनप्रायमनाहार्यं तथा परैः ॥
किञ्चिद्ब्राह्मणसंयुक्तं बहुकर्मकरं तथा ॥ 2 ॥
2.6.m: consisting mostly of vaiśyas and śūdras, incapable of being seized by others, / containing some brahmins, and possessing many laborers;

2.6.s:
adevamātṛkaṃ karmasvanuraktajanācitam ..
karairapīḍitaṃ cāpi bahupuṣpaṃ phalaṃ tathā .. 3 ..
2.6.d:
अदेवमातृकं कर्मस्वनुरक्तजनाचितम् ॥
करैरपीडितं चापि बहुपुष्पं फलं तथा ॥ 3 ॥
2.6.m: not watered by rain alone, filled with people devoted to their work, / unburdened by taxes, and possessing many flowers and fruits;

2.6.s:
agamyaṃ paracakrāṇāṃ tadvādasahamāpadi ..

2.6.d:
अगम्यं परचक्राणां तद्वादसहमापदि ॥
समदुःखसुखं राज्ञः सततं च प्रिये स्थितम् ॥ 4 ॥
2.6.m: inaccessible to enemy armies, enduring their assault in times of misfortune, / sharing the king's joys and sorrows, and continually devoted to what is dear [to him];

2.6.s:
sarīsṛpavihīnaṃ ca vyādhitaskaravarjitam ..
evaṃvidhaṃ yathālābhaṃ rājā viṣayamāvaseta .. 5 ..
