सरीसृपविहीनं च व्याधितस्करवर्जितम् ॥
एवंविधं यथालाभं राजा विषयमावसेत ॥ 5 ॥
2.6.m: and devoid of serpents, free from disease and thieves: / the king should inhabit such a territory according to availability.

2.6.s:
tatra durgaṃ nṛpaḥ kuryātṣaṇṇāmekatamaṃ budhaḥ ..
dhanvadurgaṃ mahīdurgaṃ naradurgaṃ tathaiva ca .. 6 ..
2.6.d:
तत्र दुर्गं नृपः कुर्यात्षण्णामेकतमं बुधः ॥
धन्वदुर्गं महीदुर्गं नरदुर्गं तथैव च ॥ 6 ॥
2.6.m: There the wise king should make a fortress, one of the six kinds: / a desert fortress, an earthen fortress, and a fortress garrisoned by men,

2.6.s:
vārkṣaṃ cevāṃbudurgaṃ ca giridurgaṃ ca bhārgava ..
sarveṣāmeva durgāṇāṃ giridurgaṃ praśasyate .. 7 ..
2.6.d:
वार्क्षं चेवांबुदुर्गं च गिरिदुर्गं च भार्गव ॥
सर्वेषामेव दुर्गाणां गिरिदुर्गं प्रशस्यते ॥ 7 ॥
2.6.m: a forest fortress, a water fortress, and a mountain fortress, O descendant of Bhṛgu. / Among all fortresses, a mountain fortress is praised.

2.6.s:
durgaṃ ca parikhopetaṃ nṛpāṭṭālakasaṃyutam ..
śataghnīyantramukhyaiśca śataśaśca tathā yutam .. 8 ..
2.6.d:
दुर्गं च परिखोपेतं नृपाट्टालकसंयुतम् ॥
शतघ्नीयन्त्रमुख्यैश्च शतशश्च तथा युतम् ॥ 8 ॥
2.6.m: And the fortress should be provided with a moat, joined with royal battlements, / and equipped with hundreds of śataghnīs and foremost war-machines;

2.6.s:
gopuraṃ saṅkapāṭaṃ ca tatra syātsumanoharam ..
sapatākagajārūḍho yena rājā viśetpuram .. 9 ..
2.6.d:
गोपुरं सङ्कपाटं च तत्र स्यात्सुमनोहरम् ॥
सपताकगजारूढो येन राजा विशेत्पुरम् ॥ 9 ॥
2.6.m: there should be a gatehouse with doors, very beautiful, / through which the king, mounted on an elephant with banners, may enter the city.

2.6.s:
catasraśca tathā tatra kāryāścāpaṇavīthayaḥ ..
ekasmim̐statra vīthyagre devaveśma bhaveddṛḍham .. 10 ..
2.6.d:
चतस्रश्च तथा तत्र कार्याश्चापणवीथयः ॥
एकस्मिम्̐स्तत्र वीथ्यग्रे देववेश्म भवेद्दृढम् ॥ 10 ॥
2.6.m: And four market streets should be made there; / at the end of one street there should be a solid temple of a deity.

2.6.s:
vīthyagre ca dvitīye vai rājaveśmābhidhīyate ..
dharmādhikaraṇaṃ kāryaṃ vīthyagre ca tṛtīyake .. 11 ..
2.6.d:
वीथ्यग्रे च द्वितीये वै राजवेश्माभिधीयते ॥
धर्माधिकरणं कार्यं वीथ्यग्रे च तृतीयके ॥ 11 ॥
2.6.m: At the second street-end, the royal palace is prescribed; / at the third street-end, the court of justice should be made;

2.6.s:
caturthe caiva vīthyagre gopuraṃ ca vidhīyate ..
āyataṃ caturasraṃ vā vṛttaṃ cākārayetpuram .. 12 ..
2.6.d:
चतुर्थे चैव वीथ्यग्रे गोपुरं च विधीयते ॥
आयतं चतुरस्रं वा वृत्तं चाकारयेत्पुरम् ॥ 12 ॥
2.6.m: and at the fourth street-end, a gatehouse is prescribed. / He should make the city oblong, square, or circular.

2.6.s:
muktihīnaṃ trikoṇaṃ ca yavamadhyaṃ tathaiva ca ..
ardhacandraprakāraṃ ca vajrākāraṃ ca varjayet .. 13 ..
2.6.d:
मुक्तिहीनं त्रिकोणं च यवमध्यं तथैव च ॥
अर्धचन्द्रप्रकारं च वज्राकारं च वर्जयेत् ॥ 13 ॥
2.6.m: He should avoid [a shape] lacking symmetry, triangular, wide in the middle like a barleycorn, / in the form of a crescent, and in the form of a vajra.

2.6.s:
ardhacandraṃ praśaṃsanti nadītīraṃ tu tadvaśāt ..
anyatra tanna kartavyaṃ prayatnena vijānatā .. 14 ..
2.6.d:
अर्धचन्द्रं प्रशंसन्ति नदीतीरं तु तद्वशात् ॥
अन्यत्र तन्न कर्तव्यं प्रयत्नेन विजानता ॥ 14 ॥
2.6.m: They praise a crescent shape on a riverbank due to its conformity with it; / elsewhere, the knowledgeable man should not make it, with diligence.

2.6.s:
rājñaḥ kośagṛhaṃ kāryaṃ dakṣiṇe rājaveśmanaḥ ..
tasyāpi dakṣiṇe bhāge gajasthānaṃ vidhīyate..15..
2.6.d:
राज्ञः कोशगृहं कार्यं दक्षिणे राजवेश्मनः ॥
तस्यापि दक्षिणे भागे गजस्थानं विधीयते॥15॥
2.6.m: The king's treasury house should be made to the south of the royal palace; / on its southern side, an elephant stable is prescribed.

2.6.s:
gajānāṃ prāṅmukhī śālā kartavyā cāpyudaṅmukhī ..
āgneye ca tathā bhāge āyudhāgāra iṣyate .. 16..
2.6.d:
गजानां प्राङ्मुखी शाला कर्तव्या चाप्युदङ्मुखी ॥
आग्नेये च तथा भागे आयुधागार इष्यते ॥ 16॥
2.6.m: The stable for elephants should face east or face north; / and in the south-east quarter, the armory is desired.

2.6.s:
mahānasaṃ ca dharmajñaḥ karmaśālāstathāparāḥ ..
gṛhaṃ purodhasaḥ kāryaṃ vāmato rājaveśmanaḥ .. 17 ..
2.6.d:
महानसं च धर्मज्ञः कर्मशालास्तथापराः ॥
गृहं पुरोधसः कार्यं वामतो राजवेश्मनः ॥ 17 ॥
2.6.m: The knower of dharma [should place there] the kitchen and other workshops. / The house of the royal priest should be made to the left of the royal palace,

2.6.s:
mantridaivavidāṃ caiva cikitsākartureva ca ..
tatraiva ca tathā bhāge koṣṭhāgāraṃ vidhīyate .. 18 ..
2.6.d:
मन्त्रिदैवविदां चैव चिकित्साकर्तुरेव च ॥
तत्रैव च तथा भागे कोष्ठागारं विधीयते ॥ 18 ॥
2.6.m: as well as of the minister, the astrologers, and the physician; / and in that very direction, the granary is prescribed.

2.6.s:
gavāṃ sthānaṃ tu karttavyaṃ turagāṇāṃ tathaiva ca ..
uttarābhimukhī śreṇī turagāṇāṃ vidhīyate .. 19 ..
2.6.d:
गवां स्थानं तु कर्त्तव्यं तुरगाणां तथैव च ॥
उत्तराभिमुखी श्रेणी तुरगाणां विधीयते ॥ 19 ॥
2.6.m: A place for cattle should be made, and likewise for horses; / a row facing north is prescribed for horses;

2.6.s:
prāṅmukhī cāpi dharmajña pariśeṣā vigarhitā ..
turagāśca tathā dhāryā praśastaiḥ sārvarātrikaiḥ .. .. 20 ..
2.6.d:
प्राङ्मुखी चापि धर्मज्ञ परिशेषा विगर्हिता ॥
तुरगाश्च तथा धार्या प्रशस्तैः सार्वरात्रिकैः ॥ ॥ 20 ॥
2.6.m: it may also face east, O knower of dharma; the remaining directions are condemned. / Horses should also be kept with excellent night-guards.

2.6.s:
kukkuṭānvānarāṃścaiva markaṭāṃśca narādhipa ..
dhārayedatha śālāsu savatsāṃ dhenumeva ca .. 21 ..
2.6.d:
कुक्कुटान्वानरांश्चैव मर्कटांश्च नराधिप ॥
धारयेदथ शालासु सवत्सां धेनुमेव च ॥ 21 ॥
2.6.m: He should keep roosters, monkeys, and baboons, O king, / and in the stables a milch cow along with her calf;

2.6.s:
ajāśca dhāryā yatnena turagāṇāṃ hitaiṣiṇā ..
gogajāśvaviśālāsu tatpurīṣasya niṣkramam .. 22 ..
2.6.d:
अजाश्च धार्या यत्नेन तुरगाणां हितैषिणा ॥
गोगजाश्वविशालासु तत्पुरीषस्य निष्क्रमम् ॥ 22 ॥
2.6.m: and goats should be kept with care by one wishing the welfare of horses. / In the spacious stalls of cows, elephants, and horses, the removal of their dung

2.6.s:
astaṅgate na kartavyaṃ devadeve divākare ..
tatastatra yathānyāyaṃ rājā vijñāya sāravit .. 23 ..
2.6.d:
अस्तङ्गते न कर्तव्यं देवदेवे दिवाकरे ॥
ततस्तत्र यथान्यायं राजा विज्ञाय सारवित् ॥ 23 ॥
2.6.m: should not be carried out after the sun, god of gods, has set. / Then there, in accordance with rule, having understood [matters], the king who knows the essential...

2.6.s:
dadyādāvasathasthānaṃ sarveṣāmanupūrvaśaḥ ..
yodhānāṃ śilpināṃ caiva sarveṣāmaviśeṣataḥ .. 24 ..
2.6.d:
दद्यादावसथस्थानं सर्वेषामनुपूर्वशः ॥
योधानां शिल्पिनां चैव सर्वेषामविशेषतः ॥ 24 ॥
2.6.m: He should provide living quarters to all in succession, / to warriors and craftsmen alike, all without distinction.

2.6.s:
dadyādāvasathāndurge mantrakālavidāṃ satāma ..
govaidyānaśvavaidyāṃśca gajavaidyāṃstathaiva ca .. 25 ..
2.6.d:
दद्यादावसथान्दुर्गे मन्त्रकालविदां सताम ॥
गोवैद्यानश्ववैद्यांश्च गजवैद्यांस्तथैव च ॥ 25 ॥
2.6.m: In the fort he should assign quarters to virtuous men who know mantras and proper times, / and likewise to bovine doctors, horse doctors, and elephant doctors.

2.6.s:
āhareta bhṛśaṃ rājā durge parabalārujaḥ ..
kuśīlavānāṃ viprāṇāṃ durge sthānaṃ vidhīyate .. .. 205 ..
2.6.d:
आहरेत भृशं राजा दुर्गे परबलारुजः ॥
कुशीलवानां विप्राणां दुर्गे स्थानं विधीयते ॥ ॥ 205 ॥
2.6.m: The king who destroys enemy forces should gather them abundantly in the fortress. / A place in the fort is also prescribed for actors and brahmins,

2.6.s:
na bahūnāṃ na tairdurgaṃ vinā kāryaṃ tathā bhavet ..
durge ca yantrāḥ kartavyā nānāpraharaṇānvitāḥ .. 27 ..
2.6.d:
न बहूनां न तैर्दुर्गं विना कार्यं तथा भवेत् ॥
दुर्गे च यन्त्राः कर्तव्या नानाप्रहरणान्विताः ॥ 27 ॥
2.6.m: yet not for many, nor can the business of the fort proceed without them. / And in the fort mechanical contrivances fitted with diverse weapons should be installed,

2.6.s:
sahasraghātino rāma taistu rakṣā vidhīyate ..
durge dvārāṇi guptāni kāryāṇyapi ca bhūbhujā .. 28 ..
2.6.d:
सहस्रघातिनो राम तैस्तु रक्षा विधीयते ॥
दुर्गे द्वाराणि गुप्तानि कार्याण्यपि च भूभुजा ॥ 28 ॥
2.6.m: capable of slaying a thousand [foes], O Rāma, for defense is maintained by them. / The king should also construct secret gates in the fortress.

2.6.s:
sañcayaścātra sarveṣāṃ cāyudhānāṃ praśasyate ..
dhanuṣāṃ kṣepaṇīyānāṃ tomarāṇāṃ ca bhārgava .. 29 ..
2.6.d:
सञ्चयश्चात्र सर्वेषां चायुधानां प्रशस्यते ॥
धनुषां क्षेपणीयानां तोमराणां च भार्गव ॥ 29 ॥
2.6.m: And here the stockpiling of all weapons is commended: / of bows, missiles, and spears, O descendant of Bhṛgu,

2.6.s:
śarāṇāmatha khaḍgānāṃ khanakānāṃ tathaiva ca ..
laguḍānāṃ guḍānāṃ ca huḍānāṃ parighaiḥ saha .. 30 ..
2.6.d:
शराणामथ खड्गानां खनकानां तथैव च ॥
लगुडानां गुडानां च हुडानां परिघैः सह ॥ 30 ॥
2.6.m: of arrows, swords, and digging tools, / of clubs, balls of stone, huḍas, along with iron bars,

2.6.s:
aśmanāṃ ca prabhūtānāṃ mudgarāṇāṃ tathaiva ca ..
kaṇiyānāṃ triśūlānāṃ paṭṭiśānāṃ ca bhārgava .. 31 ..
2.6.d:
अश्मनां च प्रभूतानां मुद्गराणां तथैव च ॥
कणियानां त्रिशूलानां पट्टिशानां च भार्गव ॥ 31 ॥
2.6.m: of abundant stones and mallets, / of javelins, tridents, and two-edged axes, O descendant of Bhṛgu,

2.6.s:
prāsānāṃ ca tsarūṇāṃ ca śaktīnāṃ ca narottama ..
paraśvadhānāṃ cakrāṇāṃ carmaṇāṃ carmabhiḥ saha .. 32 ..
2.6.d:
प्रासानां च त्सरूणां च शक्तीनां च नरोत्तम ॥
परश्वधानां चक्राणां चर्मणां चर्मभिः सह ॥ 32 ॥
2.6.m: of barbed darts, sword-hilts, and spears, O best of men, / of battle-axes, discs, and shields along with pelts,

2.6.s:
kuddālarajjuvetrāṇāṃ piṭikānāṃ tathaiva ca ..
hrasvakānāṃ ca pātrāṇāmagarasya ca saṃśrayama .. 33 ..
2.6.d:
कुद्दालरज्जुवेत्राणां पिटिकानां तथैव च ॥
ह्रस्वकानां च पात्राणामगरस्य च संश्रयम ॥ 33 ॥
2.6.m: of spades, ropes, reeds, and baskets, / of small vessels, and store of agaru,

2.6.s:
sarveṣāṃ citrabhāṇḍānāṃ sañcayaścātra iṣyate ..
vāditrāṇāṃ ca sarveṣāmauṣadhānāṃ tathaiva ca .. 384 ..
2.6.d:
सर्वेषां चित्रभाण्डानां सञ्चयश्चात्र इष्यते ॥
वादित्राणां च सर्वेषामौषधानां तथैव च ॥ 384 ॥
2.6.m: and the accumulation of all painted vessels is desired here, / as well as of all musical instruments and medicines,

2.6.s:
yavasānāṃ prabhūtānāṃ cendhanasya ca sañcayam ..
guḍasya sarvaśailānāṃ gorasānāṃ tathaiva ca .. 39 ..
2.6.d:
यवसानां प्रभूतानां चेन्धनस्य च सञ्चयम् ॥
गुडस्य सर्वशैलानां गोरसानां तथैव च ॥ 39 ॥
2.6.m: and a stockpile of abundant fodder and fuel, / of treacle, all varieties of stones, and dairy products,

2.6.s:
carmaṇāṃ ca sasajjānāṃ snāyūnāmasthibhiḥ saha ..
gorasasya paṭānāṃ ca dhānyānāṃ sarvatastathā .. 36 ..
2.6.d:
चर्मणां च ससज्जानां स्नायूनामस्थिभिः सह ॥
गोरसस्य पटानां च धान्यानां सर्वतस्तथा ॥ 36 ॥
2.6.m: and of well-prepared skins, sinews along with bones, / dairy products, cloth, and all kinds of grain on every side,

2.6.s:
tathaiva prapaṭānāṃ ca yavagodhūmayorapi ..
ratnānāṃ sarvavastrāṇāṃ lohānāṃ cāpyaśeṣataḥ ..37 ..
2.6.d:
तथैव प्रपटानां च यवगोधूमयोरपि ॥
रत्नानां सर्ववस्त्राणां लोहानां चाप्यशेषतः ॥37 ॥
2.6.m: and likewise fine woven fabrics, barley, and wheat, / precious gems, all textiles, and every kind of metal,

2.6.s:
kalāyamudgamāṣāṇāṃ caṇakānāṃ tilaiḥ saha ..
tathā ca sarvasasyānāṃ pāṃśugomayayorapi ..388...
2.6.d:
कलायमुद्गमाषाणां चणकानां तिलैः सह ॥
तथा च सर्वसस्यानां पांशुगोमययोरपि ॥388॥।
2.6.m: peas, mudga beans, and māṣa beans, chickpeas along with sesame seeds, / as well as all crops, dust, and cow dung.

2.6.s:
saṇasarjarasaṃ bhūrjajatulākṣākaṭaṃkaṭām ..
rājā sañcinuyāddurge yaccānyadapi kiñcana .. 39 ..
2.6.d:
सणसर्जरसं भूर्जजतुलाक्षाकटंकटाम् ॥
राजा सञ्चिनुयाद्दुर्गे यच्चान्यदपि किञ्चन ॥ 39 ॥
2.6.m: Hemp, resin of the sal tree, birch bark, and lac: / whatever else there may be, the king should store it in the fort.

2.6.s:
kumbhāḥ sāṣīviṣā dhāryā vyāghrasiṃhādayastathā ..
mṛgāśca pakṣiṇaścaiva paśavaśca pṛthagvidhāḥ ..4 0 ..
2.6.d:
कुम्भाः साषीविषा धार्या व्याघ्रसिंहादयस्तथा ॥
मृगाश्च पक्षिणश्चैव पशवश्च पृथग्विधाः ॥4 0 ॥
2.6.m: Pots filled with venomous snakes should be kept, as well as tigers, lions, and the like, / and wild beasts, birds, and animals of various kinds.

2.6.s:
sañceyāni viruddhānāṃ suguptāni pṛthakpṛthaka ..
kartavyāni mahābhāga yatnena pṛthivīkṣitā .. 41 ..
2.6.d:
सञ्चेयानि विरुद्धानां सुगुप्तानि पृथक्पृथक ॥
कर्तव्यानि महाभाग यत्नेन पृथिवीक्षिता ॥ 41 ॥
2.6.m: Separate, well-guarded stocks of hostile creatures / must be maintained with effort by the ruler of the earth, O illustrious one.

2.6.s:
uktāni cāpyanuktāni rājadravyāṇyaśeṣataḥ ..
suguptāni pure kuryājjanānāṃ hita kāmyayā .. 42 ..
2.6.d:
उक्तानि चाप्यनुक्तानि राजद्रव्याण्यशेषतः ॥
सुगुप्तानि पुरे कुर्याज्जनानां हित काम्यया ॥ 42 ॥
2.6.m: All royal goods, both spoken of and unspoken, / he should keep well-secured in the citadel out of a desire for the welfare of the people.

2.6.s:
jīvakarṣabhakākolīrāmalakyaḥ parūṣakam ..
śāliparṇī pṛśniparṇī mudgaparṇī tathaiva ca .. 43 ..
2.6.d:
जीवकर्षभकाकोलीरामलक्यः परूषकम् ॥
शालिपर्णी पृश्निपर्णी मुद्गपर्णी तथैव च ॥ 43 ॥
2.6.m: Jīvaka, ṛṣabhaka, kākolī, raw āmalakī, parūṣaka, / śāliparṇī, pṛśniparṇī, and mudgaparṇī,

2.6.s:
māṣaparṇī tathā caiva sārive dve balābhayama ..
vīrāśvagandhā vṛthvīkā bṛhatī kaṇṭakārikā ..44..
2.6.d:
माषपर्णी तथा चैव सारिवे द्वे बलाभयम ॥
वीराश्वगन्धा वृथ्वीका बृहती कण्टकारिका ॥44॥
2.6.m: māṣaparṇī, the two kinds of sārivā, balā, and abhayā, / vīrā, aśvagandhā, vṛthvīkā, bṛhatī, and kaṇṭakārikā,

2.6.s:
śṛṅgāṭikā rodragodhī varṣābhūdarbhagundrakā ..
madhuparṇīvidāryau dve mahādurgā mahā tathā .. 45 ..
2.6.d:
शृङ्गाटिका रोद्रगोधी वर्षाभूदर्भगुन्द्रका ॥

राम उवाच ॥
रक्षोघ्नानि विषघ्नानि यानि कार्याणि भूभुजा ॥

पुष्कर उवाच ॥
बिल्वाढकी यवक्षारपाटलीबाह्लिकोषणाः ॥
श्रीपर्णी सल्लकीयुक्ता निष्क्वाथः प्रोक्षणं परम् ॥ 2 ॥

2.6.m:
Long pepper, long pepper root, chavya, plumbago, and dry ginger, / kuṭheraka, along with black pepper, horseradish tree, marking-nut—the king [should maintain] the fort well-secured at all times.
Rāma said: / Tell me, O best of the upholders of dharma, / of those antidotes that destroy demons and counteract poisons, which the king must employ.
Puṣkara said: / Bilva, āḍhakī, barley alkali, pāṭalī, bāhlika, and black pepper, / combined with śrīparṇī and frankincense: this decoction is the supreme sprinkling.
Whatever is poisoned, when sprinkled with it, immediately becomes free of poison: / barley, rock salt, drinking water, wealth, bed, seat, cooked rice,
armor, ornaments, umbrellas, and hair fly-whisks. / Śailū, pāṭalī, ativiṣā, śigru, gopī, punarnavā,
tree-root bark with saṅgā, wood-apple, resinous sap, / along with danta and śaṭha: a similar sprinkling is destructive of poison.
Lac, priyaṅgu, Indian madder, samaṅgā, along with reṇukā, / combined with liquorice and incense, ground into a paste with brown mongoose bile:

2.6.d:
निखनेद्गोविषाणस्था सप्तरात्रं महीतले ॥
ततः कृत्वा मणिं हेम्ना बद्धं हस्तेन धारयेत् ॥ ॥ 7 ॥
संस्पृष्टस्सविषस्तेन सद्यो भवति निर्विषः ॥
मनोह्वालशमीपुष्पत्वङ्निशाश्वेतसर्षपाः ॥ 8 ॥
कपित्थकुष्ठमञ्जिष्ठाः पित्तेन श्लक्ष्णकल्किताः ॥
धनोगवः कपिल्लायाः सौम्याख्योऽयं पुरो गदः ॥ 9 ॥
विषजित्परमः प्रोक्तो मणिरत्र च पूर्ववत् ॥
मूषकाजिरका चापि हस्ते बद्ध्वा विषापहा ॥ 10 ॥
हरेणुमासी मंजिष्ठा रजनीमधुकं मधु ॥
अक्षत्वक्सुरसं॥॥ ॥श्वपित्तं पूर्ववर्मणि ॥ 11 ॥
वादित्राणि पताकाश्च विष्टैरेतैः प्रलेपिता ॥
श्रुत्वा दृष्ट्वा समाधाय सद्यो भवति निर्विषः ॥ 12 ॥
तत्पूषणं पञ्चलवणं मञ्जिष्ठारजनीद्वयम् ॥
सूक्ष्मैला त्रिवृतापत्रं विरुङ्गानींद्रवारुणी ॥ 13 ॥
2.6.m:
One should bury [the paste] placed inside a cow's horn in the earth for seven nights. / Then, having made an amulet mounted in gold, one should wear it on the arm.
One afflicted with poison becomes free from poison at once when touched by it. / Realgar, orpiment, śamī flowers, cinnamon bark, turmeric, and white mustard;
Wood-apple, kuṣṭha, and madder, finely ground into a paste with bile / from a brown-speckled cow—this antidote, called Saumya, was spoken of of old.
It is declared to be the supreme conqueror of poison, and here too an amulet [is prepared] as before. / Also mūṣakājīrakā, bound on the arm, removes poison.
Hareṇu, māṣī, madder, turmeric, liquorice, honey, / bibhītaka bark, holy basil, [...] dog bile in an amulet as before.
Musical instruments and banners smeared with these substances / make one instantly free from poison upon hearing, seeing, or touching them.
Black pepper, the five salts, madder, the two turmerics, / small cardamom, trivṛt leaf, viḍaṅga, colocynth,

2.6.d:
मधुकं चेति सक्षौद्रं गोविषाणैर्निधापयेत् ॥
तस्मादुष्णाम्बुना मात्रां प्रागुक्तां योजयेत्तथा ॥ ॥14॥
विषं भुक्तं जरां याति निर्विषोपि न दोषकृत् ॥
संतुसर्जरसोशीरसर्षपापत्रवालुकैः ॥15॥
सवेल्लारुष्करपुरैः कुसुमैरर्जुनस्य च॥
धूपोवासो गृहे हन्ति विषं स्थावरजङ्गमम् ॥ 16 ॥
न तत्र कीटा न विषा दर्दुरा न सरीसृपाः ॥
न कृत्याः कर्म नाऽन्यच्च धूपोयं यत्र दह्यते ॥ 17 ॥
कल्कितैश्चन्दनक्षीरपलाशद्रुमवल्कलैः ॥
पूर्वैलवालुसुरसानाकुलीतण्डुलीयकैः ॥ 18 ॥
क्वाथः सर्वोदकार्येषु काकमाचीजलैर्वृतः ॥
रोचनापत्र नैपालीकुंकुमैस्तिलकं वहन् ॥ 19 ॥
विषं न बाधते स्याच्च नरनारीनृपप्रियः ॥
चूर्णैर्हरिद्रामंजिष्ठाकिणिहीकणनिम्बकैः ॥ 20 ॥
जिघ्रं न्निर्विषतामेति गात्रं सर्वविषार्दितम् ॥
शिरीषस्य फलं पत्रं पुष्पं त्वङ्मलमेव च ॥ 21 ॥
2.6.m:
and liquorice, along with honey, should be stored in a cow's horn. / From that, one should administer the dose previously stated with warm water.
Ingested poison becomes digested, and even free from poison it causes no harm. / With sāla resin, vetiver, mustard, tejpāt leaves, and bālukā,
along with viḍaṅga, marking-nut, guggulu, and flowers of the arjuna tree— / fumigating clothes in the house with this destroys both inanimate and animate poison.
No insects, no poisonous creatures, no frogs, and no reptiles, / no sorceries, nor any other hostile rites [persist] where this incense is burnt.
With pastes of sandalwood, kṣīrī, and the barks of the palāśa tree, / and the aforesaid elavālu, holy basil, nākulī, and taṇḍulīyaka,
a decoction surrounded with the juices of kākamācī is used for all water-cleansing rites. / Wearing a forehead-mark made of rocanā, tejpāt, arsenic, and saffron,
poison does not afflict him, and he becomes beloved of men, women, and the king. / By inhaling the powders of turmeric, madder, kiṇihī, pippalī, and neem,
a body afflicted with any poison quickly becomes free from poison. / The fruit, leaf, flower, bark, and root of the śirīṣa tree,

2.28
Rāma said: / The secrets of kingly protection that should be deposited in a fortress, / or caused to be performed by the lord of the earth—tell me those quickly.
Puṣkara said: / Śirīṣa, udumbara, śamī, and citron, flooded with ghee— / this hunger-suppressing formula lasting half a month was declared by the ancients, O Rāma.
Roots of kaśeru, roots of utpala, and sugarcane root, likewise bimbī; / a paste prepared with dūrvā, milk, and ghee is supreme, lasting a month.
Having obtained a man impaled on a stake, a fire-drill should be made of his bone; / one should generate fire there with a bamboo of variegated hue.
Where that is carried counter-clockwise three times around a house, O Bhārgava, / no other fire burns there; no doubt should be entertained on this point.

Clay dense in substance and aged, struck by lightning— / a house smeared with that is not burnt by fire, O twice-born.
Fire should be guarded against by day in the fortress, especially when the wind blows; / and the king must be protected from poison—hear from me the technique in that regard.
Beasts and birds should be kept for the entertainment of the king. / And food should first be tested in fire, and then upon men.
Garments, leaves, ornaments, as well as food and bed coverings— / the lord of the earth should not even touch anything before it has been tested.

2.6.d:
मेहते वानरो राम ग्लायते जीवजीवकः ॥
हृष्टरोमा भवेद्बभ्रुः पृषतश्चैव रोदिति ॥ 21 ॥
हर्षमायाति च शिखी सविषे दर्शने द्विज ॥
अन्नं च सविषं राम चिरेण च विपच्यते ॥ 22 ॥
तथा भवत्यतिस्रावं पक्वं पर्युषितोपमम् ॥
व्यापन्नरसगन्धं च चन्द्रिकाभिस्तथा युतम् ॥ 23 ॥
व्यञ्जनानां च शुष्कत्वं द्रवाणां बुद्बुदोद्भवः ॥
ससैन्धवानां द्रव्याणां जायते फेनमालिका ॥ 24 ॥
रसस्य राजी नीला स्यात्ताम्रा च पयसस्तथा ॥
कोकिलाभा च सध्यस्य तोयस्य च भृगूत्तम ॥ 25 ॥
धान्याम्लस्य तथा कृष्णा कपिला कोद्रवस्य च ॥
मधुश्यावा च तक्रस्य नीला पीता तथैव च ॥ 26 ॥
घृतस्योदकसंकाशा कपोताभा च मस्तुनः ॥
हरिता साक्षिकस्यापि तैलस्य च तथारुणा ॥ 27 ॥
फलानामप्यपक्वानां पाकः क्षिप्रं प्रजायते ॥
प्रकोपश्चैव पक्वानां माल्यानां म्लानता तथा ॥28॥

2.6.d:
मृदुता कठिनानां स्यान्मृदूनां च विपर्ययः ॥
सूक्ष्मतन्तूपसदनं तथा चैवातिरोमता ॥29॥
श्याममण्डलता चैव वस्त्राणामविशेषतः ॥
लोहानां च मणीनां च मलपङ्कोपदिग्धता ॥ 30 ॥
अनुलेपनगन्धानां स्नानानां च भृगूत्तम ॥
विगन्धता च विज्ञेया पर्णानां म्लानता तथा ॥ 31 ॥
पीता नीला सिता ज्ञेया तथा रामाञ्जनस्य च ॥
दन्तकाष्ठत्वचः शान्तास्तन्तुसत्त्वं तथैव च ॥ 32 ॥
एवमादीनि चिह्नानि विज्ञेयानि भृगूत्तम ॥
तस्माद्राजा सदा तिष्ठेन्मणिमन्त्रौषधीगणैः ॥ 33 ॥
आप्तैः संरक्षितो राम प्रमाद परिवर्जकैः ॥ 34 ॥
प्रजातरोर्मूलमिहावनीशस्तद्रक्षणाद्वृत्तिमुपैति राष्ट्रम् ॥
तस्मात्प्रयत्नेन नृपस्य रक्षा सर्वेण कार्या भृगुवंशचन्द्र ॥ 35 ॥
2.29

वास्तुविद्यां समाचक्ष्व यादोगणनृपात्मज ॥।
हिताय मानवेन्द्राणां तथान्येषां च मानद ॥ 1 ॥

2.6.d:
पुष्कर उवाच ॥ ॥
भूमिमादौ परीक्षेत शुभलक्षणलक्षिताम् ॥
पूर्वोदक्प्रवणां धन्यां तथा वै दक्षिणोन्नताम् ॥2॥
न तथा शिकटच्छिन्नां नान्यत्तोयपरिप्लुताम् ॥
वल्मीकमूषिकावासश्वभ्रकण्टकितैर्द्रुमैः॥ 3॥
विहीनां मृदुसंस्पर्शां कठिनां चाप्यनूषराम् ॥
न तथा यवसंस्थानां नेभवज्रोपमां तथा ॥4॥
न शूर्पकूर्मसंस्थानां शक्तिहीनां तथैव च॥
सम्पूर्यमाणां कृमिभिस्तथाधिकमृदं शुभाम् ॥ 5 ॥
गर्भे च कुसुमं यस्यां न म्लानिमुपगच्छति ॥
न निर्वाणमवाप्नोति यस्यां दीपश्च भार्गव ॥ 6 ॥
उदकं च तथा यस्यां शीघ्रं राम न जीर्यते ॥
सा प्रशस्ता क्षितिस्तस्यां निवेशं कारयेद्बुधः ॥ 7 ॥
श्वेता रक्ता तथा पीता कृष्णा चैव यथाक्रमम्॥
विप्रादीनां प्रशस्ता स्यान्मृत्तिका च ततो द्विज ॥8॥

2.6.d:
घृतासृगन्नमद्यानां तुल्यगन्धा तथैव च ॥
मधुरा च कषाया च अम्लोषणरसा तथा ॥9॥
कुशैः शरैस्तथा काशैर्दूर्वाभिर्या च सम्भृता ॥
परीक्ष्य यत्नतो भूमिं तिथिनक्षत्रसम्पदा ॥10॥
सम्पूज्य ब्राह्मणान्पूर्वं निश्शल्यां तां तु कारयेत्॥
खातपूर्वां ततः कृत्वा देवभागांश्च कल्पयेत् ॥ 11 ॥
चतुःषष्टिपदं कृत्वा वास्तुपूर्वं यथाविधि ॥
चतुःषष्टिविभागेन कल्पयित्वा समन्ततः ॥ ॥ 12 ॥
एकैकं तु गृहं तत्र तथैव परिकल्पयेत् ॥
यस्मात्पुरविभागेन द्वारन्यासः प्रकीर्तितः ॥ 13 ॥
अतः परं प्रवक्ष्यामि देवभागान्यथाविधि॥
मध्ये चतुष्पदः स्वामी ब्रह्मा शुभचतुर्मुखः ॥ 14॥।
प्राक्तथा निग्रहः स्वामी कथितश्च तथार्यमा ॥
दक्षिणेन विवस्वांश्च मित्रः पश्चिमतः स्थितः ॥ 15 ॥

2.6.s:

2.6.d:
उदक्पृथ्वीधरश्चैव विकोणेष्वथ मे शृणु ॥
विकोणे शिवदैवत्ये कामपक्षावुभौ सुरौ ॥ 16 ॥
सावित्रीसवितारौ तु तथाग्नेये प्रकीर्तितौ ॥
तथा नैरृतकोणे तु जयेन्द्रौ राम कीर्तितौ ॥ 17 ॥
भद्रव्याधी तु वायव्ये कथितौ भृगुनंदन ॥
देवतानां तथैतासां भूयो बाह्ये तु मण्डले ॥18॥
पूर्वादिषु यथा दिक्षु देवतास्तान्निबोध मे ॥
महेन्द्रश्च रविस्सत्यो भृशः प्राग्राम कीर्तिताः ॥ 19 ॥
गृहक्षितो यमो भृङ्गो गन्धर्वश्चैव याम्यतः ॥
भल्लाटश्च तथा सोम अदितिर्धनदस्तथा ॥ 20 ॥
उत्तरेण स्मृता देवा विकोणेष्वथ मे शृणु ॥
दितिरीशौ मेघजयौ शिवकोणे प्रकीर्तितौ ॥ 21 ॥
व्योमाग्नी पूषवितथौ शिखिकोणे च भार्गव ॥
मृगपित्रीशदौवारिसुग्रीवाश्चैव नैरृते ॥ 22 ॥
रोगानायुश्च नागश्च मुख्याश्वानिलदिक्स्थिताः ॥
ततोऽपि बाह्यतश्चाष्टौ शृणुष्व गदतो मम ॥ 23 ॥

2.6.d:
अष्टावष्टौ विनिर्दिष्टा देवा दिक्षु विदिक्षु च ॥
आद्यन्तौ तु तयोर्देवौ प्रोक्तावथ ग्रहेश्वरौ।
पर्जन्यः प्रथमो देवो द्वितीयश्च करग्रहः ॥
महेन्द्ररविसत्याश्च भृशोऽथ गमनस्ततः ॥ 25 ॥
पवनश्च महाभागाः पूर्वेणैते प्रकीर्तिताः ॥
पुष्योऽथ त्रितुदश्चैव तथैव च ग्रहर्क्षतः ॥ 26 ॥
यमो भृशश्च गन्धर्वो मृगोऽथ पितरस्तथा ॥
दक्षिणेन विनिर्दिष्टा देवा भृगुकुलोद्वह ॥ 27 ॥
दौवारिकश्च सुग्रीवः पुष्पदंतस्तथा सुरः ॥
वरुणस्तु तथा यक्षो रोगः शोषस्तथैव च ॥ 28 ॥
पश्चिमेन विनिर्दिष्टा देवा दानवनाशनाः ॥
नागराजस्तथा मुख्यो भल्लाटश्च तथा शशी ॥ 29 ॥
अदितिश्च कुबेरश्च नागश्चाथ हुताशनः ॥
एते देवा विनिर्दिष्टास्तथा चोत्तरतो द्विज ॥ 30 ॥
एतेषामेव देवानां भागे द्वाराणि कारयेत् ॥
शुभानि तेषु वक्ष्यामि शेषाणि परिवर्जयेत् ॥ 31 ॥
2.6.m:
Eight deities are assigned to each of the cardinal and intermediate directions. / The first and the last of them, moreover, are proclaimed lords of the planets. / Parjanya is the first deity, and the second is Karagraha, / and then Mahendra, Ravi, Satya, Bhṛśa, and Gamana;
and Pavana, O fortunate ones, are declared on the east. / Then Puṣya and Trituda, and likewise Graharkṣata,
Yama, Bhṛśa, Gandharva, Mṛga, and the Pitṛs / are the deities assigned on the south, O scion of the Bhṛgu lineage.
Dauvārika, Sugrīva, Puṣpadanta, the god [Asura], / Varuṇa, Yakṣa, Roga, and Śoṣa:
[these] are the deities assigned on the west, destroyers of the Dānavas. / Then Nāgarāja, Mukhya, Bhallāṭa, Śaśin,
Aditi, Kubera, Nāga, and Hutāśana: / these are the deities assigned on the north, O twice-born.
One should construct doors precisely in the divisions of these deities; / I will tell you the auspicious ones among them, and one should avoid the rest.

2.6.d:

गृहर्क्षतश्च पुष्पश्च तथा दक्षिणतः शुभौ ॥ 32 ॥
सुग्रीवः पुष्पदन्तश्च शुभौ पश्चिमतो द्विज ॥
भल्लाटः सोमदेवश्च द्वारे श्रेष्ठौ तथा ह्युदक् ॥33॥
द्वात्रिंशच्च बहिर्देवास्तथान्तर्द्वादश स्मृताः ॥
मध्ये ब्रह्मा तथा प्रोक्त एवं ते पिण्डदेवताः ॥ 34 ॥
चत्वारिंशद्विनिर्दिष्टास्तथा पञ्च च भार्गव ॥
विन्यस्याजिरमेवादौ चतुष्षष्टिपदं द्विज ॥ 35 ॥
तत्र देवविभागेन गृहकर्म विधीयते ॥
चन्द्रसुग्रीवपर्जन्यसत्येन्द्रार्यमवारुणे ॥ 36 ॥
भगवत्संग्रहं कुर्याद्यथासंस्थानतो द्विज ॥
सूर्यान्तरिक्षसत्याग्निभागेषु च महानसम् ॥ 37 ॥
वाय्वन्तरिक्षसुग्रीवभल्लाटपितृदैवते ॥
गंधर्वपुष्पदन्ताख्ये भागे कूपं तु कारयेत् ॥ 38 ॥
2.6.m:
Those sacred to Mahendra and Soma on the east are traditionally taught as bestowing good fortune. / On the south, [those sacred to] Gṛharkṣata and Puṣpa are auspicious.
On the west, O twice-born, [those of] Sugrīva and Puṣpadanta are auspicious; / and on the north, Bhallāṭa and the god Soma are best for a door.
Thirty-two are recorded as the outer deities, and twelve as the inner. / In the centre, Brahmā is proclaimed: thus are the deities of the site.
Forty-five [deities] in all are specified, O descendant of Bhṛgu. / First laying out the courtyard [as a grid of] sixty-four squares, O twice-born,
house construction is undertaken there according to the allocation of deities. / In [the divisions of] Candra, Sugrīva, Parjanya, Satya, Indra, Aryaman, and Vāruṇa,
one should make the sanctuary of the Lord according to his placement, O twice-born. / And in the divisions of Sūrya, Antarikṣa, Satya, and Agni [one should make] the kitchen.
In the divisions sacred to Vāyu, Antarikṣa, Sugrīva, Bhallāṭa, and the Pitṛs, / and in that named after Gandharva and Puṣpadanta, one should make a well.

2.6.d:
एकवृक्षाधिकं तत्र तथा कुर्याद्द्विजोत्तम ॥
अथवा दिग्विभागेन गृहकर्म विधीयते ॥ 39 ॥
ऐशान्यां देवतावेश्म तथाग्नेय्यां महानसम् ॥
अग्न्यागारं च तत्रैव भ्रमं नैरृतके तथा ॥ 40 ॥
कोष्ठागारायुधागारौ वायव्यां च तथा स्मृतौ ॥
कूपादिस्थोदकं शस्तं दिक्षु चैवोत्तरासु च ॥ 41 ॥
अन्यासु गर्हितं राम प्रयत्नेन विवर्जयेत् ॥
पुराणं नवमिश्रं तु दारुवेश्मनि वर्जयेत् ॥ 42 ॥
सकुड्यं परकुड्यं च नैव कार्यं विजानता ॥
विनार्कचन्द्रग्रहणं द्वारसम्परिवर्तनम् ॥ 43 ॥
वृद्धिक्षयौ न कर्तव्यौ भूयः कर्मणि वेश्मनः ॥
प्रागुत्तरेऽथवा कार्यौ ब्राह्मणानुमते तथा ॥
ब्रह्मस्थानं शुचिर्नित्यं कार्यं भवति भार्गव ॥ 44 ॥
न पीडनीयं च तथा नागदन्तादिभिर्भवेत् ॥
मर्माणि राम जानीयाद्देवतापदसन्धिषु ॥ 45 ॥

2.6.d:
न पीडयेत्तथा तानि नागदन्तादिभिर्द्विज ॥
ये द्रुमा वटसंसिक्तास्तथा ये च सकोटराः ॥46 ॥
हस्तिविद्युद्धता ये च देवतावेश्मजाश्च ये ॥
वह्निस्पृष्टाः श्मशाने च ये च जाताश्चतुष्पथे॥47॥
रोकवृक्षाश्च ये केचिन्न ते शस्ताः कथञ्चन ॥
वृक्षस्य महतीं पूजां कृत्वा तद्वासकस्य च ॥ 48 ॥
मध्वाज्यदिग्धेन तथा छिन्द्यात्परशुना द्विजः ॥
पूर्वोत्तरेण पतनं प्रशस्तं परिकीर्तितम् ॥49॥
शेषासु पतनं दिक्षु गर्हितं द्विजसत्तम ॥
वटाश्वत्थौ च निर्गुण्डी कोविदारविभीतकौ ॥50 ॥
पुष्यकं शाल्मलिश्चैव पलाशं च विवर्जयेत ॥
विस्तारद्द्विगुणोच्छ्रायं द्वारं कार्यं तथा गृहे॥51 ॥
निधिप्रथमको नागहंससारसचित्रितम् ॥
द्वारको नेत्रमद्वाभ्र चतुष्पथसुरालयैः॥52॥
कूपैकवृक्षरथ्याभिर्विद्धं द्वारं विवर्जयेत्॥
द्विगुणात्तु गृहोच्छायाद्भूमिं त्यक्त्वा न दोषभाक्॥53॥
2.6.m:
one should not obstruct them with pegs and the like, O twice-born. / Trees that are entwined with banyan trees, and those that have hollows,
those struck by elephants or lightning, and those that grow in temples, / those touched by fire, and those grown in cremation grounds or at crossroads,
and any diseased trees—none of these is ever praised. / Having performed great worship of the tree and of its inhabitant,
the twice-born should cut it with an axe smeared with honey and clarified butter. / Falling toward the northeast is proclaimed most commendable;
falling in the remaining directions is censured, O best of the twice-born. / Banyan, aśvattha, nirguṇḍī, kovidāra, vibhītaka,
puṣyaka, śālmali, and palāśa should be avoided. / In a house, the door should be made twice as high as its width.
[A door] decorated with the foremost of treasures, serpents, haṃsas, and sārasas / [is auspicious]. A doorway [encroached upon] by a sewer, clouds, a crossroad, a temple,
pierced by a well, a solitary tree, or a street, one should avoid. / Leaving ground equal to twice the height of the house, it incurs no fault.

2.6.s:
ādhmātaṃ sakaṭaṃ rāma tathāmbuplavi yadbhavet..

2.6.d:
आध्मातं सकटं राम तथाम्बुप्लवि यद्भवेत्॥
द्वारं न तत्प्रशंसन्ति तस्मात्तु परिवर्जयेत्॥54॥
पुरद्वाराधिकं श्रीदं भागेषु च तथा भ्रमम्॥
धनदस्य तथा भागैर्धनवेश्म विधीयते॥55॥
इन्द्रसत्येन्द्रसुग्रीवद्वारमन्यत्र कारयेत् ॥
स्तम्भं तु नवधा कृत्वा पीठे भागं तु कारयेत् ॥ 56 ॥
भागे कुम्भस्तथा कार्यो भागे पद्मं निवेशयेत् ॥
स्तम्भं भागत्रये कार्यमष्टास्रमथ वर्तुलम् ॥ 57 ॥
तस्योपरि तथा भागे भवत्यामलसारकम् ॥
भागदोषे तुला कार्या भागे कार्या तथा तुला ॥ 58 ॥
एकशालचतुश्शालौ कर्तव्यौ स्वेच्छया सदा ॥
पूर्वोत्तराभिः शालाभिर्हीनं कार्यं द्विशालकम् ॥ 55 ॥
अन्यथा गर्हितं राम सुतार्थक्षयदं मतम् ॥
अष्टहस्तोच्छ्रयादूर्ध्वं भूमिकां तु न कारयेत् ॥ 60 ॥
2.6.m:
[A door] that is swollen, leaning, O Rāma, or flooded with water— / such a door they do not praise; therefore one should avoid it.
Larger than the town gate, it bestows prosperity, as does a water drain in its [proper] divisions. / The treasury is prescribed in the divisions of Kubera.
One should make a door elsewhere in [the divisions of] Indra, Satyendra, or Sugrīva. / Dividing a pillar into nine parts, one should assign one part to the base.
In one part a pot should be made; in one part one should place a lotus. / The shaft of the pillar should be made in three parts, octagonal or circular;
above it, in one part, is the āmalasāraka. / At the bracket part a beam is to be made, and in one part an upper beam.
A single-winged and a four-winged [house] should always be made at will. / A two-winged [house] should be made lacking the eastern and northern wings;
otherwise, O Rāma, it is censured and considered to cause the loss of sons and wealth. / One should not make a storey exceeding eight cubits in height.

2.6.s:
vāstūcchrāyaṃ na kartavyaṃ tathā hastaśatādhikam ..

2.6.d:
वास्तूच्छ्रायं न कर्तव्यं तथा हस्तशताधिकम् ॥
आरम्भं सशिलान्यासं द्वारस्तम्भोच्छ्रयावुभौ ॥ 61 ॥
तथारोहणनिष्पत्ती तथा वास्तुप्रवेशनम् ॥
सर्वाण्येतानि कार्याणि दिवसे राम पूजिते ॥62॥
शेषेष्वेतेषु कर्तव्यं देवब्राह्मणपूजनम् ॥
कालज्ञपूजनं चैव स्थपतीनां च भार्गव ॥ 63 ॥
प्रावृट्काले न कर्तव्यं वास्तुकर्म विजानता॥
कृष्णपक्षत्रिभागान्ते शुक्लाद्ये च भृगूत्तम ॥ 64 ॥
तिथिं चतुर्थी नवमीं वर्जयेच्च चतुर्दशीम् ॥
अङ्गारकदिनं राम करणं विष्टिसंज्ञितम् ॥ 65 ॥
दिव्यान्तरिक्षक्षितिजैरुत्पातैर्भं च पीडितम् ॥
ग्रहोपस्पृष्टं च तथा व्यतीपातहतं च यत् ॥ 66 ॥
चन्द्रतारानुकूले भे वास्तुकार्यं विजानता ॥
ध्रुवाणि तानि शस्तानि शाक्रं वै नैरृतं तथा ॥67॥
2.6.m:
The height of the building should not exceed one hundred cubits. / The commencement, the laying of the stone, the erection of both the door and the pillars,
the roofing, the completion, and likewise the entrance into the house— / all these, O Rāma, should be performed on an auspicious day.
In the remainder of these, one must perform the worship of the gods and brahmins, / and the worship of the astrologer and the master builders, O descendant of Bhṛgu.
Building work must not be undertaken by a wise person during the rainy season, / at the end of the third part of the dark fortnight, or at the beginning of the bright, O foremost of the Bhṛgus.
One should avoid the fourth, ninth, and fourteenth lunar days, / Tuesday, Rāma, and the division of the day called Viṣṭi;
And a constellation afflicted by portents originating in the heavens, the atmosphere, or on earth, / touched by malefics, or struck by Vyatīpāta.
When the constellation is favorable to one's Moon and birth star, the wise should undertake building work. / The fixed [constellations] are auspicious, as well as the asterisms of Indra and Nirṛti;

2.6.d:
सौम्यं च वैष्णवं पुष्यं पौष्णं सावित्रमेव च ॥
स्थिरलग्ने स्थिरांशे च कर्तुश्चोपचयात्मके ॥68 ॥
यस्य सौम्यग्रहाः केन्द्रे त्रिकोणे चापि भार्गव ॥
पापाश्चोपचयस्थाने तस्मिन्कार्यं प्रवेशनम् ॥ 69 ॥
केन्द्रस्थं वर्जयेत्पापं सर्वयत्नेन कर्मसु ॥
केन्द्रं सौम्ययुतं देवं न तु शून्यं कदाचन ॥ 70 ॥
अतः परं प्रवक्ष्यामि शिलान्यासविधिं तव ॥
चतुःषष्टिपदं कृत्वा समे स्थाने तु मण्डलम् ॥71॥
कृत्वा तु देवतान्यासं तत्र मण्डलके द्विज ॥
श्रियः सम्पूजनं कृत्वा वासुदेवस्य चाप्यथ ॥ 72 ॥
पूजनं मण्डले कार्यं वास्तुदेवगणस्य च ॥
गन्धार्धपुष्प नैवेद्यधूपदीपैर्भृगूत्तम ॥ 73 ॥
तेषां सम्पूजनं कृत्वा समादाय हुताशनम् ॥
ओंकारपूर्वमाज्यं तु जुहुयाच्छ्रीधरस्य तु ॥ 74 ॥
2.6.m:
And Saumya, Vaiṣṇava, Puṣya, Pauṣṇa, and Sāvitra; / in a fixed ascendant, in a fixed navāṃśa, and one that is an upacaya house for the builder.
When benefic planets are in a center and a trine for him, O Bhārgava, / and malefics are in an upacaya position, entry into [the house] should be performed at that [time].
One should avoid a malefic in a center with every effort in all rites; / a center should have a benefic, O king, and never be empty.
After this, I shall explain to you the ritual of laying the foundation stones. / Having made a diagram of sixty-four squares on an even ground,
and having performed the ritual placement of the deities on that small diagram, O twice-born, / and having worshiped Śrī and then also Vāsudeva,
worship of the host of house deities should be performed on the sacred diagram / with perfumes, unbroken grains, flowers, food-offerings, incense, and lamps, O foremost of the Bhṛgus.
Having performed their worship and taken up the fire, / one should offer clarified butter preceded by the syllable Om to the bearer of Śrī;

2.6.s:
śriyaḥ kṛtvā tato homaṃ brahmaṇaḥ kārayettataḥ ..
brahmāṇaṃ tu puraskṛtya vāstudevagaṇasya ca .. 75 ..
hotavyamājyaṃ dharmajña yasya devasya hūyate ..
tatkālamāśu bhajate lakṣaṇegnau dvijottama .. 76 ..
tasya devasya yatsthānaṃ tatra śalyaṃ vinirdiśet ..
śalyasyoddharaṇaṃ kāryaṃ rāma yatnena jānatā .. 77 ..
madhye śailamayaṃ kumbhaṃ śaṃkuṃ ca sthāpayedbudhaḥ ..
aiśāne ca tataḥ koṇe śilāṃ pūrvaṃ pratiṣṭhayet .. 78 ..
pradakṣiṇaṃ tato rāma śilānyāsaṃ vidhīyate ..
kumbhasya ca śilānāṃ ca tataḥ snānaṃ vidhīyate ..79..
vaṭāśvatthakaṣāyeṇa sarvauṣadhijalaistataḥ ..
tato'nulepanaṃ kāryaṃ candanena sugandhinā ..80..
ācchādanaṃ tataḥ kāryaṃ vāsobhiḥ kusumaiḥ śubhaiḥ ..
dhūpaṃ pradīpaṃ naivedyaṃ teṣāṃ rāma nivedayet .. 81 ..
2.6.d:
श्रियः कृत्वा ततो होमं ब्रह्मणः कारयेत्ततः ॥
ब्रह्माणं तु पुरस्कृत्य वास्तुदेवगणस्य च ॥ 75 ॥
होतव्यमाज्यं धर्मज्ञ यस्य देवस्य हूयते ॥
तत्कालमाशु भजते लक्षणेग्नौ द्विजोत्तम ॥ 76 ॥
तस्य देवस्य यत्स्थानं तत्र शल्यं विनिर्दिशेत् ॥
शल्यस्योद्धरणं कार्यं राम यत्नेन जानता ॥ 77 ॥
मध्ये शैलमयं कुम्भं शंकुं च स्थापयेद्बुधः ॥
ऐशाने च ततः कोणे शिलां पूर्वं प्रतिष्ठयेत् ॥ 78 ॥
प्रदक्षिणं ततो राम शिलान्यासं विधीयते ॥
कुम्भस्य च शिलानां च ततः स्नानं विधीयते ॥79॥
वटाश्वत्थकषायेण सर्वौषधिजलैस्ततः ॥
ततोऽनुलेपनं कार्यं चन्दनेन सुगन्धिना ॥80॥
आच्छादनं ततः कार्यं वासोभिः कुसुमैः शुभैः ॥
धूपं प्रदीपं नैवेद्यं तेषां राम निवेदयेत् ॥ 81 ॥
2.6.m:
then having made an oblation to Śrī, one should then make [an oblation] to Brahmā; / and placing Brahmā at the head, to the host of house deities
clarified butter must be offered, O knower of dharma. For whichever deity the oblation is being made, / if an inauspicious mark appears in the fire at that time, O best of the twice-born,
at the place belonging to that deity one should designate an extraneous bone. / The removal of that bone should be performed with effort by the wise [builder], O Rāma.
In the middle, the wise one should set up a stone jar and a gnomon, / and then first consecrate the stone in the north-eastern corner.
Then, O Rāma, the ritual placement of the stones is prescribed in a clockwise direction. / Then the bathing of the jar and of the stones is prescribed,
with a decoction of banyan and sacred fig, and then with water containing all medicinal herbs; / then anointing should be done with fragrant sandalwood.
Then covering must be done with garments and auspicious flowers; / one should present incense, lamps, and food-offerings to them, O Rāma.

2.6.s:
dakṣiṇābhirdvijendrāṇāṃ tataḥ pūjā vidhīyate ..
kālavitsthapatī pūjyau tato rāma vijānatā .. 82 ..
tato mantraṃ japetkartā kālajñaḥ sthapatiḥ svayam ..
gṛhaṃ puṣṭikaraṃ rāma munivaktrādvinissṛtam .. 83 ..
nande nandaya vāsiṣṭhe vasubhiḥ prajayā saha ..
jaye jayāvahe devi prajānāṃ jayamāvaha .. 84 ..
pūrṇe'ṅgirasadāyāde pūrṇakāmaṃ kuruṣva māma ..
bhadre kaśyapadāyāde kuru bhadrāṃ matiṃ mama .. 85 ..
sarvabījasamāyukte sarvaratnauṣadhairvṛte ..
rucire nandane nande vāsiṣṭhe ramyatāmiha .. 86 ..
prajāpatisute devi caturagre mahīmaye ..
subhage suvrate bhadre gṛhe kāśyapi ramyatām .. 87 ..
pūjite paramācāyairgandhamālyairalaṃkṛte ..
bhavabhūtikarī devi gṛhaṃ bhārgavi ramyatām .. 88 ..
2.6.d:
दक्षिणाभिर्द्विजेन्द्राणां ततः पूजा विधीयते ॥
कालवित्स्थपती पूज्यौ ततो राम विजानता ॥ 82 ॥
ततो मन्त्रं जपेत्कर्ता कालज्ञः स्थपतिः स्वयम् ॥
गृहं पुष्टिकरं राम मुनिवक्त्राद्विनिस्सृतम् ॥ 83 ॥
नन्दे नन्दय वासिष्ठे वसुभिः प्रजया सह ॥
जये जयावहे देवि प्रजानां जयमावह ॥ 84 ॥
पूर्णेऽङ्गिरसदायादे पूर्णकामं कुरुष्व माम ॥
भद्रे कश्यपदायादे कुरु भद्रां मतिं मम ॥ 85 ॥
सर्वबीजसमायुक्ते सर्वरत्नौषधैर्वृते ॥
रुचिरे नन्दने नन्दे वासिष्ठे रम्यतामिह ॥ 86 ॥
प्रजापतिसुते देवि चतुरग्रे महीमये ॥
सुभगे सुव्रते भद्रे गृहे काश्यपि रम्यताम् ॥ 87 ॥
पूजिते परमाचायैर्गन्धमाल्यैरलंकृते ॥
भवभूतिकरी देवि गृहं भार्गवि रम्यताम् ॥ 88 ॥
2.6.m:
Then the worship of the foremost brahmins with sacrificial fees is prescribed; / then the astrologer and the architect must be worshiped by the wise one, O Rāma.
Then the patron himself, the astrologer, and the architect should chant the mantra / that brings prosperity to the house, O Rāma, which issued from the mouth of the sage:
"O Nandā, daughter of Vasiṣṭha, bring joy along with treasures and offspring! / O Jayā, bringer of victory, O goddess, bring victory to my progeny!
O Pūrṇā, heiress of Aṅgiras, make my desire fulfilled! / O Bhadrā, heiress of Kaśyapa, make my mind auspicious!
Furnished with all kinds of seeds, surrounded by all gems and medicinal herbs, / delightful, pleasing, O Nandā, daughter of Vasiṣṭha, take delight here!
O goddess, daughter of Prajāpati, four-cornered, made of earth, / fortunate, of good vows, auspicious, O daughter of Kaśyapa, take delight in this house!
Worshiped by the supreme teachers, adorned with perfumes and garlands, / causing growth and prosperity, O goddess, O daughter of Bhṛgu, take delight in this house!

2.6.s:
avyaṅge cākṛte pūrṇe sunetryaṅgirasaḥ sute ..
iṣṭake tvaṃ prayaccheṣṭaṃ pratiṣṭhāṃ kāmayāmyaham .. 89..
2.6.d:
अव्यङ्गे चाकृते पूर्णे सुनेत्र्यङ्गिरसः सुते ॥
इष्टके त्वं प्रयच्छेष्टं प्रतिष्ठां कामयाम्यहम् ॥ 89॥
2.6.m: Unimpaired, shapely, complete, O beautiful-eyed daughter of Aṅgiras! / O brick, grant what is wished; I desire a secure foundation.

2.6.s:
deśasvāmipurasvāmigṛhasvāmigṛhe vasa ..
manuṣyadhanahastyaśvapaśuvṛddhikarī bhava .. 90 ..
2.6.d:
देशस्वामिपुरस्वामिगृहस्वामिगृहे वस ॥
मनुष्यधनहस्त्यश्वपशुवृद्धिकरी भव ॥ 90 ॥
2.6.m: Dwell in the house of the lord of the land, the lord of the city, and the lord of the house; / cause an increase of people, wealth, elephants, horses, and cattle!"

2.6.s:
gṛhapraveśe'pi tathā śilānyāsasamo vidhiḥ ..
kartavyaḥ sakalo rāma śilānyāsavivarjitaḥ .. 91 ..
2.6.d:
गृहप्रवेशेऽपि तथा शिलान्याससमो विधिः ॥
कर्तव्यः सकलो राम शिलान्यासविवर्जितः ॥ 91 ॥
2.6.m: At the entrance into a house, all the same rites as the foundation-stone ritual / should likewise be performed, O Rāma, with the exception of laying the foundation stones:

2.6.s:
pūjitāparalakṣmīkaṃ hutvāgniṃ cāpyalaṃkṛtam ..
pañcaraṅgena sūtreṇa baddhapratisaraṃ tathā .. 92 ..
2.6.d:
पूजितापरलक्ष्मीकं हुत्वाग्निं चाप्यलंकृतम् ॥
पञ्चरङ्गेन सूत्रेण बद्धप्रतिसरं तथा ॥ 92 ॥
2.6.m: Having worshiped Aparā-Lakṣmī, offered oblation in the decorated fire, / and having tied a protective thread made of five-colored cord,

2.6.s:
saphaleṣu ca bāṇeṣu diśāsu vidiśāsu ca ..
gavākṣakeṣu kartavyāścakrā rakṣohaṇāstathā .. 93 ..
2.6.d:
सफलेषु च बाणेषु दिशासु विदिशासु च ॥
गवाक्षकेषु कर्तव्याश्चक्रा रक्षोहणास्तथा ॥ 93 ॥
2.6.m: and on arrows with fruit in the cardinal and intermediate directions, / and in the latticed windows, demon-slaying diagrams should be made.

2.6.s:
sarvasyāsya tathā nyāsaṃ mantrai rakṣohaṇairbhavet ..
gopṛṣṭhavinyastakaraḥ praviśecca gṛhī gṛham .. 94 ..
2.6.d:
सर्वस्यास्य तथा न्यासं मन्त्रै रक्षोहणैर्भवेत् ॥
गोपृष्ठविन्यस्तकरः प्रविशेच्च गृही गृहम् ॥ 94 ॥
2.6.m: The ritual placement of all this should be performed with demon-slaying mantras. / With his hand placed on the back of a cow, the householder should enter the house,

2.6.s:
sva'nuliptassukhī sragvī sapatnīkastathaiva ca ..
dvijapuṇyāhaghoṣeṇa vīṇāveṇuraveṇa ca ..
bandināṃ ca ninādena paṭahānāṃ svanena ca .. 95 ..
2.6.d:
स्वऽनुलिप्तस्सुखी स्रग्वी सपत्नीकस्तथैव च ॥
द्विजपुण्याहघोषेण वीणावेणुरवेण च ॥
बन्दिनां च निनादेन पटहानां स्वनेन च ॥ 95 ॥
2.6.m: anointed, happy, wearing a garland, together with his wife, / accompanied by the sound of the brahmins' blessing of the day, the sound of the vīṇā and the flute, / the singing of bards, and the sound of kettledrums.

2.6.s:
kāle śubhe kālavidā pradiṣṭe satoraṇaṃ pūrṇaghaṭābhirāmam ..
praviśya kālajñasamarcitānāṃ kṛtvārcanaṃ tatra surottamānām .. 96 ..
2.6.d:
काले शुभे कालविदा प्रदिष्टे सतोरणं पूर्णघटाभिरामम् ॥
प्रविश्य कालज्ञसमर्चितानां कृत्वार्चनं तत्र सुरोत्तमानाम् ॥ 96 ॥
2.6.m: At an auspicious time indicated by the astrologer, entering [the house] adorned with an archway and charming with full water pots, / having performed worship there to the highest gods honored by the astrologer,

2.6.s:
sampūjya vahniṃ dvijapuṅgavāṃśca māṅgalyamālabhya ca bhojayitvā ..
viprānmadhukṣīraghṛtotkaṭānnaiḥ sadakṣiṇāṃstāṃśca tathā visarjya .. 97 ..
2.6.d:
सम्पूज्य वह्निं द्विजपुङ्गवांश्च माङ्गल्यमालभ्य च भोजयित्वा ॥
विप्रान्मधुक्षीरघृतोत्कटान्नैः सदक्षिणांस्तांश्च तथा विसर्ज्य ॥ 97 ॥
2.6.m: having worshiped the fire and the foremost brahmins, having touched auspicious items, and having fed / the brahmins with foods rich in honey, milk, and clarified butter, and having dismissed them with sacrificial fees,

2.6.s:
saptāhamagniṃ paricarya tatra sampūjya viprānvidhivacca rāma ..
gṛhe vasetpūjitadevavipre śucau sadā sarvaguṇopapanne .. 98 ..
2.30
.. puṣkara uvāca .. ..
uttareṇa śubhaḥ plakṣo vaṭaḥ prāgbhārgavottama ..
udumbaraśca yāmyena saumyenāśvattha eva ca .. 1 ..
ete krameṇa neṣyanti dakṣiṇādisamudbhavāḥ ..
samīpajātāśca tathā varjyāḥ kaṇṭakino drumāḥ .. 2 ..
vāmabhāge tathodyānaṃ kuryādvāsagṛhācchubham ..
vāpayetprāktilāṃstatra mṛndīyāttāṃśca puṣpitān .. 3 ..
tatastu ropayedvṛkṣānprayataḥ susamāhitaḥ ..
snāto drumamathābhyarcya brāhmaṇāṃśca śivaṃ tathā .. 4 ..
dhruvāṇi pañca vāyavyaṃ hastaḥ puṣyaḥ savaiṣṇavaḥ ..
nakṣatrāṇi tathā mūlaṃ śasyate drumaropaṇe 55..
udyānaṃ sajalaṃ rāma nābhirāmaṃ yadā tadā ..
praveśayenna vipaṭa (kuruhān )puṣkariṇyaśca kārayet .. 6 ..
2.6.d:
सप्ताहमग्निं परिचर्य तत्र सम्पूज्य विप्रान्विधिवच्च राम ॥
गृहे वसेत्पूजितदेवविप्रे शुचौ सदा सर्वगुणोपपन्ने ॥ 98 ॥
2.30
॥ पुष्कर उवाच ॥ ॥
उत्तरेण शुभः प्लक्षो वटः प्राग्भार्गवोत्तम ॥
उदुम्बरश्च याम्येन सौम्येनाश्वत्थ एव च ॥ 1 ॥
एते क्रमेण नेष्यन्ति दक्षिणादिसमुद्भवाः ॥
समीपजाताश्च तथा वर्ज्याः कण्टकिनो द्रुमाः ॥ 2 ॥
वामभागे तथोद्यानं कुर्याद्वासगृहाच्छुभम् ॥
वापयेत्प्राक्तिलांस्तत्र मृन्दीयात्तांश्च पुष्पितान् ॥ 3 ॥
ततस्तु रोपयेद्वृक्षान्प्रयतः सुसमाहितः ॥
स्नातो द्रुममथाभ्यर्च्य ब्राह्मणांश्च शिवं तथा ॥ 4 ॥
ध्रुवाणि पञ्च वायव्यं हस्तः पुष्यः सवैष्णवः ॥
नक्षत्राणि तथा मूलं शस्यते द्रुमरोपणे 55॥
उद्यानं सजलं राम नाभिरामं यदा तदा ॥
प्रवेशयेन्न विपट (कुरुहान् )पुष्करिण्यश्च कारयेत् ॥ 6 ॥
2.6.m:
having tended the fire there for seven days and having honored the brahmins according to the rules, O Rāma, / he should live in the house in which the gods and brahmins have been worshiped, pure, and endowed with all good qualities at all times.
2.30 Puṣkara said: / To the north, a plakṣa tree is auspicious; a banyan tree to the east, O foremost of the Bhṛgus; / an udumbara tree to the south, and a sacred fig tree to the north.
These arising to the south and other [wrong directions] are not desired in their order; / and similarly, thorny trees that have grown nearby should be avoided.
Likewise, one should make an auspicious garden on the left side of the dwelling house. / One should first sow sesame seeds there and crush them when they have flowered;
then, purified and concentrated in mind, having bathed, / having worshiped the tree, the brahmins, and Śiva, one should plant trees.
The five fixed asterisms, Vāyavya, Hasta, Puṣya, along with Vaiṣṇava, / and Mūla are recommended for the planting of trees.
When a garden with water is not charming, O Rāma, / then one should not introduce […], and one should construct water reservoirs.

2.6.s:
saṃskāryamudbhidaṃ toyaṃ kūpāḥ kāryāḥ prayatnataḥ ..
hastaṃ maghā tathā maitraṃ saumyaṃ puṣyaṃ ca vāsavam .. 7 ..
uttarātritayaṃ rāma tathā pūrvā ca phalgunī ..
jalāśayasamāraṃbhe praśaste vāruṇaṃ tathā .. 8 ..
sampūjya varuṇaṃ devaṃ viṣṇuṃ parjanyameva ca ..
tarpayitvā dvijānkāmaistadāraṃbhakaro bhavet .. 9 ..
athodyāne pravakṣyāmi praśastānpādapāndvija ..
ariṣṭāśokapunnāgaśirīṣāmrapriyaṅgavaḥ .. 10 ..
panasāśokadacalījambūlakucadāḍimāḥ ..
māṅgalyāḥ pūrvamārāme ropaṇīyā gṛheṣu vā .. 11 ..
kṛtvā bahutvameteṣāṃ ropyāssarve hyanantaram ..
śālmaliṃ kovidāraṃ ca varjayitvā vibhītakam .. 12 ..
asanaṃ devadāruṃ ca palāśaṃ puṣkaraṃ tathā ..
na vivarjyastathā kaściddevodyāneṣu jānatā .. 13 ..
tatrāpi bahutā kāryā māṅgalyānāṃ dvijottama ..
sāyaṃ prātastu gharmānte śītakāle dināntare .. 14 ..
2.6.d:
संस्कार्यमुद्भिदं तोयं कूपाः कार्याः प्रयत्नतः ॥
हस्तं मघा तथा मैत्रं सौम्यं पुष्यं च वासवम् ॥ 7 ॥
उत्तरात्रितयं राम तथा पूर्वा च फल्गुनी ॥
जलाशयसमारंभे प्रशस्ते वारुणं तथा ॥ 8 ॥
सम्पूज्य वरुणं देवं विष्णुं पर्जन्यमेव च ॥
तर्पयित्वा द्विजान्कामैस्तदारंभकरो भवेत् ॥ 9 ॥
अथोद्याने प्रवक्ष्यामि प्रशस्तान्पादपान्द्विज ॥
अरिष्टाशोकपुन्नागशिरीषाम्रप्रियङ्गवः ॥ 10 ॥
पनसाशोकदचलीजम्बूलकुचदाडिमाः ॥
माङ्गल्याः पूर्वमारामे रोपणीया गृहेषु वा ॥ 11 ॥
कृत्वा बहुत्वमेतेषां रोप्यास्सर्वे ह्यनन्तरम् ॥
शाल्मलिं कोविदारं च वर्जयित्वा विभीतकम् ॥ 12 ॥
असनं देवदारुं च पलाशं पुष्करं तथा ॥
न विवर्ज्यस्तथा कश्चिद्देवोद्यानेषु जानता ॥ 13 ॥
तत्रापि बहुता कार्या माङ्गल्यानां द्विजोत्तम ॥
सायं प्रातस्तु घर्मान्ते शीतकाले दिनान्तरे ॥ 14 ॥
2.6.m:
Spring water should be purified, and wells should be made with effort / under Hasta, Maghā, Maitra, Saumya, Puṣya, and Vāsava.
The three Uttarās, O Rāma, and Pūrvaphalgunī,
and Vāruṇa [Śatabhiṣaj] are commended at the commencement of a reservoir.
Having worshipped the god Varuṇa, Viṣṇu, and Parjanya,
and having gratified the twice-born with desirable gifts, one should undertake its commencement.
Now I shall tell of the trees commended in a park, O twice-born:
ariṣṭa, aśoka, punnāga, śirīṣa, mango, and priyaṅgu,
panasa, aśoka, kadalī, jambū, lakuca, and pomegranate—
auspicious, these should first be planted in a garden or in houses.
Having made these abundant, all others may indeed be planted thereafter,
avoiding śālmali, kovidāra, and vibhītaka,
asana, devadāru, palāśa, and puṣkara.
However, one who knows should not avoid any tree in divine groves.
Even there, a multitude of auspicious ones should be made, O best of the twice-born.

2.6.m:
and in the rainy season when the ground dries up, the planted trees should be watered.
Twenty cubits apart is best, sixteen cubits interval is middling;
twelve [cubits] between one spot and another is the minimum distance to be made for trees.
Trees that have grown close together, touching one another,
become fruitless because their roots are indistinguishably intermingled, O twice-born.
When disease arises among them, hear the treatment, O Rāma.
First, one should perform a cleansing on them a little with an instrument;
smeared with viḍaṅga, ghee, and mud, one should sprinkle them with cool water.
In case of failure of fruit, watering with boiled and cooled milk with kulattha, māṣa,
mudga, sesame, and barley is always [effective] for fruit and flowers.
Powder of sheep and goat dung, barley meal, and sesame seeds,
beef, and water—one should let these sit for seven nights.
This watering promotes fruit, flowers, and growth for all trees.

And sprinkled with fish-water, branches grow.
Then I shall describe in principal detail the pregnancy cravings of trees.
Watering mango trees with cool fish-water is desired.
Likewise, it should be done in that manner for grapevines, O destroyer of foes;
and cooked blood is commended for pomegranates.
Chaff should be given to bhavyas, and wine to the bakula tree,
especially that which has virtue from contact with the mouth of a lovely woman.
And the kick of a lovely woman's foot is commended for aśoka trees;
jackal-meat broth is beneficial for orange and walnut trees.
Licorice water is commended for jujube trees,
and scented water and beef are commended for katakas.
By watering with milk, the saptaparṇa becomes beautiful;
watering with flesh-cleansed fat and marrow is beneficial for the kurabaka.
Putrid fish, ghee, and rotting cotton fruits—
this watering is commended for arimeda and for trumpet flowers.

कपित्थबिल्वयोः सेकं गुडतोयेन कारयेत् ॥

2.6.m:
One should sprinkle the kapittha and bilva trees with jaggery water;
scented water is exceedingly beneficial for varieties of jasmine and mallikā.
Likewise, turtle flesh is commended for kubjaka jasmines.
For date palms, coconuts, bamboo, and plantain,
watering with salted water is traditionally said to cause growth.
Viḍaṅga, together with rice and fish meat, O foremost of the Bhṛgus,
one should prescribe without distinction as a pregnancy craving for all.
When this is done, trees constantly possess lovely leaves and flowers, are fragrant, free from disease,
full of sap, long-lived, and endowed with fine fruits.
